Modding Men of War: Assault Squad 2

Author: Imperator_Aug (guide and A.R.S.E.N.A.L, the All-in-one Resource SDK for Engine Assets & Levels). A mod that loads clean in the editor is half done; a mod that survives a game update is done.

Join The AS64 Community! https://discord.gg/pgmfaaBVbf

This book teaches you to change Men of War: Assault Squad 2 (and its 64-bit build, as64.exe) by editing the plain text and resource files the game reads. You will change units, weapons, armour, interface text, maps, bots and multiplayer modes without touching the game program itself. Nothing here needs programming skill.

Who this is for

You are comfortable with a text editor and with folders, and you want to mod the game, but you do not know how the engine works inside. Every page explains a new term the first time it appears, and the glossary collects them all. ARSENAL, the toolkit that comes with this guide, does most jobs from a window with tabs; every step is also given as a command for those who prefer a terminal.

The three parts and when to use which

Part I, By process. One job per page, the short way: what you need, the steps, what can go wrong and where the detail is. Use it when you know what you want to make ("add a unit", "change a gun", "pack my mod"). If you are new, read p01 first, then the page for your job.

Part II, In detail. Twenty-two chapters on how each area of the game works. Use it when a Part I page is not enough, when a change does not behave the way you expected, or when you want to understand a whole area before you start. Chapters 1 to 5 are the foundation every other chapter builds on.

Part III, Reference. Every key and every function, one entry each, always in the same shape. Use it when you need the exact facts about one name: where it is written, what values the game accepts, and what silently fails, crashes or desyncs. Part I and Part II link to the entries; the PDF contents list every entry so you can find a key by eye.

Read in this order the first time: this page, then Part I, then Part II, with Part III open beside you.

Gates of Hell. This book is about Assault Squad 2, but Gates of Hell (GoH) grew from the same engine, and ARSENAL has GoH in the game picker of its header: under it the window shows the same pages, for porting units and for making, checking and packing Gates of Hell mods. So every part also says where Gates of Hell differs. A Part I page ends with a section "In Gates of Hell": what is different when you do that job for Gates of Hell and what ARSENAL can and cannot do under the GoH button. A Part II chapter adds a subsection "In Gates of Hell" to each section where Gates of Hell differs, and a table "Gates of Hell: summary" that names every section of the chapter as different, the same as far as known, or not looked at. A Part III entry adds a line starting "Gates of Hell:" where its key works differently there, and each reference page ends with "Gates of Hell only", the keys and functions only Gates of Hell has. None of these notes has been tested in a running game; each Gates of Hell section says so in its first line, and a note that is less sure says "probably" or "not confirmed". Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

The engine technical document is a separate book that describes how the engine of the 64-bit build works, subsystem by subsystem, for programmers and tool authors. This book does not link into it; where it helps, a page names the engine document's chapter in plain words. It is published as its own download, ARSENAL-engine-docs-public-<version>.zip, beside the ARSENAL downloads. Copy its techdoc folder into the ARSENAL folder and the Docs page of the ARSENAL window shows it (Whole documents in chapter 19 says how).

Contents

Part I. By process

  1. Make a mod and see it in the game: the mod folder, mod.info, switching the mod on and checking it.
  2. Change a unit's numbers: price, health, speed and the other numbers on the price card and in the definition.
  3. Add a new unit from an existing one: copy a working unit, give it its own id, name and buy panel card, or describe a new unit in plain words.
  4. Change a gun or its ammunition: reload time, range, muzzle speed, penetration and damage.
  5. Change armour and see the result: armour macros, volume thickness and the armour simulator on the Models page.
  6. Edit a model or an animation: model, mesh, volume and animation files, the Models page and SOEdit.
  7. Add or change text and translate it: .lng files, text keys and translation.
  8. Icons and interface: buy panel icons, portraits, squad pictures and buttons.
  9. Copy and change a map: your own copy of a multiplayer map, its lobby name and objects placed on it.
  10. Missions and multiplayer modes: game cards, mode files, starting money, army size and checking a mission.
  11. Bots: what they buy and how they play: making bots buy your units, their difficulty and their way of playing.
  12. Bring a unit from Gates of Hell: a Gates of Hell unit built on top of a working donor unit.
  13. Bring an old mod up to the 64-bit build: Classic and Enhanced mode and the version lines that pick between them.
  14. Check a mod, fix what the check finds, read the game log: checking without the game, the patch mod and game.log.
  15. Pack and share: version lines, packing, multiplayer compatibility and publishing.
  16. Find guides and tools others made: the Guides & External Tools page and its offline index.
  17. Use the Quick Guided Task: the row above the tabs, its 27 tasks, what they write and where, and which task does the job of each page above.
  18. Work with Claude: skills and MCP servers: the skills and the two servers that let Claude look things up, check and change a mod, answer questions about playing, and work the ARSENAL window, for all three games.

Part II. In detail

  1. Getting started: what soft-code modding is, what you can and cannot change, and your first small mod.
  2. Install layout: a tour of the game folder, your user data and the executables.
  3. Mod folder and load order: mod.info, activation, ordering, and Classic against Enhanced mode.
  4. Virtual file system, paks and patches: how files override each other.
  5. The SDL language: the syntax shared by all data.
  6. Data keys and entities: the anatomy of an entity and how to add one.
  7. Units, vehicles and movement: chassis, physics and pathfinding.
  8. Infantry and humans: soldiers, abilities, morale and inventory.
  9. Weapons, ammo and damage: penetration, armour, blast and fire.
  10. AI and bots: how units choose targets and how multiplayer bots work.
  11. Interaction scripts: the {on event} language.
  12. Missions and multiplayer setup: game modes, budgets, mission scripting and sync.
  13. Maps: map folders, terrain and map points.
  14. Localization: .lng files and adding text.
  15. Interface and icons: data-driven interface, icons and hotkeys.
  16. Effects, sound and models: vision, effects, sound and asset formats.
  17. Balance, pricing and gameplay: what your data changes mean for players.
  18. Testing and logs: the test loop and reading game.log.
  19. The toolchain: the ARSENAL window and tools (the Quick Guided Task among them), their commands and the order to run them in, with a section on porting from Gates of Hell.

  21. Troubleshooting: symptoms, causes and what to attach when asking for help.

Part III. Reference

  1. mod.info and the mod folder: mod.info keys, mod folder items, patch documents and which file wins.
  2. Entity definition: top-level keys and blocks of a .def file, common stuff keys and the shared data sets.
  3. Extenders and components: every extender type and its keys.
  4. Chassis, movement, wheels and tracks: chassis types, engine and gears, pathfinding profiles, obstacles and physics.
  5. Humans: breed, skills, perks, veterancy, abilities, inventory and the stance machine.
  6. Weapons and ammunition: timing, range, aim, damage, penetration, bursts, ammunition and the weaponry block.
  7. Armour, volumes and damage: armour macros, volumes, materials and how damage reaches parts.
  8. Vision, effects and sound: sight, effects, sounds and the model file.
  9. Interface and localization: action files, command panels, hotkeys, HUD settings and the rules of .lng files.
  10. Interaction scripts: every event, command and condition of the interaction script language.
  11. Mission files: mission commands, triggers, conditions, game mode cards, budgets, units, armies and map files.
  12. Bot Lua and console: the Lua functions a multiplayer bot may call, bot data, and console commands.

Conventions

  • Placeholders. <game folder> is the folder where the game is installed. mods/mymod/... is a path inside your own mod. Always work in your own mod folder and treat the game folder as read-only.
  • Encoding. Text data files (.def, .ext, .set, .mi, .patch, scripts and similar) use CRLF line endings. The 64-bit build reads every string value as UTF-8, in data and .lng files alike; a string saved as cp1251 shows as boxes. Identifiers must be plain ASCII. Original data is ASCII outside ; comments, where some old cp1251 bytes remain; leave them as they are. Paks are ordinary zip files. Many editors silently change encoding or line endings when you save, so check yours.
  • Unconfirmed. A fact that is not proven carries the word "(unconfirmed)". Do not build on it without trying it in your own game first.
  • Window and commands. Part I gives the ARSENAL window way first (tab and button names as they are on screen) and the command way second. Commands are written as ARSENAL <tool> .... Without npm link, type node tools/as2/as2.js <tool> ... from the repository root; chapter 19 explains both.
  • Page layouts. A Part I page has "You need", "The quick way" (when a Quick Guided Task does the job), "Steps", "What can go wrong", "In Gates of Hell" and "More". A Part II chapter has numbered sections, "In Gates of Hell" subsections, a "Gates of Hell: summary" and a "Pitfalls" list. A Part III entry has the lines Where, Type, Values, Does, Limits, Example and See, in that order, and a page ends with "Gates of Hell only".
  • Links. A link to another page goes to the right place in the PDF too. Links to a reference entry name the key, for example range.

Where to go when you are stuck

Look the word up in the glossary. If the game closes, or a change does nothing, use the symptom lists in chapter 21 and read the log as p14 shows. If you want a tool to do the checking, chapter 19 lists the tools and the order to run them in. In the ARSENAL window, the Quick Guided Task explore tasks ("what went wrong in the last run", "what is possible") answer in plain words; see p17.

Part I

By process

One job per page, the short way. Each page says what you need, gives the steps (the ARSENAL window way first, then the command way), lists what can go wrong on that job with its fix, and points to the chapter and the reference entries that hold the detail. Start here when you know what you want to make.

18 pages

Make a mod and see it in the game

A mod is a folder in the game's mods folder. It holds a text file called mod.info (the mod's name and the game versions it works with) and the files the mod adds or replaces. This page makes a mod for the 64-bit build (as64.exe), checks it and switches it on.

You need

  • Men of War: Assault Squad 2 with as64.exe in its folder.
  • ARSENAL, as a window or from a command prompt (type ARSENAL.exe where this guide writes ARSENAL).
  • A text editor that keeps UTF-8 text and Windows (CRLF) line endings.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make, choose a mod and press Start. The task asks for the title shown in the game's mod list, where the mod goes (the game's mods folder is best, because the game lists it at once) and the folder name, then, if you like, a short description and the mods it needs. Review lists every file before Write; after that the task checks the mod and hands the test over to the Play page. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below do the same by hand and show what each part does.

Steps

  1. Tell ARSENAL where the game is. In the window, press "Game folder..." in the top bar and pick the folder that holds as64.exe and the mods folder. The command way: ARSENAL game prints the folder found through Steam; if it is wrong, add --game "<game folder>" to any command.
  2. Make the mod folder. In the window, open the Mods page and press "Make my first mod", or open the New mod card under the mod list. Fill in Folder, Name (the title shown in the game's Mods menu) and, if you like, Description. Press "new: dry run" to see what would be made, then "new" to make it. The command way:

`` ARSENAL new mymod --name "My Mod" --dry-run ARSENAL new mymod --name "My Mod" ``

Both make the folder name lowercase (spaces become _) and write a mod.info with MinGameVersion 3.301 and no MaxGameVersion, the form the 64-bit build wants, plus a text file for names and a readme. Whenever the window is about to write or start something, it first shows one confirm box that lists what will happen and where (the confirm box). ARSENAL new makes 64-bit mods only; ARSENAL newmod mymod --name "My Mod" --target mowas2 makes one for the original game.

  1. Put a change into it. An empty mod changes nothing. For a first change, set a new price on one unit: see Change a unit's numbers.
  2. Check it. Open the Check page and press "Check the mod". The check only reads files; nothing is written and the game is not started. The command way: ARSENAL check mymod. The verdict LOADS_STATIC means that no known crash pattern was found. It does not prove that the mod does what you meant. The page groups what it finds by how bad it is and can write the safe fixes into a separate patch folder; see Check a mod, fix what the check finds, read the game log.
  3. Play a test match. Open the Play page. Tick "Let ARSENAL start the game" (it stays on until you close the window). Press "play: dry run" first: it lists every step and changes nothing. Then press "play". ARSENAL checks the mod, installs it, starts the game on a small test map with a separate copy of the game settings (never your own), and reads game.log. "BOOT OK" means the mod loaded and the match started. The command way:

`` ARSENAL play mymod --dry ARSENAL play mymod ``

  1. Use it in your normal game. On the Play page, card "Install into the game", press "install: dry run", then "install". The command way: ARSENAL install mymod. Then start the game, open Options and the MODS tab. Select your mod under "Deactivated", press >> to move it to "Activated", keep as64+ in the Activated list above your mod, and press Apply. Applying takes about half a minute and needs no restart. More on the list in The mod folder and load order.
  2. Confirm it is on. The reliable check is the file options.set in your profile folder (under Documents, My Games\Men of War - Assault Squad 2\profiles\<profile>\): its {mods block has one line per active mod, such as "mymod:0".
  3. Undo when you want. ARSENAL uninstall mymod --yes removes a mod that install put there, and nothing else. On the Play page, the card "Remove an installed mod" does the same with "uninstall". Your source folder stays as it was.

What can go wrong

  • The mod is not in the Mods list. The folder has no file named exactly mod.info, or its version range is empty. Make the folder with new and keep the MinGameVersion line.
  • The game stops at start or the mod is not applied. A mod made for the original game (both MinGameVersion and MaxGameVersion set to 3.262) does not load beside as64+, and an AS64 mod (3.301) needs as64+. Do not mix the two kinds in one Activated list.
  • Nothing changes in the game. A file in your mod counts only if its path below resource/ is exactly the path of the game file it replaces. A wrong folder makes an extra file that nothing reads.
  • A copied file loses entries. Your copy replaces the game's file as a whole; the game does not merge them. Copy the complete file, then change only what you need.
  • Text shows boxes or question marks. Save every text file as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark and keep CRLF line endings.
  • The mod drops out of the Activated list. The game knows a mod by its lowercase folder name, not by its title. Renaming the folder means switching it on again.
  • The log of the run you wanted is gone. game.log is overwritten every time the game starts. Copy it before you start the game again.

More symptoms and their causes: Troubleshooting.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button. The Mods page lists the mods in Gates of Hell's own mods folder, and the Check page checks a mod against Gates of Hell. The New mod card and the Quick Guided Task "make a mod" make a Gates of Hell mod; on the command line: ARSENAL newmod mymod --name "My Mod" --target goh. The Play page is there, but ARSENAL does not start Gates of Hell: put the mod in place and start the game yourself. It sets MinGameVersion and MaxGameVersion both to the version of your Gates of Hell program.
  • Folder name. Gates of Hell skips a mod folder whose name has a space, a letter outside plain English, or any of - + ( ) [ ] { } ! @ # $ % ^ & * = ; : | ' ". The only sign is a warning in game.log. my_mod works; my-mod does not.
  • mod.info. Each version bound may be left out, and a missing bound counts as open. A Tags line with the word develop lifts the version check. A Priority number (default 1) orders mods that do not need each other: the higher number is applied later and wins. A broken or empty mod.info only skips the mod, with a warning.
  • Where the files go. Gates of Hell reads resource/, N.pat patches and localizations/ in a mod. A resource.pak, localization.pak or localization/ folder in the mod's root is not read: put paks into resource/ and texts under localizations/<language code>/ (see Add or change text and translate it). newmod still makes the 64-bit layout with a localization/ folder, so move the text file.
  • No as64+. That layer belongs to the 64-bit Assault Squad 2 build. Switch the mod on in Gates of Hell's own mod list.
  • Profile folder. Settings and game.log live under Documents, My Games\Gates of Hell\, or under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Digitalmindsoft\Gates of Hell\ when the Documents folder is on OneDrive.
  • Workshop mods are known as mod_<item number>, not by their title.

To bring a unit or a whole mod from Gates of Hell into Assault Squad 2, see Bring a unit from Gates of Hell.

Change a unit's numbers (price, health, speed)

A unit's numbers live in two places. The buy panel numbers (price, rank needed, how long the button waits) sit on its price card in the multiplayer unit lists. Its own numbers (top speed, armour, gun) sit in its definition file, the .def file. ARSENAL changes both and writes the changed copy into your mod.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • The unit's name or id, for example t34_0. The Units page finds it from part of the name.

The quick way

The Quick Guided Task row above the tabs has a task for each kind of number. Set "I want to" to change, then choose:

  • prices of an army: what changes on that army's cards and how, its command points, score and capture, and the money rules that hold for every army.
  • a vehicle: its groups include "Buying and army" for the card and "Speed and fuel" for the speeds.
  • a soldier: "Health and stamina" and "Price".
  • a squad: "Price", "Members" and "Buy card".

Press Start. Review lists every file before Write, and the task then checks the mod. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below show the same changes on the Units and Balance pages.

Steps

  1. Pick your mod and find the unit. Open the Units page. Under "Mod folder" press "Pick folder" and choose your mod. In "Find a unit", type part of the name or id. Narrow with Kind and Army; tick "also units not in the buy panel" to see every unit. Click a unit to read its stats in plain words.
  2. Change one buy panel number. In "Quick change", choose what to change: Price, Name, Armour, Unlock time, Rank needed or Head start. Type the "New value", press Preview, read the table, then press Write. The command way:

`` ARSENAL balance "<game folder>" --folder mymod --where "id=t34_0" --change "cost set 400" --plan ARSENAL balance "<game folder>" --folder mymod --where "id=t34_0" --change "cost set 400" ``

--plan shows the change and writes nothing. The other card columns are rank, charge (the unlock time) and fore (the head start). In the card file these are the keys cost, level, charge and fore. A price on the Units page shows what it is paid with: MP for manpower, SP for special points, or a mod's own points.

The Units page's Balance card has three more helpers. "Change all prices of an army" takes a Percent: 10 makes the army's prices 10% higher, -20 makes them 20% cheaper, and prices are rounded to 5. "Price hint for this unit" shows what similar units cost. "Compare mod with the game" counts the buy panel units of the game and of your mod and lists the new and changed ones.

  1. Change speed, many prices at once, or a whole army. Open the Balance page. Pick your mod folder, then narrow the list in Filter, for example army=ger cls=tank. Tick rows in the Sheet view to change only those. Under the Change view, choose the column to change (Price, Rank, Cooldown s, Fore, Wait at start s, Top speed, Armour or Reload s), the way to change it (by percent, add, multiply by, set to, or to the model price), and the number. Press Preview, then "Write into the mod". The command way is the same tool:

`` ARSENAL balance "<game folder>" --folder mymod --where "id=t34_0" --change "speed set 40" --plan ARSENAL balance "<game folder>" --folder mymod --where "army=ger cls=tank" --change "cost pct 10" ``

Top speed is the MaxSpeed value of the unit's Locomotion block, in km/h. More on the Balance page in Balance, pricing and gameplay.

  1. Change a soldier's health. Vehicles and guns have no health number: they are destroyed through their armour and parts, so make them tougher with armour (see Change armour and see the result). A soldier's health comes from his soldier type, the breed file under set/breed/mp/<army>/. Its perks block holds a line such as {"health" "250%"}. The text in quotes is a level name from set/ability/health.set, which lists the allowed names from "20%" to "1000%". To change it, open the Editor page (tab IDE), switch the file view to Game, find the breed file, use "Copy into my mod", change the level name, and press Save. No single command does this edit.
  2. Change squad size. On the Units page, pick a squad and open "Recipes", "Bigger squad". Choose the Soldier type and How many. The price does not change by itself; change it with Quick change.
  3. Check and look. Run the check on the Check page (or ARSENAL check mymod), then play a test match from the Play page. The Units page lists what to look at in its "Buy panel checklist".

What can go wrong

  • The game crashes at load after a buy panel change. Unlock time and Rank needed take whole numbers only. Even 30.0 stops the game; write 30. Price and Head start may have decimals.
  • A typo in a card field does nothing. Field names on price cards are matched exactly, including capital letters, and an unknown field is skipped without a message. The Units and Balance pages write only fields the game reads.
  • The new top speed does not show when you order a move. Ordered moves use the unit's three speed steps (the Speed block with Slow, Normal and Fast), not MaxSpeed; see Speed settings. MaxSpeed limits direct control. If the unit's file sets its own Speed block, change those numbers too. Roads never let a unit go faster than MaxSpeed.
  • A misspelled health level makes the soldier much stronger. A level name that is not listed in set/ability/health.set gives the soldier the top level instead of an error. Copy a name from that file exactly.
  • The unit waits longer or shorter than you set. The wait at the start of a match is the unlock time times the game mode's factor times (1 minus the head start). The Units page prints this sum; the test mode sets the wait to zero.
  • Players cannot join each other. Every player in a match needs the same version of your mod.
  • Another mod undoes your change. Your copy of a file replaces the game's file as a whole, and a mod lower in the Activated list wins over one higher up. Keep only one mod that changes the same unit list active, or merge them. See who wins the load order.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Units, Balance and Editor pages: they read Gates of Hell units and write into a Gates of Hell mod. The price calculator is not available there, and the Quick Guided Task's price, vehicle, soldier and squad tasks are greyed out. Change the numbers on those pages or in a text editor, then run the Check page.
  • The card. level and fore are not read: there is no rank lock and no head start. charge is a block, {charge {delay N} {interval N}}: the wait at the start of a match and the wait after each buy. A card with no cost costs 0, not 1.
  • Squad prices are worked out. A squad card's price is its own cost plus each member's cost times the card's squad_cost_factor. With round_multiple the sum is rounded up to that step.
  • More card keys: cost_ap and cost_sp, score_factor, not_for_player_sale, conditions, action and doctrine. The 64-bit build stops on keys it does not know, so a Gates of Hell card cannot be copied into an Assault Squad 2 mod as it is.
  • Speed. Slow, Normal and Fast are written inside the Locomotion block; a separate Speed block is skipped. A slope lowers the top speed as well as the pull.

Add a new unit from an existing one

The safe way to add a unit is to copy one that works. The copy gets its own id (the name of its .def file and of its price card), its own name text and its own card in the buy panel. It keeps the 3D model of the unit you copied.

You need

  • A mod folder with a mod.info (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • A unit to copy that is in the buy panel of the army where the new unit should appear.
  • A new id: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, 2 to 41 characters, not ending in _x.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a vehicle, a soldier or a squad, then press Start. The task asks what to copy, then walks through groups of questions: for a vehicle "Id and name", "Buying and army", "Armour", "Guns", "Icons" and "Texts" among others; for a squad "Members", "Buy card" and "Computer players". Review lists every file before Write; then the task checks the mod and hands the test over to the Play page. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below show the Units page and the command way.

Steps

  1. Pick your mod and the unit to copy. Open the Units page, pick your mod under "Mod folder", and find the unit in "Find a unit".
  2. Fill in the copy. In "Add a unit (copy)", type the New id, the Name players will see, and the Price. Leave "also copy the wreck (_x)" ticked, so that a destroyed vehicle leaves a wreck. Tick "bots buy it" if computer players of that army should buy the new unit too. Press Preview to see the new id and the files it will write, then Write. The copy is a new .def file and a new card in the army's list.
  3. Or describe it in words. In "Describe a new unit", write what you want, for example "fast Soviet heavy tank with a big gun, cost 900, called Molot". ARSENAL picks the closest game unit, copies it under a new id and gives the copy its own gun file, armour, speed, price, name and buy panel line. The built-in reader runs on your computer; the AI tick sends the text to an outside service and needs your own key. Read the "Understood" and "Assumed" lines before you write.
  4. The command way. gen builds the same from a recipe file (a spec):

`` ARSENAL gen --sample clone-unit > newunit.yaml ARSENAL gen newunit.yaml --target as64 --out mymod_units --plan ARSENAL gen newunit.yaml --target as64 --out mymod_units ``

Edit the sample before you run it: the clone step names the unit to copy (entity) and the new id (as); the roster step puts it on an army's buy list (unit is the new id again, like the card to copy, army, fields: {cost: ...}, and bots: true for computer players). gen writes a new mod folder, never into your existing one. On Tools & Settings > Other Tools > Generator the same recipe file goes into the spec box, with the target and place chosen beside it. To describe in words from the command line: ARSENAL gen --describe "fast Soviet heavy tank, cost 900" --target as64 --out mymod_units --plan.

  1. A new infantry squad. The squad step of gen copies a squad and sets its members as "breed:count", for example ["squadleader:1", "rifle:5"]. See ARSENAL gen --sample squad. A member is a soldier type, a breed file.
  2. Give it its own look and icon. The copy uses the buy panel picture named after its card id, which the game does not have yet. See Icons and interface. For a different model see Edit a model or an animation.
  3. Check and look. Check the mod (ARSENAL check mymod), then play a test match. Go through the "Buy panel checklist" on the Units page: right army and button group, a name and not a key, price and rank, unlock, spawn, move, fire, wreck.

What can go wrong

  • The new unit shows a key instead of a name. A name key that no .lng file defines is shown as the key itself, with no error. A key that the game's desc.lng also has keeps the game's text. The Units page writes the name into the right file.
  • Bots never buy it. Computer players buy only units listed by exact card name in bot.data.lua (its Purchases table; see Bots: what they buy and how they play). Tick "bots buy it" and copy a unit that bots of that army already buy.
  • Your bot list hides another mod's. To add a unit for bots, your mod ships its own copy of the bot buy list. It replaces the game's list as a whole, so another mod that changes bot buying is covered by yours.
  • Your army list hides another mod's. Your copy of an army's unit list replaces the game's list whole: of two mods adding units to one army, only the lower one in the Activated list counts.
  • The copy does not appear at all. Two .def files with the same name: the first one loaded wins and the other is ignored. Use an id that no game unit and no other active mod uses.
  • The buy panel shows an empty picture. A missing picture shows nothing or a stub, with no error. Add the icon frames for the new card id.
  • A soldier type is missing from a new squad. Each breed in members must exist as set/breed/mp/<army>/<breed>.set.
  • A model mix looks wrong. When "Describe a new unit" joins the hull of one vehicle with the turret of another, the turret can sit wrong and recoil or crew seats can be off (unconfirmed). Look at the unit in the editor before you share it.
  • Players cannot join each other. Every player in a match needs the same version of your mod.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Units page: "Add a unit (copy)" copies a Gates of Hell unit, and a buy holds soldiers only. "Describe a new unit" is not available there, and the Quick Guided Task's vehicle, soldier and squad tasks are greyed out. The Generator (Tools & Settings > Other Tools) and gen take --target goh: ARSENAL gen newunit.yaml --target goh --out mymod_units --plan.
  • What gen can do there. The clone, roster, card, squad, breed and text steps work. The gun, weapon, kitbash, shell, item, sound, skin and mission-clone steps, and gen --describe, are for Assault Squad 2 only.
  • Unit lists are per period. Cards live in set/multiplayer/units/<period>/units_<army>.set; gen uses the period late unless the step names another. A squad goes into the same file, and a soldier type is declared in units/<period>/inf_<army>.set with its breed file under set/breed/mp/<army>/<period>/.
  • Bots. gen does not add a new unit to Gates of Hell's computer players.
  • Card keys differ: see Change a unit's numbers. A card can also carry doctrine, conditions and action.
  • Names. gen writes the names into a .pot file under localizations/default/interface/text/ (see Add or change text and translate it).

To go the other way and bring a Gates of Hell vehicle into Assault Squad 2, use the GoH unit page: Bring a unit from Gates of Hell.

Change a gun or its ammunition

Weapons and ammunition are "stuff" files: text files without an extension under set/stuff/ (cannons under set/stuff/gun/, rifles under set/stuff/rifle/ and so on). A unit names the gun it carries; many units can carry the same gun file. A gun file holds the reload time, range, muzzle speed and, per kind of shell, penetration and damage.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • The unit that carries the gun, or the gun's file name.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make or change and choose a gun or weapon or ammunition, then press Start. The gun task starts with what the weapon is and then asks for the main numbers (range, reload and recovery time, shell speed and damage); the ammunition task asks what the shell is and its damage. Review lists every file before Write, and the task checks the mod after. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below show the pages and the command way.

Steps

  1. Find the gun. On the Units page, pick a unit and read the "Main gun" line: range in map units (20 map units are 1 m), damage and penetration of the default shell. The Balance page shows the same for every unit in the columns Gun, Calibre mm, Pen 100 m, Damage, Reload s and Range m. The command way prints tables of every gun and shell:

`` ARSENAL statsheet "<game folder>" --sheet weapons,ammo --filter 75mm ``

  1. Change the reload time. On the Balance page, pick your mod folder, narrow the list in Filter, open the Change view, choose "Reload s", choose how (set to, add, multiply by, by percent), type the number, press Preview, then "Write into the mod". The preview lists every unit that carries the same gun, because they all change with it. The command way:

`` ARSENAL balance "<game folder>" --folder mymod --where "id=t34_0" --change "reload set 6" --plan ``

Remove --plan to write.

  1. Change a rifle's range. On the Units page, pick a squad, open "Recipes", "Longer rifle range", choose the Weapon and type the Range (one number, or two: aimed and longest).
  2. Give one unit its own, stronger gun. The command way does this best. Write a spec with a gun step and a weapon step:

``` name: my_guns title: My Guns ops:

  • op: gun name: my_76mm like: <existing gun name> recharge: 6 pen: "120 110 100 90 80"
  • op: weapon entity: t34_0 weapon: my_76mm

```

gun makes a new gun file that copies an existing one (like) and changes only what you list: recharge (seconds between shots), speed (shell speed in m/s), damage, pen (penetration in mm at 100, 500, 1000, 1500 and 2000 m) or pen_scale (multiply the copied table, 1.2 is 20% more), and the presets range, accuracy and caliber. weapon mounts the new gun on one unit. Run ARSENAL gen my_guns.yaml --target as64 --out my_guns --plan, then again without --plan. On the Units page, "Describe a new unit" also gives the new unit a gun file of its own.

  1. Edit the gun file by hand. Open the Editor page (tab IDE), switch the file view to Game, find the gun under set/stuff/, press "Copy into my mod", then change the keys and press Save. Useful keys: rechargeTime (reload, seconds), recoveryTime (time between shots or bolt cycle), range (aimed and longest range, metres), speed (muzzle speed, m/s). Settings for one kind of shell go inside a parameters "<ammo tags>" block. All weapon keys are in Weapon keys and the per-shell rules in Ammunition and per-ammunition blocks.
  2. See what the gun does to a target. Open the Models page, pick a vehicle, open the Armor part, and under "Who shoots" choose your gun, a Shell and a Range. The page says how many millimetres of flat armour the shell goes through. Click a part to run the shot test; "Behind the armour" under it says what the shot does to the parts, the crew and the tank as a whole. The Shot button above the 3D view of the Model tab shoots at the point you click. See Seeing and testing armour in the ARSENAL window and Change armour and see the result.
  3. Check and look. ARSENAL check mymod, then play a test match and fire the gun.

What can go wrong

  • A setting inside parameters changes the whole gun. Only some keys can differ per shell (among them reload, range, gravity, damage and its table, speed and spreading). Others written inside the block, such as calibre, burst or DisableRicochet, apply to every shell of the gun.
  • The shell uses the gun's normal values. A parameters block applies only when the loaded shell has all its tags. The first matching block in the file wins, and apc is not apcbc.
  • Penetration stops past a range. The penetration table runs in straight lines between its points and ends a few metres after its last range. Outside the table the first or last value is used, with no extrapolation. Give points up to the longest range you want.
  • A damage line removes the old effect. damage X without add replaces the gun's earlier effect of that kind, for example the first blast layer. Write damage add ... to add one.
  • A damage threshold below 1 is ignored. projectileDamageThreshold is raised to 1 when it is read.
  • The game stops at load. A curve name that is not listed in set/ballistics.set is fatal.
  • The gun is silent or shows a checkered cursor. Sound names (fireSound and the others) have no aliases: a name that matches no file or folder under sound/ plays nothing. A cursor that names no file under interface/cursor shows a checker pattern.
  • Every unit with the gun changed. Units share gun files. Make a new gun (step 4) when only one unit should change.
  • Players cannot join each other. Every player in a match needs the same version of your mod.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Units, Balance, Models and Editor pages for Gates of Hell files, but the Armor part of Models is not available there, and the gun and ammunition tasks of the Quick Guided Task are greyed out. The gun and weapon steps of gen are for Assault Squad 2 only. Change a Gates of Hell weapon in a text editor, then run the Check page.
  • More weapon keys, among them FireSoundClose, ClickSound, AutoReload, FiringTimeout, Recoil and SwayParams. A parameters block also takes MinRange, FalloffMeter and FalloffStrength, MinimumDamageModifier and three overmatch tables. The full list is in Weapon keys and Ammunition and per-ammunition blocks.
  • Penetration is judged with more factors than in Assault Squad 2, and armour does not wear; see Penetration test, step by step.
  • The armour tools on the Models page and armorsim follow the Assault Squad 2 rules only. Do not use them to judge a gun in Gates of Hell.
  • Bringing a gun over. The 64-bit game stops with unexpected token on any of these keys, so a weapon from Gates of Hell must lose them first: see Bring a unit from Gates of Hell.

Change armour and see the result

A vehicle's armour is set in two layers. The unit's .def file usually calls an armour macro such as armor_tank with four numbers per part: front, side, rear and top, in millimetres. Below that, each volume of the model (a box or shape that shells hit, such as body1 or turret) can carry its own {thickness}. A shell goes through when it can pierce more than the thickness along its path, which grows with the slope. The Models page, Armor part, shows and changes all of this.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • A vehicle in the game, or one your mod adds.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to change, choose the armour of a vehicle and press Start. The task asks for the vehicle, then for the armour preset and its lines, the hit volumes and the repair time, with volumes and parts under "Advanced". Review lists every file before Write, and the task checks the mod after. See Use the Quick Guided Task. To see what a shell does to the result, use the Models page as in the steps below.

Steps

  1. Pick your mod and the vehicle. Open the Models page. Press "Pick mod folder" and choose your mod: the armour is read with your mod laid over the game. In Unit, type part of the vehicle's name or id and click it. Open the Armor part.
  2. Read the thickness of each part. The table "Thickness of each part" (the armour table) lists every armoured part and its six sides in millimetres, and notes where each number comes from (set on the part itself, from an armour area, or no value, which counts as 0 mm). "Where each number comes from (file and line)" shows the file. The command way:

`` ARSENAL armorsim table t34_0 ``

  1. Change a number. Click a number in the table ("click to change"). Type the New thickness (0 to 1000 mm), choose Which sides ("only the" one side, or "all six sides"), press "Try it" (nothing is written), then "Change it". A shared number lists the other parts; "Change all of them" changes them together. The unit's file is copied into your mod first. The command way:

`` ARSENAL armorsim edit t34_0 --volume turret --side front --mm 60 --out mymod --dry ARSENAL armorsim edit t34_0 --volume turret --side front --mm 60 --out mymod ``

Add --shared when the number is shared. The Units page (Quick change, Armour: front side rear top, _ keeps one) and the Balance page (Armour) change the macro numbers too.

  1. Choose who shoots. Under "Who shoots", search a Gun, pick one of its Shell types and set the Range (0 to 5000 m).
  2. See the whole side. Under "What happens across the whole side", choose "Shoot from" Front, Rear, Left, Right or Top. The map colours every spot by what happens and gives the share of hits that go through. Click a spot to shoot through it.
  3. Fire one shot. Click a part in the 3D view, or a spot on the map, for a "Shot test": each plate the shell meets, its slope, and what happens. The command way:

`` ARSENAL armorsim shot t34_0 --weapon "<gun name>" --ammo "<shell tags>" --range 500 --from 0,0 ARSENAL armorsim map t34_0 --weapon "<gun name>" --ammo "<shell tags>" --range 500 --view front ``

--from 0,0 is straight from the front; 90 is the left side. The Shot button above the 3D view of the Model tab does the same on the model you have open for editing, and runs the last shot again when you change the model.

  1. See what happens behind the armour. Under the shot test, "Behind the armour" follows the shot past the plates: the chance that the tank cannot move, cannot shoot, burns or explodes, the state of each part and crew member, and which event or script line led to each result. "Without the mod" runs the same shot on the game's own files to compare. After a thickness change it shows the result before the edit next to the new one. Read its lists of skipped script words before you trust a number. Every option is described in Seeing and testing armour in the ARSENAL window.
  2. Check in the game. Press Apply again in the game's mod list (no restart is needed), then shoot at the vehicle in a test match or in the editor. The page follows the game's rules for thickness, slope and penetration and the unit's own scripts; a hit in a running match is still the final word.

What can go wrong

  • A changed {thickness} does nothing. A nonzero number in the armour macro for that side wins over the thickness written on the volume. Change the macro number, or set it to 0 for that side so that each volume's own thickness is used.
  • Left and right, top and bottom cannot differ through the macro. The macro's "side" number is used for both left and right, and its "top" number for the bottom.
  • One hull, several plates. A hull is often several volumes (an upper and a lower front plate, for example). A nonzero macro number overwrites all of them with one value. Keep the plates apart by leaving the macro at 0 on that side.
  • Changing a shared number changes other units. An armour area or macro value can be used by more than one part or unit. Read the list the page shows before "Change all of them".
  • A part is never hit. A volume named in the unit's file but missing in the model is dropped without a message, and its armour is lost.
  • Which side a hit counts as is fixed in the model. Each face of a volume carries its side (front, side, rear, top) in the .vol file; it does not come from the shot's angle.
  • Very flat hits stop growing. The slope multiplies the thickness at most ten times.
  • Armour-piercing shells rarely break hull or turret. The game's tank macro gives those parts a very high durability against piercing, so only blast damage breaks them. See Armour thickness, threshold and durability.
  • Three numbers in a {thickness} block shift the sides. Write all four: front, side, rear, top.
  • Players cannot join each other. Every player in a match needs the same version of your mod.

More causes: Troubleshooting: armor and damage surprises.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button shows the Models page without its Armor part, and the armour task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed out. The Armor part, the Shot tool and armorsim follow the Assault Squad 2 rules only, so do not use them to judge a vehicle in Gates of Hell.
  • More factors on a plate. Against a piercing shell, the thickness is multiplied by an overmatch factor and by three volume keys: Quality (no_flaw, small_flaw, medium_flaw or large_flaw: a flawed plate counts as thinner at an angle), CastSteel (cast armour counts as weaker) and HighHardness (a flag for very hard plate, with its own factor). The overmatch factor comes from the shell's OvermatchCalibre, OvermatchFixed or OvermatchSlope table. Against a blast the thickness is used as it is.
  • Armour does not wear. durability blocks are read but do nothing: a plate never weakens with hits.
  • Part health. set/component.set gives each kind of part its own hit points (hp, hp_broken, armor_damage_modifier). The 64-bit game never reads this file.
  • The rules in full: Penetration test, step by step and Armour thickness, threshold and durability. When you bring a vehicle over, see Bring a unit from Gates of Hell.

Edit a model or an animation

A unit's look is made of several files. The model file (.mdl, text) lists the bones, the meshes (.ply, the shapes that are drawn), the volumes (.vol, the shapes shells hit) and the animations (.anm). Materials (.mtl) tie meshes to textures. Meshes, volumes and animations are binary: change them with an editor, never by hand. The Models page of ARSENAL is that editor. SOEdit, the model and animation editor, can still be used beside it.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • SOEdit only if you want it: it is not part of the ARSENAL download, and the Models page can download and install it for you.
  • For a brand new model: Blender with the GEM2 Engine Tools add-on. The Models page can start a "New model" from a template and bring in a mesh from an .obj or .ply, but it does not model shapes from scratch.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a model, or to change and choose a model of the game or of my mod, then press Start. The task asks what the model is, which files it has and what comes with it, and can go through its bones one by one. Review lists every file before Write. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below use the Models page, which shows the model in 3D while you change it.

Steps

  1. Pick your mod and the model. Open the Models page (tab Models & Sim) and press "Pick mod folder". In Unit, type part of a unit name or id and click the unit, or give a "Model file" path and press "Use this file". The page lists the "Files of" that model in groups (model, meshes, volumes, animations, materials, textures), each marked as in your mod, only in the game, or not found, and shows it in a 3D view.
  2. Change it on the page's own tabs. The page opens every file of the model for editing; the game files are only read.
    • Skeleton: add, delete, move, duplicate and rename bones; their limits and speed, meshes and levels of detail.
    • Volumes: the hit volumes, their shape, tags, part and material; "Apply thickness" sets the armour per side.
    • Meshes and materials: put a mesh on a bone, move, resize or mirror it, join or split meshes, "Bring in a mesh", set textures and make materials.
    • Animation: see the next step.
    • Armor: the armour table and the shot test (see Change armour and see the result).

Undo and Redo work for every change (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y).

  1. Save into your mod. Press Save (Ctrl+S). It first lists the files it will write, what a save would lose and what the file checks found; "Write these files" writes them into your mod at the same paths, so your copies win over the game's. The old copies of files already in your mod are kept in .arsenal/model-edit/backup in your mod first. On the Files tab, "Check before saving" runs the checks alone, "Undo all changes" drops everything not yet saved, and "Save as" writes the model under a new name. Every sub-tab is described in The Models page and SOEdit.
  2. Change an animation. Open the Animation tab and pick the animation; it plays in the 3D view frame by frame. You can set and delete a bone's key at a frame, and change the whole animation with "Insert after", "Delete frames", "Drop the first frame", "Set length", "Stretch", "Reverse" and "Make it loop". "Rename bone" renames a bone's track, and "Take bones from" copies tracks from another animation. The command way:

`` ARSENAL soedit ops anim info mymod/<path>/fire.anm ARSENAL soedit ops anim reverse mymod/<path>/fire.anm --dry ``

The command's first change keeps a .bak copy of the file.

  1. Or use SOEdit. Open the fold "External SOEdit (optional)". Everything on the page works without it. Press "Copy into my mod" first. The model, meshes, volumes, animations and materials go to the same paths inside your mod, so your copies win over the game's. Files already there are kept. Textures are not copied; to repaint a unit use the Look & Sound page. The command way:

`` ARSENAL soedit stage t34_0 --out mymod --dry ARSENAL soedit stage t34_0 --out mymod ``

Then press "Open in SOEdit". SOEdit starts with your mod's copy. Make your change, save, and close SOEdit. To open one animation with the model, use the "External SOEdit (optional)" fold on the Animation tab. The SOEdit card says "SOEdit found" and where, with "Open SOEdit". When SOEdit is not on your computer, the button reads "Get SOEdit and open it": the confirm box names the download and its size, and the package is checked against its known checksum before it is unpacked. The command way: ARSENAL soedit locate, ARSENAL soedit install, and ARSENAL soedit open mymod/.arsenal/soedit/<model>.stage.json (the stage record that stage wrote; a copied .mdl path works too).

  1. Check what SOEdit changed. Back on the Models page, press "Check what changed". It compares your files with the copies taken when you copied them, and lists what changed and anything lost on saving, such as a setting inside a bone or volume, a block of the model file, or an animation saved in another file version. The command way: ARSENAL soedit check mymod/.arsenal/soedit/<model>.stage.json. The SOEdit commands are in The toolchain: soedit.
  2. Check the mod and look at it. Run ARSENAL check mymod and the Art check on the Look & Sound page, then look at the unit in the editor or a test match.

What can go wrong

  • The game crashes while loading the model. Every mesh needs its .mtl file, or a .materials file in the same folder.
  • A mesh or animation stops the game with a chunk error. Mesh and animation files have no length fields, so one wrong field breaks the rest of the file. Edit them only on the Models page, in SOEdit or with an exporter.
  • A mesh is too big. One mesh holds at most 65535 vertices, and one skinned part can use at most 25 bones. Split big models.
  • An animation is refused. An animation needs at least one frame and at most 255 bones; a very old file version is refused. A frame number outside the frame count is fatal at load.
  • An animation plays on nothing. A bone track whose name is not in the model's skeleton is skipped without a message. Keep bone names as they are in the .mdl; "Rename bone" on the Animation tab can match them.
  • A part loses its armour. A volume named in the unit's .def that the model no longer has is dropped silently. Keep volume and bone names.
  • Your new texture does not show. If a .tga or .png of the same name sits beside your .dds (textures), the last of .dds .tga .bmp .jpg .png wins. DDS files saved as DX10 or with a size not divisible by 4 do not load.
  • A path in the model points nowhere. Paths in model files are read from the folder of the file that names them, unless they start with /, which means resource/.
  • Players cannot join each other. Model files under entity/ are compared between players. Every player in a match needs the same version of your mod.

More causes: Troubleshooting: models appear untextured or invisible.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Models page: it opens a model of a Gates of Hell mod in the built-in editor or in SOEdit and saves into your mod folder. Its Armor part is not available there, and the model tasks of the Quick Guided Task are greyed out. To use the unit in Assault Squad 2, bring it over first with the GoH unit page (Bring a unit from Gates of Hell). Under the other games the Models page reads animation files of the kind Gates of Hell uses.
  • Animations. The .anm file is laid out the same, with the same cap of 255 bones. A sequence whose file names a folder takes every .anm directly inside it as variants, and each unit picks one. Two new animation kinds exist, blendspace and aimset. Two animations with the same name in one list are an error.
  • Meshes. A file <model>#<variant>.ply beside the model replaces the mesh while the unit wears the skin variant of that name.
  • Materials. A mesh with no .mtl and no .materials entry loads with a dummy texture and a warning in game.log; the 64-bit game crashes on it. Missing textures are named in game.log too.
  • Textures. Two-channel BC5 .dds files (often normal maps) load in Gates of Hell. Check what the 64-bit game does with such a file before you copy it over.

Add or change text and translate it

Every word the game shows comes from .lng files. Your mod's localization/ folder is where the game looks for them. Each text has a key, a path such as desc/entity/t34_0, built from the file's name and the blocks around the text.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game). The new command already made a text file for it, named #<your mod>.lng.
  • The key of the text, or the unit whose name you want to change.
  • An editor that saves UTF-8. Keep Windows (CRLF) line endings.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose new texts or a translation, or to change and choose the game's texts or a translation, then press Start. The task asks what to do, then takes the lines as key = text, one per row, or a translation table. Review lists every file before Write, and the task checks the mod after. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below show each part by hand.

Steps

  1. Change a unit's name. On the Units page, pick your mod and the unit, choose Name in "Quick change", type the new name, press Preview, then Write. A new key goes into your mod's #<mod>.lng; a name the game's desc.lng already holds goes into a full copy of desc.lng in your mod, so the other names stay. The command way, for one key:

`` ARSENAL lng-add mymod --file "#mymod.lng" --key desc/entity/my_t34 --text "T-34 Model 1942" --dry-run ARSENAL lng-add mymod --file "#mymod.lng" --key desc/entity/my_t34 --text "T-34 Model 1942" ``

lng-add refuses a key that already exists unless you add --force, and warns when the game's own files define the same key.

  1. Write texts by hand. Open the Editor page (tab IDE), open your mod's .lng file under localization/, and add lines in blocks. The Editor checks the file while you type and can also open text files inside your mod's paks. A file starts with {tags, and the key comes from the blocks (the .lng syntax): in desc.lng, {"entity" {"my_t34" "T-34 Model 1942"}} is the key desc/entity/my_t34. In a file whose name starts with #, the file name is not part of the key. Press Save.
  2. Know which key to use. All families are in Key families.
    • Vehicle or gun name: desc/entity/<def name>.
    • Squad name: desc/squad/<name>(<army>), for example desc/squad/riflemans(usa).
    • Soldier name: desc/human/mp/<army>/<breed>.
    • Long tooltip behind the "i" button: info/entity/<name> or info/squad/<name>. A squad card shows the button only when its info/squad/ key exists.
    • Multiplayer map name: mission/multi/<map folder>/name.
    • Weapon and ammunition names: desc/weapon/<tags> and desc/ammo/<tags>, made from the item's tags.
  3. Format a text. \n starts a new line, \" writes a quote. Colour with <c(ffaf00)> and go back with <c(ffffff)> or </c>. A literal < is written <<. Every tag is in Text formatting tags and Colours and formatting tags.
  4. Find missing names. ARSENAL loccover mymod lists buy panel cards, squads and soldier types of your mod that have no name key, squads without a tooltip, and a mod .lng that replaces a whole game file. ARSENAL lnglint mymod/localization checks the files themselves: encoding, braces, strings, duplicate keys and colour tags.
  5. Translate. The game loads one set of texts, the one for the language it is installed in, and every .lng your mod ships. To make your mod read in another language, give translators a table and build a translated copy from it:

`` ARSENAL lng extract mymod --out mymod_texts.tsv ARSENAL lng merge mymod mymod_texts_ru.tsv --out mymod_ru --dry-run ARSENAL lng merge mymod mymod_texts_ru.tsv --out mymod_ru ``

extract writes every key of the mod with its text in a tab-separated table that a spreadsheet opens; the translator fills the translation column. merge writes the translated files to a new folder at the same paths as your mod's own files; your mod is not written. It warns when a translation drops or reorders % values or colour tags. Ship that folder as a language patch that players put below your mod. More in Translating a mod.

  1. See it. Text is read when mods are applied, so press Apply again in the game's mod list (no restart is needed), then hover the card in the buy panel.

What can go wrong

  • All the game's names turn into keys. A mod file with the same path as a game file, such as localization/desc.lng, replaces the game's file whole. Keys you left out show as raw keys. Put new keys in your own #<mod>.lng, or copy the whole game file before you change it.
  • Your new name does not show. If your # file uses a key that the game's desc.lng also has, the game's file is read later and its text wins. game.log then shows Localization key redefinition. Change such a name in a copy of desc.lng.
  • A key shows instead of text. A key no file defines is shown as written, with no error. Keys ignore capital letters, so 75mm_41M and 75mm_41m are the same key; a second definition of a key replaces the first.
  • Letters show as boxes or question marks. .lng files must be UTF-8. A file in the old Windows Cyrillic encoding loads without an error but shows replacement marks; a UTF-16 file stops the game with "Please resave file in UTF8". Long dashes and curly quotes may show as ?.
  • The rest of a text disappears. A colour tag without its closing > swallows the rest of the text. One string must stay on one line.
  • Numbers in a text go missing. Some texts carry % values the game fills in order. Keep every % value of the original, in the same order.
  • Only one language patch works at a time. A language patch holds files at the same paths as your mod, so it replaces your mod's files whole. With two language patches active, the lower one in the Activated list wins.

How the game picks between files is in How the game chooses between files; more causes in Troubleshooting: text is missing or shows as a key.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • Where texts go. One folder per language: localizations/<code>/interface/text/, for example localizations/default/interface/text/. A mod's root localization/ folder is not read. The default language reads .pot and then .lng files; the chosen language reads .mo, .po and .lng, and a key missing there comes from the default. default and en never read .po or .mo.
  • .po and .pot files. The key is the entry's msgctxt; an entry without one, or marked fuzzy, gives no text, and an empty msgstr shows the msgid. Plural entries do not work.
  • .lng still works inside that folder, with the same key rule as in Assault Squad 2.
  • Which text wins. Between files the later one wins, with Localization key redefinition in game.log. Inside one file the first definition stays.
  • Missing keys are logged. A key no file defines still shows as the key, and game.log gets Missing text: [key] once per key.
  • Console. dev_l10n_reload reads the texts again without a restart. dev_l10n_export_pot turns every .lng below /interface/text/ into a .pot under localizations/exported/.
  • In ARSENAL. Under the GoH button the Editor page opens Gates of Hell text files too, but the text tasks of the Quick Guided Task are greyed out. gen --target goh writes its text step as a .pot under localizations/default/interface/text/. ARSENAL lng extract mymod --out t.tsv --lang <code> reads the .pot files of one language, and ARSENAL lnglint checks .po and .pot files as well as .lng.

More in Localization.

Icons and interface

The pictures of the interface live under interface/ in the game: buy panel icons in interface/scene/unit_icon/, the small icons of the unit list in interface/scene/unit_icon_small/, soldier portraits in interface/scene/portrait/ and squad pictures in interface/scene/squad/. A button picture is a set of frames: the same name with _00 (normal), _01 (mouse over), _02 (pressed) and _03 (locked) at the end. The command panel, actions, keys and fonts are text files.

You need

  • A mod folder (see Make a mod and see it in the game).
  • A picture for each icon, as .png (ARSENAL converts it) or as .tga.
  • The unit's card id for a buy panel icon, and its .def name for the small icon. For a squad the name carries the army, for example riflemans(usa).

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make or change, choose an icon and press Start. The task asks which picture of the unit you want (an icon, a portrait, a squad card or a damage scheme), which name it goes under, and which picture it should show: your own PNG or a game icon. Review lists every file before Write. See Use the Quick Guided Task. The steps below do the same on the Look & Sound page (tab Models & Sim).

Steps

  1. See which files the game wants. Open the Look & Sound page and pick the job "Change a buy-menu icon". In "Icon helper", type the unit name and press "Show icon files". The table lists each Folder (unit_icon, the large one, and unit_icon_small), Frame, File, Size, whether the game has it and whether your mod has it.
  2. Make the icons from a PNG. In "Use my own PNG", choose the kind "icon (4 frames)", choose your .png with "Choose file...", press Preview to see the files it will write, then "Write into my mod". The four frames are made at the size the game uses, as .tga, at the right paths in your mod. For a portrait choose the kind "portrait": it writes one picture with the portrait name the soldier type uses (the breed's portrait key). "squad card (3 frames)" writes the three frames of a squad picture in interface/scene/squad/, and "damage scheme" writes the one scheme.tga of a vehicle under structure/<vehicle>/. The preview says when a file replaces one of yours. Where each kind goes is in Where each kind of picture goes and Icons from your own PNG.
  3. The command way. There is no command that converts a picture. Save the frames yourself as .tga at resource/interface/scene/unit_icon/<card id>_00.tga to _03.tga (and the same in unit_icon_small/ with the .def name). For a new unit that should look like an old one on the buy panel, a gen spec can copy the old unit's icon files: add icon_like: <unit> to its roster or card step.
  4. Check the pictures. On the Look & Sound page press "Run Art check". It reads the headers of your pictures and lists pictures hidden by another file of the same name. The command way: ARSENAL check mymod. To look at one picture, open it in the window's picture viewer (File viewers): it shows zoom, channels and mipmaps and says whether the game can load the file.
  5. Change the command panel, actions or keys. These are text files: the command panel in set/panel_control/*.set, button actions in interface/action/*.set, key bindings in keys.set, fonts in interface/font/. Open the Editor page, switch the file view to Game, find the file, press "Copy into my mod", change it and press Save. Then run:

`` ARSENAL uilint mymod ``

It finds missing pictures, unknown action instructions and conditions, panel cells that clash or are full, panel items with no action, unknown key names and font problems.

  1. Look at it. Play a test match or open the editor, place your unit, and look at the buy panel and the unit list.

What can go wrong

  • The icon is empty and there is no error. A missing picture shows nothing or a stub picture, never an error. Make all four frames, and check the name: the buy panel uses the card id, the small icon uses the .def name, a squad adds its army in brackets.
  • Your picture is ignored. For one name the game takes the last of .dds, .tga, .bmp, .jpg, .png, so a stray .tga or .png beside your .dds replaces it. Art check lists such hidden files. A .dds saved as DX10, or with a size not divisible by 4, does not load.
  • The file is in the wrong folder. Your file must sit at the same path as the game file, starting with resource/. A wrong folder is simply never read.
  • You cannot move or resize a panel. The screens, the buy panel, the control bar and the command grid are built into the program. A mod changes pictures, texts, actions, panel items and keys, not the layout.
  • A panel button shows but does nothing. A panel item whose name matches no action file and no item kind becomes a dummy button. Make interface/action/<name>.set or fix the name. An unknown action instruction crashes the game.
  • The command grid hides a button. The main grid has 12 cells. Items without a position are hidden when it is full, and the second of two items in one cell is hidden. Give each item a position or priority.
  • A key does nothing. Unknown key names are ignored without a message; the middle mouse button is MOUSE2, not MOUSE_MIDDLE. A new action of your own cannot get a hotkey, and a new id in keys.set is shown in the options but nothing reads it.
  • Default settings in a mod are never read. The game reads settings only from the player's own profile.
  • The game stops at start after a font change. The font main at size 10 must exist. A letter the font does not have is drawn as ?.
  • Players cannot join each other. Mods that change interface/action files must be the same for every player in a match.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Look & Sound page, whose Icon helper writes the icon files from your PNG into your mod folder, and the Editor page; the icon task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed out. uilint checks Assault Squad 2 interface files only. Paint the pictures yourself and check the mod on the Check page.
  • Frame names. Under /interface/ and /map/ a file is a frame only when its name is the picture's name plus two digits (flag02) or plus _ and two digits (flag_02). Assault Squad 2 also takes longer names that end in two digits, so frame sets made for one game can animate wrongly in the other.
  • Pictures. Soldier portraits have 22 kinds instead of 15, and there are new squad icons in /interface/scene/squad/. Two-channel BC5 .dds files load.
  • Keys. The common/... key ids moved to interface/... and others, so a keys.set copied between the games leaves keys unbound with no error. An action file with Key takes the hotkey bound under that name, so your own actions can have hotkeys.
  • Command panel. Six lists are loaded, among them right_special and the new right_emplacement.
  • Fonts. The font main at size 8 must exist (Assault Squad 2: size 10). Ship both sizes when you share fonts.

The full list is in Interface and icons and the Gates of Hell parts of its sections Actions, The command panel, Hotkeys and Fonts, cursors and HUD files.

Copy and change a map

This page shows how to make your own copy of a multiplayer map, give it a lobby name, put an object on it and check it. The original map is never changed: everything goes into your mod folder.

You need

  • The game folder known to ARSENAL (the Mods page shows it).
  • A mod folder of your own (the first page of this part shows how to make one).
  • For placing things by sight: the game's own map editor.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a map, starting from a game map, or to change and choose the settings of a map. The task asks, group by group, for the copy and its name, the players, the game modes and bots, the season and pictures, objects on the map, and the ground and start points, then writes the copy into your mod after a review and checks it. It works under the 64-bit build only.

Steps

  1. Pick a map. In the window: open the Maps page. Under "1. Pick a map", type part of a name, or narrow the list with "Players" and "Game mode". Click a map to see its terrain and details. The first reading takes a minute or two; the list is saved afterwards, and "Read the list again" reads it anew after you add a map. A map file opened in the Editor's file viewer can open this page too. On the command line: ARSENAL maps list prints the game modes of every multiplayer map, and ARSENAL maps view --map multi/<map> draws one in the terminal.
  2. Make your copy. In the window: under "2. Make my copy", choose "My mod folder" with "Pick folder". Type a "New map name" (letters, digits and _ only; it becomes the folder name) and the "Name in the lobby". Under "Game mode", keep "Keep the modes the map has" or pick one mode (see Missions and multiplayer modes). Press "Preview (writes nothing)", read the plan, then "Write the copy". On the command line: `` ARSENAL maps clone --map map/multi/<map> --name <new> --out <mod folder> --target as64 --plan ` Remove --plan to write. The terrain files are copied byte for byte, the map's name is changed inside its text files, a mod.info is written if the mod has none, and a lobby name file localization/mission/multi/<new>.lng gets the original map's name. --only-mode <mode>` copies one game mode only.
  3. Set the lobby name (command way). The window did this in step 2. On the command line: `` ARSENAL lng-add <mod folder> --file mission/multi/<new>.lng --key mission/multi/<new>/name --text "My map" --force ``
  4. Put an object on the map. In the window: under "3. Put an object on a map", choose the "Map", type the "Object name" (the definition's file name without .def), "East-west (m)", "North-south (m)", optionally "Height (m)" and "Turn (degrees)", then press "Place it". You type metres; the page converts them at 20 map units to 1 metre. On the command line: `` ARSENAL place-entity <mod folder> --game <game folder> --map multi/<new> --entity <name> --pos x,y --dir 90 --dry-run ` Here --pos takes map units. Remove --dry-run to write: the tool copies the map's map file into your mod and adds one {Entity ...}` with a fresh id.
  5. Check the map. In the window: "Check my mod's maps" runs after every write; "Check now" runs it again. On the command line: ARSENAL milint <mod folder> --game <game folder>.
  6. Place things by sight. The Maps page lists the steps under "Use the game's own editor": install the mod, start the game's editor, enable your mod, open your map, edit and save. Saved files belong in the mod's resource/map folder; copy them there if they land elsewhere.
  7. Test it in a match. In the window: "Go to Play", and put your map in the "Map" field. On the command line: ARSENAL play <mod folder> --map multi/<new>:combat --dry, then without --dry. On a map other than the default test map, play cannot decide the start verdict, because it has no clean run to compare with: read the log yourself (Check a mod, fix it, read the log).

What can go wrong

  • "A map with this name already exists in the game." Pick another name.
  • A Gates of Hell map is refused. Its ground grid has a different cell size. See In Gates of Hell below.
  • A name you typed is not found. The page offers the nearest map names; pick one.
  • captureflag crashes at the start with Clipper 'captureflaga' is not found! when the map lacks its two capture areas. Copy from a map that has captureflag, add the areas in the editor, or write the mode with ARSENAL misgen (next page).
  • A mode file includes a file the game cannot find, and the map stops loading when that mode is picked. Copy only the mode you need, or put the missing file beside it.
  • The map is missing under a mode. The mode file's name must match a game mode; otherwise the log says Mission '...' is skipped.
  • The lobby shows a raw key. For a map in a sub-folder the key is mission/multi/<sub>/<map>/name.
  • The object lands in the wrong place. The window takes metres, the command map units. Flag zone sizes are metres.
  • Flags placed by the tool stand at a computed spot; check in a match that they capture (unconfirmed).
  • "Allow bots" switches bots on in the mode's rule file in your mod, so every map with that mode gets bots.
  • unexpected token on an xform. It takes only zl, zw, y and scale.
  • Multiplayer: model, material and patch files are compared by size only, so a same-size edit passes the lobby and goes out of sync later.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Maps page: it lists Gates of Hell maps and copies one into your mod, and the Map Viewer shows them. The map task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed, and ARSENAL starts no Gates of Hell test of the map. Edit the copy with Gates of Hell's own editor.
  • The ground grid. A Gates of Hell height map has cells of 5 units; Assault Squad 2 uses 10 and stops loading a map with another cell size, with Different grid cell sizes!.
  • map.net is always read in its newest layout in Gates of Hell. An old map saved in an older layout reads wrong there: save it again in the editor.
  • New blocks in the map file: Haze, GlobalTexture and CampaignSquads. Assault Squad 2 stops on them with unexpected token.
  • Flags and points. A flag can name a polygon zone with zoneId and is captured from anywhere inside it. A circle radius is taken as given, with no 1 m minimum. Gates of Hell adds waypoint map points, which Assault Squad 2 does not know.
  • Object ids in a Gates of Hell map can be larger than Assault Squad 2 loads (above 65535; not confirmed).
  • The scene camera starts from the preset main in Gates of Hell, not perspective (probably; not confirmed).
  • To bring a Gates of Hell map into Assault Squad 2 for your own use, ARSENAL mapport <GoH resource root> --out <folder> --dry plans the conversion: it resamples the ground to cells of 10 and drops the blocks that stop the load; --check lists files still in Gates of Hell form. ARSENAL mission-clone turns zoneId flags into zoneA/zoneB circles (--flag-zone, metres, default 12) and takes files the mode includes from --src <GoH root>. The packer's Gates of Hell guard covers units, not maps: keep a ported map off the Workshop.
