Missions and multiplayer modes

A multiplayer game mode is two things that must match: a game card, the rule file set/multiplayer/games/<mode>.set, and a mode file in each map, map/multi/<map>/<mode>.mi, which places spawn points and flags. This page shows how to give a map another mode, change the starting money and army size, and check a mission before you play it.

You need

  • A mod folder, and a map: a vanilla one or your copy from Copy and change a map.
  • The game folder known to ARSENAL.
  • A text editor, or the Editor page (tab IDE), for hand changes to .mi files.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a multiplayer game mode, or to change and choose the rules of a multiplayer game mode. The task asks for the mode to copy, the name in the lobby, the sides, the goals, the rules of the match, new units to buy, teams and alliances, and money and buy limits, and shows the mission file in the Editor. It writes after a review, then checks. It works under the 64-bit build only.

Steps

  1. See which modes a map has. In the window: the Maps page list has a "Game modes" column and a "Game mode" filter. On the command line: ARSENAL maps list, or ARSENAL maps list --map map/multi/<map>.
  2. Add a mode to a map. In the window: on the Maps page, pick the map, choose the "Game mode" under "2. Make my copy", press "Preview (writes nothing)", then "Write the copy". The modes are:
    • combat: two teams fight until one side runs out of points or units; spawn points only.
    • battle_zones: teams capture flag zones and earn points while they hold them.
    • captureflag: one flag in the middle; hold it long enough to win. It needs two capture areas. On the command line:

    `` ARSENAL maps mode --map map/multi/<map> --from combat --to battle_zones --out <mod folder> --dry-run ` Remove --dry-run to write. Between combat and battle_zones the flag points are added or removed; for captureflag a centre flag and its ring are added. Other modes, such as frontline`, are copied as they are and marked as needing hand work.

  3. Make a mode with a new name (command way only). `` ARSENAL mission-clone --game <game folder> --map map/multi/<map> --from combat --to <new> --with-mode <new> --title "My mode" --out <mod folder> --dry-run ` --with-mode (the same name as --to) writes a new game card based on an existing mode, the map's info entry and the lobby title. The new mode plays by its base mode's rules; it registers, lists the map in the lobby and hosts. Whether the lobby shows its title correctly is unconfirmed. A mode cloned from combat gets bots switched on unless you add --no-bots`.
  4. Write a captureflag mission from numbers (command way only). ARSENAL misgen --map <map folder> --spec spec.json writes captureflag.mi, captureflag.info and the two capture areas into the map's map file, from one flag position and zone, the spawn points of each side (the same number on both) and optional times. ARSENAL misgen --check <map folder> reports a missing area, flag, spawn or key.
  5. Change starting money and army size. In the window: on Game Modes & AI > Game Modes, section "Multiplayer start settings", pick the "Preset file" ("Competitive presets", "All-units presets", "Custom (user) presets" or "Test presets"), find a preset with "Show only names containing", and change "Start money", "Top money", "Army size cap (command points)" or "Seconds to grow from start to top". Press "Preview changes", then "Write into my mod". "Back to stock (remove my copy)" undoes it. On the command line: ARSENAL patch-entity <mod folder> --game <game folder> --file set/multiplayer/games/presets_user.inc --set <path>=<value> --dry-run.
  6. Write triggers and commands. Edit the map's .mi; chapter 12 and reference page r11 describe them.
  7. Check the mission. In the window: Maps page, "Check now". On the command line: ARSENAL milint <mod folder> --game <game folder>. It compares the game card with the .mi and checks player counts, presets, budgets, unit sets, bot orders and mission commands.
  8. Play it. In the window: the Play page, with multi/<map>:<mode> in the "Map" field. On the command line: ARSENAL play <mod folder> --map multi/<map>:<mode> --dry, then without --dry. For two players on one computer, start the 64-bit build with -instance N (N from 1 to 9); each instance keeps its own settings and game.log.

What can go wrong

  • The map is missing under the mode. The .mi name must match a game card, or the log says Mission '...' is skipped - game type(...) is undefined.
  • captureflag crashes at the start with Clipper 'captureflaga' is not found! when the capture areas captureflaga and captureflagb are missing. Use a map that has them, add them in the editor, or use misgen.
  • A copied frontline or custom mode needs hand work on its phases and spawn chains.
  • Tool-placed flags sit at a computed spot; whether they capture as expected is unconfirmed.
  • minTeamPlayers and maxTeamPlayers are not read. Player counts come from map.info, rounded up to even.
  • Payback lists need tabs between values and lists of equal length.
  • A unit set that only excludes matches nothing.
  • {# in a .mi does not comment out. Use ;.
  • Your copy of a preset file replaces the whole file. If another mod changes it too, only the later mod wins.
  • Multiplayer: every player needs the same game cards, maps and mod order. Lua and model files are compared by size only, so a same-size change goes out of sync during play.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has both tabs, with less in them: Missions compares the missions of a Gates of Hell map but cannot add a game mode to it, and Game Modes reads the Gates of Hell mode cards and changes bot difficulty and start money but cannot allow bots in a mode. The game mode task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed. Edit Gates of Hell mode files by hand.
  • Game cards. Gates of Hell keeps them in set/multiplayer/games/ too: ammunition, battle_zones, campaign_capture_the_flag, cooperative, evacuation and frontlines, with the presets in set/multiplayer/games/presets/ (early, mid and late presets, battle zones, frontlines, last stand and alliances).
  • Mode names differ. The frontline mode is called frontlines in Gates of Hell, and combat is not a mode there. koth, ammunition, heroes, campaign_capture_the_flag, evacuation and guerrilla exist only in Gates of Hell; a game card for one of them makes no game in Assault Squad 2.
  • New game card settings: loseOnZeroPoints (a team at zero points loses), pauseDuringPreparation (default on; off lets the battle run during preparationTime), and waveTime and firstWaveTime for evacuation waves. allowRejoin is not read.
  • Rounds. A frontlines card without rounds probably plays one round in Gates of Hell, where Assault Squad 2 plays two (not confirmed).
  • Conquest, Gates of Hell's own campaign, reads set/dynamic_campaign and fights its battles in campaign_capture_the_flag against bots. Assault Squad 2 has nothing like it.
  • Copying a Gates of Hell mode into Assault Squad 2: see the mapport and mission-clone notes in Copy and change a map.

Bots: what they buy and how they play

Bots are the computer players in multiplayer and skirmish games. A bot does two things itself: it chooses what to buy, and it sends squads towards flags. The fighting is done by the units themselves. This page shows how to make bots buy your units, change their difficulty, and apply a ready-made way of playing.

You need

  • A mod folder, picked on the Mods page.
  • The game folder known to ARSENAL: the stock bot files are read from it.
  • Units with a buy card (the entry players buy them from).

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to change and choose what bots buy and how they play. The task asks, group by group, for a unit the bots of one army buy first, the bot difficulty for every army, the lobby money for every army (players and bots), and how the bots of every army fight (a persona from Bot Doctrine). It writes the same files as the steps below after a review, then checks. It works under the 64-bit build only.

Steps

  1. See what bots buy now. In the window: on the Bots page (Game Modes & AI > Bots), "What bots buy" shows the shopping list for the chosen "Army", stage by stage. Stage 1 is the bot's first order; later stages add heavier units. The page also lists "Units of your mod that no bot buys yet". On the command line: ARSENAL botrecipe <mod folder> --check --game <game folder> compares your bot list with the stock one and checks that every listed unit has a buy card.
  2. Make bots buy a unit. In the window: in "Make bots buy a unit", type the "Unit name" (the name on its buy card), and pick the "Army", the "Stage" (1 to 8, or "automatic") and the "Kind of unit". Tick "Buy it first" for priority 1000, picked almost every time, or set a lower priority. "Make it cheap and quick to unlock" is for testing only. If your mod has no buy card for the unit, name a unit whose card should be copied. Press "Preview", then "Write into my mod". This writes a copy of script/multiplayer/bot.data.lua into your mod with one new line. On the command line: `` ARSENAL botrecipe <mod folder> --out <mod folder> --buy-first <unit> --army <army> --stage 3 --class Tank --priority 1000.0 --game <game folder> --dry-run ` --class takes Infantry, ATInfantry, Vehicle, Tank, AATank, ATTank, HeavyTank or ArtilleryTank. --card-like <unit> copies a buy card. Remove --dry-run` to write.
  3. Change how rich each difficulty is. In the window: in "Bot difficulty", each of "Easy", "Normal", "Hard" and "Heroic" has "Army size x", "Income x" and "Payback x". 1.00 is normal; higher is richer. Change a number, press "Preview changes", then "Write into my mod". The values live in set/multiplayer/games/bots_generic.inc. "Settings shared by a whole game mode" changes, the same way, "Seconds to grow from start to top", "Army size multiplier", "Income multiplier" and the payback table of a mode; "Back to stock (remove my copy)" removes your copy. If a written change does not show in the game, press "My change is not showing". On the command line: ARSENAL patch-entity <mod folder> --game <game folder> --file set/multiplayer/games/bots_generic.inc --set <path>=<value> --dry-run.
  4. Apply a way of playing (a persona). In the window: open the Bot Doctrine page (Game Modes & AI > Bots > Bot Doctrine), or press "Apply a persona (Bot Doctrine)" on the Bots page. Its own tabs are "Rules", "Personas", "Scenarios", "Profile", "Generate" and "Check". Choose a persona on the "Personas" tab. On "Profile" press "Detect from my mod". On "Generate" set "Strength" (1 is the persona as written, 0 no change, up to 2), optionally a "Base bot file (optional)" to start from, press "Preview", then "Write into my mod"; "Check now" then opens the Check page. On "Check" press "Check my mod". The universal persona puts the original numbers back. The numbers are starting guesses not yet tried in a match (unconfirmed). On the command line: `` ARSENAL doctrine list personas ARSENAL doctrine gen --persona <id> --out <mod folder> --game <game folder> --plan ARSENAL doctrine check <mod folder> --game <game folder> ` Remove --plan` to write.
  5. Let bots join a LAN lobby. The stock game cards have no bot switch. In the window: tick "Allow bots" on the Maps page when you copy a map. By hand: put {enableBots 1} inside the {settings} block (not {options}) of your mod's copy of a game card, such as set/multiplayer/games/combat.set. The lobby command mp_slot 2 normal then puts a normal bot in slot 2.
  6. Watch them and read the log. Play a game with bots and your mod on. Bot scripts write print lines to game.log with a [LUA] prefix; ARSENAL logtriage <log folder> --lua prints only those.

What can go wrong

  • A new unit never shows up in bot games. Bots buy only what is on their list. The unit also needs a buy card, and the bot must be able to pay.
  • An army missing from a stage buys nothing at that stage. List every army in every stage.
  • A typo in a unit name is silent. The bot's buy call reports success for a name that does not exist or is not for sale. Use the exact card name: squad cards are written name(army), such as bazookers(ger); vehicle cards are plain names, such as achilles; single soldier cards carry a path, such as mp/eng/bazooker.
  • Your own bot.lua makes the bot buy nothing. The first handler subscribed for an event wins. Load the stock script first, then add your handlers.
  • A Lua error no longer stops the game. The bot goes idle and the log says Lua call failed.
  • Bot scripts run on the host only.
  • Bots cannot be ordered to attack, retreat or board. Better fighting comes from unit data.
  • The stock bot reads only three settings from its data file: squad size, how often orders change, and which flags to go for. AttackBaseTime and the per-entry period are not read. A persona changes more only with a larger replacement bot script in the same mod set.
  • Your copy of bot.data.lua replaces the whole file. If another mod changes it too, the later mod wins.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button shows the Bots page, which changes the multiplayer settings there, but its bot shopping list, the bot match and the Bot Doctrine page are not available, because Gates of Hell has no bot.data.lua. Bot difficulty is on the Game Modes page. The bots task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed, and botrecipe and doctrine work for Assault Squad 2 only. Edit Gates of Hell's bot scripts (bot.main.lua, modes/*.lua) by hand.
  • Different files. The bot script is script/multiplayer/bot.main.lua with one script per mode in script/multiplayer/modes/ (battle zones, conquest, frontlines, last stand). What bots buy is in per-army lists script/multiplayer/units/<army>/ with early, mid, late and conquest files (armies eng, fin, ger, rus, usa). There is no bot.data.lua. bots_generic.inc sits in set/multiplayer/games/presets/global_parameters/.
  • Bot Lua differs. EnemyHasTanks is gone: count tanks with QueryScene. Spawn with an unknown unit name crashes the game instead of failing: check with IsUnitAvailable first. New are SpawnAt (spawn at one of the team's points), CanSpawn, TimeToSpawnUnit and SeekAndDestroy, and the events PrepTimeOver, WinnerDecided and Waypoint. BotApi.Instance has gameMode, difficulty and ownTeamSize (Assault Squad 2's teamSize).
  • Porting a bot script: hook events by name, not by number; the numbers differ (probably).
  • Where bots run. Bot scripts run on the game's server side, not on the clients. The console variable dev_enableBotAi 0 starts the next match with bots that neither buy nor move, which helps when testing.

Bring a unit from Gates of Hell

Gates of Hell (GoH) and Assault Squad 2 (AS2) grew from the same engine, but their data does not carry over one to one. ARSENAL builds the AS2 unit on top of a donor: an AS2 unit of the same kind that already works in the game. The GoH unit brings its model, textures, animations and name; the donor brings crew places, weapon slots and armour layout. The result is a start to test in the game.

A ported unit holds GoH files. It is for your own computer only and can never be shared or uploaded.

You need

  • Gates of Hell and Assault Squad 2 installed on the same computer. Both are only read.
  • The AS2 game folder known to ARSENAL (Mods page).
  • An output folder for the new mod. Inside the AS2 folder only mods/<name> is allowed, and nothing inside the GoH folder. The window offers a new folder in the game's mods folder.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a unit from Gates of Hell. The task asks for the unit and its donor, then shows the numbers that do not fit one by one (keep the AS2 scale, the translated value or the donor's), asks how players buy it (army, the card it sits next to, cost, name, icon and whether bots buy it), and brings it over into an Assault Squad 2 mod after a review. "More choices" holds the converter's switches and the two game folders. It works under the 64-bit build and under the GoH button.

Steps

  1. Pick the GoH unit. In the window: pick GoH in the game picker of the header. The header then shows the GoH folder and the AS2 folder the results go to. Open the Units & Balance tab (Alt+7) and pick GoH unit in the row above the page. Under "1. Pick the GoH unit", type part of a name, for example panzer4j, and press "Search". Click a unit in the list. On the command line, you name the unit exactly with --entity in step 3. An unknown name ends with PORT_NOT_FOUND.
  2. Pick the donor. In the window: under "2. Pick the donor", type an AS2 unit name, or press "Suggest donor". The page shows the best three in the same class, compared by gun size, armour, drive type and crew, each marked "good match", "fair match" or "weak match". Press "Use this donor". On the command line: `` ARSENAL donorpick --goh "<GoH folder>" --game <game folder> --entity <unit> `` With no fitting candidate it reports no donor rather than guess.
  3. Convert. In the window: under "3. Convert", check the "Output folder", press "Preview (writes nothing)" and read the findings, warnings first. Then press "Convert and write" and confirm. On the command line: `` ARSENAL goh2as2 --goh "<GoH folder>" --entity <unit> --donor <AS2 unit> --rep-key --pull-props --mtl-fallback --match-weapon --no-ask --game <game folder> --out <output folder> --dry-run ` Remove --dry-run to write. With a donor, speed, turn, mass, fuel, armour and crew values are translated to the AS2 scale. Without --no-ask` it asks about each value outside the usual range.
  4. Read what changed. The page lists "What changed vs the GoH tank" and "Translated values" with a column "Advice" for each value. To decide value by value, open the fold "Translate numbers" in step 3: "Translate" asks one question per value that is unusable or outside the AS2 range of its class, with three answers: "AS2 scale" (the GoH value mapped onto the range AS2 units of this class use), "Translated" (the translation table's value) and "Donor" (keep the donor's own value). Keys 1 to 3 pick, Enter takes the default, and R keeps the answer for the rest of the class. "Translate, never ask" takes every default, the AS2 scale.
  5. Fit the model to the rules. In the window: under "Fit check", press "Run the fit check". It checks that the model has the bones, doors and seats the donor rules expect. "Fix what can be fixed" edits the unit file after you confirm. On the command line: `` ARSENAL donorfit <output folder>/resource/entity/<unit>/<unit>.def --game <game folder> --fit --write --in-place --moddir <output folder> ``
  6. Check, install and look at it. In the window: under "Show me my unit", "Show the steps" lists the commands to preview the install, plan a tiny test and place the unit on your own map; the page itself never starts the game. Under "Next step", press "Open in Mods", "Check it", then "Go to Play". On the command line: `` ARSENAL check <output folder> ARSENAL install <output folder> --name <mod name> --game <game folder> --dry ARSENAL install <output folder> --name <mod name> --game <game folder> ` Then activate the mod after as64+` in Options, MODS, and try the unit in a match: that it moves, fires and takes damage.

What can go wrong

  • The crew is cut to the donor's places. Seats are bound to the model and its animations, so the seat count cannot grow in the unit file alone.
  • The gun is swapped for the nearest AS2 gun when the GoH one has no match.
  • The armour comes from the donor, not from the GoH plates. GoH extra-hard and cast steel have no equivalent, so their strength bonus is lost. Compare with the donor and test with shots.
  • A penetration table is used only when the ammo tags match exactly.
  • GoH animation events and some effects are dropped. AS2 has no animation events.
  • The game stops at loading with define not found. A GoH file calls a macro that its chain of included files does not hold. Include the file that defines it, or rename the call. ARSENAL check finds most of these first.
  • The game stops with Extender not found. Some GoH parts, such as a medic tent or a fortification, have no counterpart in AS2. Remove that part from the unit file.
  • The game stops with Resource not found for an animation. GoH can name a folder of animation variants; AS2 takes one file.
  • Speeds look wrong. GoH speeds run higher than AS2's. Keep the translated values and tune in the game.
  • The output folder is refused. The tool never writes into the GoH folder, a Workshop folder, or the AS2 folder outside mods/<name>. Pick another folder.
  • Packing and sharing are refused. The packer and the Share page find the GoH files listed in GOH-ORIGIN.tsv and refuse to pack or upload the mod.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

This page is about Gates of Hell already; this section says what in Gates of Hell's own unit data has no place in Assault Squad 2, so you know what the port leaves behind.

  • Armour volumes can carry HighHardness, CastSteel <value> and Quality (no_flaw, small_flaw, medium_flaw, large_flaw). Gates of Hell lowers or raises a plate's effective thickness with them; Assault Squad 2 has no such words, which is why the port keeps the donor's armour.
  • Ammunition can carry overmatch tables (OvermatchCalibre, OvermatchFixed, OvermatchSlope) that Assault Squad 2 does not read.
  • Animations. An animation file named without .anm is tried first as a folder: every .anm in it is a variant, picked per unit. Sequences can be additive and carry events. Assault Squad 2 takes one file and no events.
  • Materials. A second diffuse line in a .mtl is an error in Gates of Hell.
  • The other way round. A mod for Gates of Hell itself needs a folder name with no space, -, + or other sign; the GoH button's Check page checks it against Gates of Hell, and Mods > Mods > Upgrade or Port, which shows every upgrade setting under GoH, can plan a port of an Assault Squad 2 mod --to goh.

Bring an old mod up to the 64-bit build

The 64-bit build of the game (as64.exe) runs in two modes. In Classic mode it loads mods written for the original game version 3.262. In Enhanced mode, which is on when the built-in package as64+ is active, it loads only mods that declare a minimum game version of 3.301 or higher. The version lines in mod.info decide the mode. Upgrading makes a new copy with the right version lines and the changes the 64-bit build needs. The old mod is never written.

You need

  • The old mod folder. A Steam Workshop mod is fine: it is only read.
  • Room for a copy next to it.
  • The 64-bit build installed, and its folder known to ARSENAL.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to change and choose an old mod to 64-bit. The task asks for the old mod, where the new copy goes and a few extra choices, shows the upgrade plan at the review, then makes the copy in a new folder; the old mod is only read. It needs no mod picked at the top.

Steps

  1. See what would change. In the window: open Mods > Mods > Upgrade or Port, card "Upgrade an old mod to AS64". Fill in "Old mod" and choose the "Kind": "Enhanced (new AS64 features)" or "Classic (as close to the old mod as possible)". Press "See what changes". On the command line: `` ARSENAL upgrade <old mod> --to as64 --plan `` The report sorts each point into: read, would change, cannot do, needs a look, and test in game.
  2. Make the AS64 copy. In the window: press "Make the AS64 copy" and confirm. The copy goes into a new folder next to the old one and becomes the current mod. On the command line: `` ARSENAL upgrade <old mod> --to as64 --out <new folder> --mode enhanced ` Use --mode classic for a Classic copy. --then-fix also runs the safe fixes and a check on the result. The copy holds an UPGRADE.md` report. Exit code 3 means something was left out or findings remain.

What the upgrade changes for you:

  • the version lines in mod.info: 3.262 to 3.262 for Classic, a minimum of 3.301 with no maximum for Enhanced;
  • a mod.info for a folder that had none;
  • include paths of files that moved in the 64-bit build;
  • text read as cp1251 rewritten as UTF-8 (the 64-bit build reads strings as UTF-8), and line ends set to CRLF;
  • the Workshop FileId line removed, so the copy can never be uploaded over the original item;
  • a Require line for a mod the 64-bit build already has built in, dropped;
  • .dll files left out: they are tied to one build of the old program.
  1. Check the copy. In the window: the Check page, "Check the mod". On the command line: ARSENAL check <new folder> --target as64. LOADS_STATIC means no known crash pattern was found; it does not mean the mod works.
  2. Play a test match. In the window: on the Play page, card "Play a test match", press "play: dry run" and read the steps, then "play". It uses its own game copy (instance 1). On the command line: ARSENAL play <new folder> --dry, then ARSENAL play <new folder>.
  3. Switch it on in your own game. Install it (the Play page's "Install into the game", or ARSENAL install <new folder>). In the game, open Options, Mods, move the mod to Activated, keep as64+ in Activated above an Enhanced mod, and press Apply. Applying takes about half a minute and needs no restart.
  4. Test what the report asked for. On the Read Game.log page (Mods > Check & Fix > Read Game.log), "Try these in the game" is a tick list built from the notes written during the upgrade, plus the basics.
  5. Before you share it, read Pack and share. A mod made from someone else's needs that author's permission.

What can go wrong

  • The mod is not in the list, or does nothing. A mod in the wrong mode is switched off without a message. One mod.info cannot run in both modes; to reach both, keep two copies. A mod with no version lines at all is treated as unsupported.
  • The game will not start after a mode change. A mod of the wrong kind left in the active list has caused a fatal Unable to determine fallback font before the menu. Take it out of the list.
  • Letters come out as boxes or as Cyrillic. Old text in cp1251 shows as boxes on the 64-bit build until it is UTF-8. The upgrade converts it, and warns when a file looked like Western accented letters instead; fix those lines by hand.
  • Your own shader files were built for the old program and may break rendering (unconfirmed).
  • A broken bot script passes unseen. A Lua error no longer stops the game: the bot goes idle and the log says Lua call failed.
  • Animations look smeared. Mesh-frame animations are blended every step now, so deliberately abrupt keys smear. This is only visual.
  • Behaviour changes with no sign in the data, such as how weapons aim, are listed as behaviour warnings. Only a match shows whether they matter.
  • Multiplayer: a Classic player cannot join an Enhanced game, and every player needs the same build and the same mod list in the same order.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • No Classic and Enhanced. Gates of Hell has one mode and no as64+. Its version numbers are 1.x, so an Assault Squad 2 mod.info with 3.262 or 3.301 bounds is switched off there until the bounds are rewritten.
  • Version lines. Each bound may be left out; a missing bound is open. A Tags line with the word develop lifts the version check, and so does the console command dev_disableModVersionControl. Priority (a number, default 1) orders mods that do not need each other.
  • Folder name. A space, -, +, a letter outside plain English or another sign in the folder name makes Gates of Hell skip the mod with only a warning in game.log.
  • ARSENAL under the GoH button hides the "Upgrade an old mod to AS64" card, and the task "an old mod to 64-bit" makes a Gates of Hell copy there. On Mods > Mods > Upgrade or Port the fold "Advanced: every upgrade setting" stays open there and can plan or write a port of an Assault Squad 2 mod for Gates of Hell. On the command line: ARSENAL upgrade <mod> --to goh --plan, then with --out <new folder>. It sets the version lines for the Gates of Hell version it finds (--goh <GoH folder> or --goh-version), and --donor swaps vehicle definitions for Gates of Hell ones.
  • Workshop mods in Gates of Hell are known by mod_<item number>, not by their title.

Check a mod, fix what the check finds, read the game log

Checking reads your mod's files and lists what would stop it from loading, crash the game or be ignored, without starting the game. Fixing writes the safe repairs into a separate patch mod, a new folder that loads after yours, so your mod is never changed. The game log, game.log, is what the game itself wrote on its last run.

You need

  • Your mod folder, picked on the Mods page.
  • The game folder known to ARSENAL.
  • For the log: the game started at least once with your mod on.

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to change and choose a mod with problems (fix them). The task looks for problems, makes the safe fixes after a review, and then walks you through the rest one per screen. For the log, set "I want to" to explore and choose what went wrong in the last run: it lists the errors of the last run in plain words, with the file and line and what to do, and offers the fix task next. It writes nothing.

Steps

  1. Check the mod. In the window: open the Check page (Mods > Check & Fix > Check). Its guided fix has seven steps: "Pick the mod", "Check", "Review findings", "Choose fixes", "Apply into a new folder", "What changed and next steps" and "Fix the rest by hand". "quick check" skips the slow deep scans; the page ticks it for you on a big mod and unticks it on a small one (under 300 files), and your own tick wins. Press "Check the mod". On the command line: `` ARSENAL check <mod folder> ARSENAL check <mod folder> --fast ARSENAL check <mod folder> --plain ` The verdict is LOADS_STATIC (no known crash pattern found), LIKELY_CRASH or REFUSED (the game would not load it). The exit code is 0 for LOADS_STATIC, 1 otherwise. --plain` prints the result in plain words only: one line for the overall result, then one line per finding.
  2. Read the findings. In the window: "Review findings" shows one card per problem, most serious first, with "Where", "Why it matters" and "How to fix". "Open in Editor" jumps to the line in the Editor page.
  3. Choose and apply fixes. In the window: under "Choose fixes", the safe fixes are ticked for you; fixes marked "check after" change how something looks and start unticked. "Select all", "Select none" and "Only safe fixes" set the ticks at once. Fill in the "patch folder" (a new folder, not inside your mod), press "Apply ticked fixes" and confirm in the confirm box. A finding's "Rerun ... alone" button runs only the tool that found it again. On the command line: `` ARSENAL fix <mod folder> plan ARSENAL fix <mod folder> apply --out <patch folder> ` plan writes nothing. To undo, delete the patch folder. --only <kinds> limits the fix to some kinds; among them, botkeys removes bot data keys the game does not read, and lngdup removes the earlier copy of a text key that a .lng` file repeats (the later one is what the game shows).
  4. Check again with the patch. In the window: "Check again with the patch" compares the counts before and after. On the command line: ARSENAL check <mod folder> --with <patch folder>. In the game, enable the patch mod together with your mod, the patch after it.

Fix the rest by hand. Problems with no automatic fix stay on their cards with the steps to fix them. "Walk through the hand fixes" shows each place with its lines and the suggested change, and opens it in the Editor ("Previous", "Next", "Next kind", "Done", "Close the walkthrough"). Up to 50 places are listed per kind of problem; check again after fixing to see the rest. What you change there goes into your mod itself, and the Editor keeps a restore point.

  1. Run the game. In the window: the Play page. Switch on "Let ARSENAL start the game" first; then "play: dry run" shows each step and "play" starts a test match and says from the log whether the mod loaded (BOOT). On the command line: ARSENAL play <mod folder> --dry, then ARSENAL play <mod folder>.
  2. Read the log. In the window: open the Read Game.log page (Mods > Check & Fix > Read Game.log) and press "Explain my last game log". The newest game.log is read and explained in plain words, each card with "What to do". "Show the game's own text" shows the original lines. "Read every game window" adds the test copies, crash reports and out-of-sync reports. On the command line: `` ARSENAL logtriage <log folder or game.log> --mod <mod folder> --game <game folder> ` The log is in your Documents folder under My Games\Men of War - Assault Squad 2\log\; a test copy writes to ... - instance N`.
  3. Follow a missing mod or unit. On the Read Game.log page, "Why is it missing?" checks the mod's mod.info, version lines, folder name and whether it is switched on. "Check this unit" follows a unit from its file to its model, materials, buy card, army and picture, and names the first broken link. "Show what is switched on" lists your mods in the order the game uses.

Reading a log line yourself

  • [hh:mm:ss] message (/path/file.def, 188) was raised while a data file was read. The path tells you whether the line is about your mod.
  • An ***** Exception ***** block means the game stopped. The common causes are define not found (a macro call with no visible definition), unexpected token (a missing brace, a wrong word, or a bone or volume name that is gone), and Resource not found (a mesh, volume, animation or material that does not exist; check the name and its case).
  • No Stuff found for tags 'X' (may lead to crash) is the one warning that turns into a crash, when the missing weapon or ammo is used.
  • Localization key redefinition lines and Mission ... is skipped for leftover titles appear in a clean game too. Keep a clean run's log and look for new kinds of message.

What can go wrong

  • A clean check is not proof. LOADS_STATIC means no known crash pattern was found, not that the mod does what you meant. Wrong but valid values pass every check.
  • The log you needed is gone. The game overwrites game.log at every start and keeps the run before only once, as game.prev.log. Copy it before you start the game again.
  • A fix applies to a whole group. Ticking part of a group applies all of it; the page warns "Fix applies whole groups".
  • A misspelled key is skipped silently by the game. The check finds it; the log usually does not.
  • Line order in the log misleads. Phase ... lines print after the data warnings, so a warning's position says nothing about whether it came from your mod.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • Check under the GoH button. The Check page checks the mod against Gates of Hell. Its fix steps write a Gates of Hell patch mod (fix --target goh); the fixes that follow Assault Squad 2 rules are left out, each with a line saying why. The task "a mod with problems (fix them)" still only looks there. On the command line: ARSENAL check <mod folder> --target goh --goh <GoH folder>, then ARSENAL fix <mod folder> plan --target goh.
  • Read Game.log under the GoH button reads the game.log in the Gates of Hell user folder, and so does the task "what went wrong in the last run". On the command line: ARSENAL logtriage --exe goh. Many Gates of Hell lines still come out as unknown kinds; [LUA] lines are read.
  • Where the log is. Under Documents, My Games\Gates of Hell\log\, or under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Digitalmindsoft\Gates of Hell\log\ when Documents is on OneDrive or the game was started with -useLocalDataFolder.
  • Every line starts with [hh:mm:ss], warnings too.
  • Mod lines to look for: Scanning mods in, Found N available mods, Mod: activate mod <name>, Warning: invalid mod folder name, Warning: empty mod.info file found at, Warning: failed to load mod and Warning! Duplicate mod found. A folder named with a space, - or another sign is skipped with the folder name warning.

Pack and share

A mod that works on your computer must reach other players with the right version lines, no stray files, correctly packed paths, and the same data for everyone in a match. The Share page walks through this and shows what it will write before it writes.

You need

  • A mod that passed the check and a test match (see Check a mod, fix it, read the log).
  • A preview picture: PNG or JPG, under 1 MB.
  • For the Steam Workshop: Steam running and signed in. The Workshop uploader, workshop_gui.exe, comes with ARSENAL; the Share page puts it into the game folder for you (step 4).

The quick way

In the Quick Guided Task row above the tabs, set "I want to" to make and choose a release. The task asks for the name, text and version, the picture, runs the release check, makes the package and the clean Workshop copy in a folder you pick, and makes a play card for friends; "More checks" covers mods played together and a game update. The upload itself stays on the Share page: the task does not put the uploader into the game folder or start it.

Steps

  1. Describe the mod. In the window: open the Share page, step "About my mod". Fill in "Name", "Description" and "Version". Under "Which game version can friends use?" pick "Older game (Classic, 3.262)" or "Newer game (Enhanced, 3.301 and up)". Press "Show what will change", then "Save to mod.info". Under "Preview picture" press "Choose picture..." and "Use this picture"; it is copied into the mod as preview.png or preview.jpg. On the command line: ARSENAL modinfo <mod folder> reports what the game makes of mod.info; edit it in a text editor, keeping CRLF line ends.
  2. Check that it is ready. In the window: "Ready to share?", press "Check if ready". Tick "Also run the check for known crash problems (slower)" for the full check. It checks mod.info, the version range, name, description, version and picture, stray files (.git, notes, UPGRADE.md), Gates of Hell content, and whether the files can be packed. On the command line: `` ARSENAL check <mod folder> ARSENAL packer <mod folder> --dry ARSENAL release-check --publish <mod folder> `` The last line refuses (exit 1) a mod that still holds Gates of Hell files.
  3. Package it for friends. In the window: "Package for friends". Choose the "Folder to write into", press "Show plan", then "Write package". On the command line: ARSENAL packer <mod folder> --out <folder> (without --out, or with --dry, it only plans). A friend puts the mod folder into the game's mods folder, then in the game opens Options, Mods, moves it to Activated (with as64+ above it for an Enhanced mod), and presses Apply. The game applies the mods in about half a minute; no restart is needed.
  4. Upload to the Steam Workshop. In the window: "Workshop" shows the checklist. Press "Show what the clean copy holds", then "Make clean copy". The box "Workshop uploader" says whether the uploader is in the game folder. Press "Put the uploader into the game folder"; the page lists each file it will copy, then "Copy these files now" copies them beside the game program. A steam_api64.dll or steam_appid.txt already in the game folder is never overwritten, and no other game file is touched. "Another game folder, for example Gates of Hell" puts it into another game instead of the one ARSENAL is set to. Then press "Open the Workshop uploader" (Steam must be running and signed in), choose the clean copy folder, fill in the title and the picture, and press Upload. On the first upload the uploader writes the Workshop ID into mod.info. "Check again" looks at the game folder again.
  5. Release a new version. In the window: "New version". Pick "Small fix (1.0 to 1.0.1)", "New things (1.0 to 1.1)" or "Big change (1.0 to 2.0)", write a "Change note" press "Show what will happen", then "Set the new version". Then check, make the clean copy and upload again.
  6. Play together. In the window: "Play together" makes a short text card for your friends' chat: which mods, in which order, on which game build. Press "Make the card". "Mods together" takes two or more installed mods and, with "Show clashes", lists the files and values they both change. The last mod in the list wins every clash. On the command line: `` ARSENAL conflicts --game <game folder> --mods a,b ARSENAL mpsync --game <game folder> --mods a,b --export fp.json ARSENAL mpsync --compare a.json b.json ``
  7. After a game update. In the window: "Game updated?", press "Check for a game update". On the command line: ARSENAL release-check compares the game with the last known build, and ARSENAL release-check --replan <mod folder> shows what the changes hit in your mod.

What can go wrong

  • Friends cannot see the mod. A mod with no version range, or for the other mode, is switched off without a message. To reach both Classic and Enhanced players, share two copies.
  • Files packed one folder off. A pak placed directly in the mod's resource/ folder must hold its top folder names, such as entity/... or set/..., inside it. Let the packer build the paks.
  • A loose .patch file is never read. Only patches inside a numbered N.pat archive are.
  • The Workshop gets everything in the folder, including .git, notes and development files. Upload the clean copy.
  • Changing the Name after the first upload changes the mod's folder name on every subscriber's computer.
  • Keep the FileId line in mod.info. It ties the folder to your Workshop item.
  • A desync in a match although the lobby agreed. The lobby compares model, volume, material, animation and Lua files by size only. If a changed binary file kept its size, also change a text file so the lobby sees a difference.
  • Gates of Hell content can never be shared or uploaded. The packer refuses a mod that still holds it.
  • A mod made from someone else's needs that author's permission. Name the original mod and its author in the description, and share it as a new Workshop item, not as an update of theirs.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • ARSENAL under the GoH button has the Share page: it fills in mod.info with the Gates of Hell version range, packs in the Gates of Hell layout and runs the release checks against Gates of Hell. The release task of the Quick Guided Task is greyed. "Put the uploader into the game folder" puts the Workshop uploader beside the Gates of Hell program in binaries\x64 and does not overwrite the steam_api64.dll there.
  • Packing. Gates of Hell reads only resource/, N.pat and localizations/ in a mod. A resource.pak, localization.pak or localization/ in the mod's root is not read there: put paks into resource/.
  • mod.info. Use Gates of Hell's own version numbers (1.x); each bound may be left out. Tags may hold develop (any game version) and no_delete (no delete button in the mod list). Priority orders mods that do not need each other.
  • Folder name. No space, -, + or other sign, or Gates of Hell skips the mod. Subscribers see a Workshop mod as mod_<item number>.
  • Gates of Hell content in an Assault Squad 2 mod can never be shared: the packer and the release check refuse a mod whose GOH-ORIGIN.tsv files are still in it.

More

Find guides and tools others made

Modders have written guides and tools for the GEM engine games (Men of War, Assault Squad 2, Gates of Hell and others) for years, spread over forums, wikis, file sites and Discord servers. The Guides & External Tools page (tab Help & Docs) searches a saved index of about 9,000 such links, offline. It shows what others made and where; it does not copy or vouch for their work.

You need

  • The guide index folder. It is not part of ARSENAL, because its saved pages are other sites' text. It is a folder that holds a guides.json file and a builtin folder.
  • A web browser for opening the links.

Steps

  1. Point ARSENAL at the index. In the window: open Help & Docs > Guides & External Tools. If it says "The guide index was not found", it lists where it looked; press "Pick the index folder". It is used until ARSENAL closes; "Use another index folder" and "Back to the default folder" switch it later. On the command line: every gemindex command takes --data <folder>. Without it the tool looks at the environment variable GEM_INDEX_DIR, then at a gemindex folder next to the exe.
  2. Search. In the window: on the "Search" tab, type "Words to find". Narrow with "Show" ("Everything", "Complete guides", "Tools and plugins", "Other links", "History"), "Game" (for this game, "AS2 and AS64 related"), "Topic", "Sub-topic" and "Language". Tick "Also search the saved page text (slower)", "Include links posted on Discord", or "Only copies of closed sites (Wayback Machine)" for forums that are gone. Press "Search". On the command line: `` ARSENAL gemindex search armour penetration --game as2rel --tab guides --text ` --tab takes guides, tools, history, less or all; --lang, --archived and --limit n` narrow further.
  3. Read a result. In the window: "Preview text" shows the saved text of a page. "Open in browser" opens the original in your normal browser. On the command line: ARSENAL gemindex show <id or address> --around <word> prints the row and an excerpt.
  4. Browse questions, tools and missing pieces.
    • "Questions and answers" lists answers picked from old forum pages by keyword. Command: ARSENAL gemindex faq <words>.
    • "Tools by topic" groups the tools and plugins in the index by what they do. Command: ARSENAL gemindex tools --game as2rel.
    • "What ARSENAL can and can't make" says, for each kind of content (3D models, textures, sound, maps, animation, icons, object editing, mod managers), what ARSENAL does itself and what still has to be made in another program, with guides and tools for each and the ARSENAL page to go to. Models and animations, for example, are edited on the Models page, while a new mesh shape or a painted texture comes from another program. Command: ARSENAL gemindex gaps --lang en.
  5. Keep a list. In the window: under "Export these results", pick a "File type", press "Count first" then "Pick a folder and save". On the command line: ARSENAL gemindex export <words> --out links.csv --dry, then without --dry. The file may end in .csv, .md or .json.
  6. Credit what you use. Share the links, not copied page text. The texts belong to each page's author.
  7. Fetch more pages (optional, goes online). In the window: the "Update the index" tab fetches the public pages behind links that have no saved text yet. Choose "Which links" and "At most", then press "Try it first (nothing goes online)" to see the pages and sites. "Start (goes online)" fetches one page at a time and obeys each site's robots.txt; "Stop" ends after the current page. Fetched pages are saved only in the index folder, in its scrape folder. On the command line: ARSENAL gemindex scrape <words> --missing --limit 25 --dry, then without --dry. ARSENAL gemindex wayback <id> lists archive captures of one page.

What can go wrong

  • "The guide index was not found." Pick the folder that holds guides.json. The "What ARSENAL can and can't make" tab still works.
  • A link is dead. Many pages are more than ten years old. Try "Only copies of closed sites" or gemindex wayback.
  • A download is unsafe. ARSENAL does not open or safety-check any link. Downloads from these pages are untrusted: scan them first, keep them in their own empty folder, and never run them from inside your game folder.
  • A tool is for another game. Most tools in the index were made for other GEM games. Check which game a tool is for before you use it on your mod.
  • A Discord link does not open. Such links often need a server invite, and files there can expire.
  • An answer is wrong. The "Questions and answers" tab picks answers by keyword rules and nobody has checked them. Treat them as hints; many are in Russian. Confirm them against this guide and in the game.
  • The preview is cut off or shows broken letters. The saved text is only part of the page, and old pages can carry broken encodings. Open the original for the rest.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • The Guides & External Tools page is there under every game, GoH included, and searches the same index.
  • Many links are for Gates of Hell. The index covers all GEM games, and most of the mod managers in it are Gates of Hell tools. Check which game a guide or tool is for before you follow it.
  • Mod layout advice does not carry over. Gates of Hell reads only resource/, N.pat and localizations/ in a mod and skips folder names with a space or -; an Assault Squad 2 guide's folder advice can be wrong there, and the other way round.
  • Outside programs. When a Quick Guided Task sends you to a program that is not on your PC, its card links to this page with the program's name as the search words.

Use the Quick Guided Task

The Quick Guided Task is the row above the tabs of the ARSENAL window. You say what you want ("I want to make a vehicle", "I want to change the prices of an army") and a task window asks one question at a time, shows what it will write, writes it into your mod, checks it and tells you what to look at in the game. It does the jobs of the other pages of this part from one place. This page shows how to start a task, what each of the 27 tasks does, where a task keeps your answers and what it writes.

You need

  • The ARSENAL window, open on the PC itself. From a phone or another device on the LAN the tasks are greyed: "only on the PC, not from another device".
  • The game folder known to ARSENAL (most tasks need it to read the game's own files).
  • For every task that writes into a mod: a mod picked at the top of the window. A task can also make a new empty mod for you on its first step.

Steps

  1. Pick a task. In the window: the row starts with "Quick Guided Task" and "I want to". Pick the verb, make, change or explore, then the task in the list beside it. "Type to filter" narrows the list as you type. Press "Start". A greyed task says why: "needs a mod picked", "needs the game folder", "not for" the game picked in the header, "not built yet", or "this task has a fault" with the reason. On the command line: the row has no command of its own. Each task runs the same tools as the pages; the Part I page for the job, in the table below, gives the commands.
  2. Choose how many questions. The first step, "Quick or everything", asks "How many questions should the task ask?". Quick asks only the main questions; everything else stays as in the thing you copy (or as it is now, for a change). Everything asks every value, one by one. The switch "How many questions" at the top of the window changes it at any time.
  3. Pick the mod and the thing to copy or change. The step "Mod" asks "Which mod does this go into?" and offers the mod picked at the top. "Make the mod" makes a new empty mod in the game's mods folder. The next step, "What to copy" (make) or "What to change" (change), picks the unit, gun, map or other thing to start from.
  4. Answer the questions. The window has three parts: "Steps" (the list of steps, each marked done, kept, to do or needs a look), the question, and "Look" (a preview of the thing: a small 3D view for a model or a unit, a picture, a sound, or the first lines of a text file). "So far" lists your answers. "Next" (Enter) goes on, "Back" (Alt+Left) goes back. "Keep as copied" keeps a value, and "Keep this whole group as copied" or "Ask me this group" skips or opens a whole group of questions. Where a question needs a file or another thing, it offers:
    • Use one that exists in the game or a mod.
    • Copy one and change it. This opens a branch task for that thing ("Open the branch task"); when it is done, "Back to" returns to the task above.
    • Bring my own file. "Pick a file from this PC" or "Or pick a whole folder", up to 64 MB. The kind of file is read from its bytes, not its name.
    • Make it in an outside program. A card names the program (SOEdit, Blender, an image or DDS editor, Audacity and others), whether it is on this PC, and the steps. "Open it" starts it, "Open the folder with my files" shows where to save, and "I am done: here is my file" or "I am done: it is saved in my mod" brings the result back. ARSENAL never downloads a program; a program that is not on this PC links to the Guides & External Tools page.
  5. Review and write. "Review" lists every answer ("Look over every answer"; "Details" opens one). "Write" lists every file the task will write, with "Write it into the mod". Press "Write" and confirm "Write these files into your mod?" in the confirm box. A restore point is taken first. "Do not write now: save and close" keeps the task for later.
  6. Check and test. "Check" runs the check on your mod ("Check now"). "Test in game" sends you to the Play page; the task window never starts the game itself. "What to look at in game" is a tick list for the match. "What next" offers "Make another", "Make one like it", "Back to the tabs" and "Share the mod".
  7. Stop and come back later. "Save and close" (Esc) closes the window; every answer is already saved. Back in the row, "Saved tasks" lists your open tasks: pick one and press "Continue" to go on at its step, or "Throw away" to delete it. A page reload opens the open task again.

The tasks

The window shows each task as the verb plus the title below. Most tasks are for Assault Squad 2, both the 64-bit build and the original program; the last column says which game, picked in the header, they work under.

Task in the rowWhat it doesGames

"Both builds" means the 64-bit build and the original 32-bit program. Explore tasks only read: they have no review, write, check or test steps.

Sounds, voice sets and armies have no Part I page of their own: see chapter 16, Effects, sound and models and chapter 12, Missions and multiplayer setup (armies).

What it writes and where

  • Your answers. One file per task in ARSENAL's own data folder, %LOCALAPPDATA%\ARSENAL\tasks, saved on every answer. Files you bring wait in a folder of the system's temporary folder until the task writes them.
  • Your mod. Only "Write" changes the mod, and only the files the Write step lists. "Make a mod" makes a new mod folder, the upgrade task writes a new folder next to the old mod, and the release task also writes the package and the clean copy into the folder you pick, outside the mod.
  • Restore points. Before a file is written, a restore point is taken in a folder next to your mod, named after it with .arsenal-undo. Undo a write in the Editor's Restore points panel ("Open the restore points").
  • Never. The game folder and other mods are never written, and the game is never started from the task window.

"Throw away" asks "Throw this saved task away?". It removes your answers, the files you brought and any branch tasks. Files already written into your mod stay; undo them with the restore points.

What can go wrong

  • The task you want is greyed. Read the reason beside it. Pick a mod at the top, set the game folder, or pick another game in the header.
  • A file you bring is refused. The kind is read from the bytes, so a renamed file of the wrong kind is refused, as is a file over 64 MB.
  • The task stops before writing. The Write step stops at the first error in its plan, before any file is written. Fix the answer it names and press "Write" again.
  • A write did more than you wanted. Undo it in the Editor's Restore points panel. A file a tool changed without a restore point is listed as written with no restore point.
  • The outside program is "not on this PC". Install it yourself; the card links to the Guides & External Tools page.
  • A Quick task kept a value you wanted to change. Switch "How many questions" to Everything, or open the group with "Ask me this group".
  • Nothing shows in the game. A written and checked mod still has to be switched on and tested. See Check a mod, fix it, read the log.

In Gates of Hell

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

  • Tasks that work under the GoH button: "a mod" (make), "an old mod to 64-bit" (it makes a Gates of Hell copy), "a mod with problems (fix them)", "a unit from Gates of Hell", and the explore tasks "a mod", "what went wrong in the last run" and "what is possible": seven of the 27. Every other task is greyed "not for" Gates of Hell.
  • "A mod with problems" only looks. There are no one-click fixes for Gates of Hell: the cards say what to change by hand, and nothing is written.
  • "A unit from Gates of Hell" writes into an Assault Squad 2 mod, not into Gates of Hell. The header shows where the results go.
  • "What went wrong in the last run" reads the Assault Squad 2 log folders. Gates of Hell keeps its game.log under Documents, My Games\Gates of Hell\log, or under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Digitalmindsoft\Gates of Hell\log when Documents is on OneDrive. Read it on the command line: ARSENAL logtriage <that log folder>. Every Gates of Hell log line starts with [hh:mm:ss], and many of its lines are not yet known to the reader.
  • The Play and Share buttons at the end of a task lead to pages that belong to Assault Squad 2.

Work with Claude: skills and MCP servers

ARSENAL comes with a set of skills and two MCP servers for Claude. With them Claude can look up how the game behaves, check and change a mod, tell you whether a gun beats a tank, read the game log, and work the ARSENAL window for you. They cover Men of War: Assault Squad 2, its 64-bit build AS64 and Gates of Hell, for modding and for playing.

Two terms first. A skill is a short guide Claude loads when your question matches it: it tells Claude which tool to use and which rule of the game applies. An MCP server is a small program that gives Claude tools it can call, such as "check this mod". The skills name the server tools first and the plain command second, so they work with or without the servers.

You need

  • Claude Code or Claude Desktop.
  • Node.js, and the ARSENAL folder with its tools folder and .claude/skills folder.
  • For the window tools: the ARSENAL window running (node tools/gui/gui.js).

The quick way

In the ARSENAL window open Help & Docs > Claude. The page lists every skill and every group of tools as its own piece, the pack groups (Modding, Playing, The three games and lookups, ARSENAL window, RobZ Realism) and the full pack. Each has "Download" (a zip) and "Install into Claude". Pick where to install (Claude Code for you, one project folder, or Claude Desktop), press Preview to see the exact files and entries, then Install. It makes a backup of a settings file before it changes it, leaves other entries alone, and "Uninstall" takes out only what it put in. For Claude Desktop the skills are saved as zips for you to upload there.

The same from the command line:

node tools/mcp/pack/pack.js list
node tools/mcp/pack/pack.js zip --group playing --out playing.zip
node tools/mcp/pack/pack.js install --all --target claude-code-user --write

Steps

  1. Switch the servers on. In Claude Code, started in the ARSENAL folder: nothing to set up. The file .mcp.json registers both servers; approve them when Claude Code asks and check with /mcp. From another folder, or in Claude Desktop: follow tools/mcp/install.md. It gives the two claude mcp add lines and the block for claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Say which game you mean. Every tool takes the game: as64, mowas2 or goh. Tell Claude the game once ("this is for Gates of Hell") or set ARSENAL_GAME. Without either, AS64 is used. One tool serves all three games and names the differences in its answer; where a game can not be served, the answer says why.
  3. Ask in plain words. Claude picks the skill by what you ask. Examples:
    • "Check my mod in D:\my-mods\frontline and tell me what is wrong."
    • "Can a Panther's gun go through a T-34-85 at 500 m from the front?"
    • "Why did the game crash on loading the map?"
    • "My friend and I get out of sync with this mod. Which files differ?"
    • "Raise the price of the Tiger in my mod by 10 percent."
    • "Open the Units page on the Tiger in the ARSENAL window."
  4. Allow writing, if you want Claude to change files. Out of the box every tool only reads. A tool that changes files answers a preview: what it would change. To allow changes, set ARSENAL_WRITE_ROOTS to the folder that holds your own mods (more than one with ; between them) and restart the server. Claude must still ask for the change with write: true; the preview comes first.
  5. Allow starting the game, if you want test runs. Set ARSENAL_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 and restart the server. Then Claude can switch the enabled mods, start a test match, drive the menus and take a screenshot. Without it Claude can still ask for a dry run, which says what would be started and starts nothing.

The two servers

arsenal (tools/mcp/server.js) works on its own, without the window. Its tools, by group:

GroupWhat the tools doExamples
KnowledgeHow the game behaves, known limits, what differs between the games, which tool does a job, the pages of this guide.mow_lookup, mow_limit, mow_game_diff, mow_tools, mow_guide
ModsRead, check and fix a mod; what a mod changes; clashes between mods and a patch mod that keeps both sides; upgrade or move a mod to another game; pack it.mow_mod_info, mow_mod_check, mow_mod_fix, mow_mod_diff, mow_mods_clash, mow_mods_patch, mow_mod_upgrade, mow_port_plan, mow_mod_pack
Units and weaponsFind a unit or a weapon, read its numbers, change price, armour, name, squad, equipment, weapon slots, skin and texture variant.mow_unit_find, mow_unit_stats, mow_unit_change, mow_kit_slot, mow_look_set, mow_weapon_find, mow_weapon_change
Text, maps, modes, botsFind and set a text; read maps and missions; copy a map, add a game mode, place an object; allow and check bots.mow_text_find, mow_text_set, mow_map_info, mow_map_clone, mow_mode_add, mow_map_place, mow_mode_bots, mow_bots_recipe
Balance and multiplayerUnits whose price does not fit, the price calculator, which files the lobby compares between players.mow_balance_check, mow_price, mow_mp_sync
PlayingThe install and its enabled mods, the last game log, a crash explained, gun against armour, the armour of a unit, what an army can buy, what beats a unit, game modes, bots, options and key bindings.mow_game_status, mow_game_log, mow_game_crash, mow_matchup, mow_unit_armor, mow_army, mow_unit_counter, mow_mode_info, mow_bots_info, mow_settings_info
Running the gameSwitch the enabled mods, start a match, drive the menus, take a screenshot. Off until you allow it.mow_mods_enable, mow_game_start, mow_game_drive, mow_game_shot
Models, textures, effects, soundFind and read a model, check it, copy it into a mod, missing textures, animations, sounds, effects, icons.mow_model_find, mow_model_info, mow_model_check, mow_asset_missing, mow_texture_info, mow_anim_list, mow_sound_find, mow_fx_find, mow_icon_check
ScriptsCheck interaction scripts, mission triggers and bot Lua; list the events and commands the game knows; find where one is used.mow_script_lint, mow_script_words, mow_script_find, mow_mission_lint, mow_mission_triggers, mow_lua_check, mow_console_find
RobZ RealismFind the installed RobZ, what it changes, its own systems, its unit cards, check a sub-mod against it, known issues.mow_robz_find, mow_robz_changes, mow_robz_system, mow_robz_unit, mow_robz_submod, mow_robz_issues

Load only what you need. The tools sit in small groups (knowledge, mod, together, units, weapons, text, maps, bots, play, coach, run, assets, scripts, robz). Started plain, the server offers all of them. Started with --groups units,weapons it offers only those, so Claude reads a short tool list. The Claude page and tools/mcp/install.md give the ready lines per group.

arsenal-gui (tools/mcp/gui.js) talks to the running ARSENAL window. It finds the window by itself. Its tool list is made from the window's own pages and routes, so it follows the window as the window changes.

ToolWhat it does
gui_statusWhether the window runs, which game tab is open, which mod is chosen.
gui_pagesThe tabs and pages, and what each is for.
gui_routesWhat the window can be asked, with the fields of each request.
gui_callOne request to the window: the same answer the page shows. A request that changes files answers a preview first; the change itself needs a folder you allowed and a clear yes in the call (write: true in the request, or confirm_write: true where the window has no preview of its own). Requests that open the window to other devices are never sent.
gui_jobsLong jobs that are running or done.
gui_openA link that opens a page of the window for you, on the right game, unit or file.
gui_langThe words on a page, in the language of the window.
gui_startStarts the window when it is not running. Off until you allow starting (ARSENAL_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1).

The full list, one line per tool and skill, is in tools/mcp/CATALOG.md. It is written by a command, so it is always the list of what is really there.
