  • A name with letters outside plain ASCII may be at most 1023 bytes; a longer one stops with path is too long.
  • Each pak entry without a CRC writes no crc for file in package ... performance may be slowed to the log. Write paks with a tool that stores real CRCs.
  • A damaged pak entry stops the game with Failed to read file from pak <name>, so it names the pak. In Assault Squad 2 the same damage goes unnoticed.
  • Text entries are kept in memory after their first read, not read in at mount time; model entries are read from the pak each time.
  • A multiplayer map that carries its own resource.pak inside the map folder is not read.
  • The log names each pak it mounts: Mount package <file> with <n> entries.

4. Encoding check

Before you pack, make sure the text files are what the engine expects.

  • Text data files (.def, .ext, .set, .mi, .patch, scripts and similar) use CRLF line endings.
  • The 64-bit build reads every string value as UTF-8, in data and .lng files alike. A string saved as cp1251 loads without error but shows as boxes on screen.
  • Identifiers and keywords must be plain ASCII. Old cp1251 bytes inside ; comments of vanilla files are skipped by the game; leave them as they are.
  • Paks are plain zip files.

Many editors silently change the encoding or line endings when you save, especially on files that contain Russian comments. A UTF-16 byte-order mark in an SDL file is fatal. The game itself reads a bare LF as a line break, so a missing CRLF will not break loading; the CRLF convention matches vanilla files and keeps version-control diffs clean. packer checks all of this and reports .lng files that are not UTF-8, string values that are not UTF-8, non-ASCII identifiers, UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte-order marks, and non-CRLF text. The enc pass of ARSENAL fix resaves cp1251 text values as UTF-8 in a patch mod. See chapter 5 and chapter 14.

In Gates of Hell

The game's own texts are .pot files (UTF-8), and the game ships no .lng files. A .lng file of a mod is read only from localizations/<code>/interface/text/ (section 2). Whether the other encoding rules of this section hold the same way is not mapped; check your mod with the Gates of Hell checks on the Check page. See chapter 14.

5. The pre-release gate

In the window, the Share page does this in order: "About my mod" fills in mod.info (name, description, version, and which game version can load it) and the preview picture; "Ready to share?" runs the release checks (tick the slower check for known crash problems too); "Package for friends" writes a ready mod folder with its paks into a folder you choose; "Workshop" makes a clean copy for the uploader. Each step shows what it will write before it writes.

  • About my mod: "Show what will change" lists the lines of mod.info that would change, and "Save to mod.info" writes them. Lines the form does not know, such as the Workshop ID, are kept as they are. For a mod made from someone else's, the credit line takes "Original mod" and "Original author", and "Add credit line to the description" adds "Ported from ... by ...". "Choose picture..." and "Use this picture" copy a PNG or JPG under 1 MB into the mod as preview.png or preview.jpg.
  • Ready to share?: "Check if ready" reads mod.info, the version range, the name, the description, the version, the picture, stray files (.git, notes, UPGRADE.md), Gates of Hell content and whether the files can be packed. Each line says OK, "Look at this" or "Fix this". "Also run the check for known crash problems (slower)" adds the static crash check.
  • Package for friends: "Show plan" and "Write package" write a ready mod folder (its mod.info and its paks) into a folder you choose. The folder may not be inside the game folder or a Steam folder ("Not this folder: ..."). Your friend puts the whole folder into the game's mods folder.
  • Before you share lists the rules for a mod made from someone else's: ask the author first, keep the credit, publish it as a new Workshop item. The Apache licence of ARSENAL covers the tool only and gives no rights to anyone's mod or to game files.

A mod that holds a GOH-ORIGIN.tsv file (content ported from Gates of Hell, see chapter 19) is refused by the package, the clean copy and the release check: "this mod holds Gates of Hell content (GOH-ORIGIN.tsv). That can never be shared, so it is not packed." Such a mod is for your private use only.

On the command line, run these from any folder. Replace G with your game folder.

ARSENAL build "G/mods/mymod" --game "G" --strict --out <pak folder>
ARSENAL packer "G/mods/mymod" --dry
ARSENAL doctor "G/mods/mymod" --game "G" --release
ARSENAL release-check --publish "G/mods/mymod"

build runs the whole linting pipeline (see chapter 19) and, only if it passes, writes the paks to the --out folder. With --strict, warnings count as failures too. The tool refuses to write paks inside a game install, so keep --out somewhere else. After writing, it reads each pak back to confirm it is valid.

packer --dry shows the plan: which loose files would go into which role pak, plus any encoding or name warnings. It also warns when a loose file would shadow an entry in a pak you are shipping. packer <mod folder> --out <folder> writes the package.

doctor --release is the ship checklist. It looks for stray development files and root notes, loose files that duplicate pak entries, a missing mod.info, empty folders, unusually large files (use --big MB to set the limit), and files that the multiplayer check compares only by size.

release-check --publish refuses (exit 1) a mod that still holds files ported from Gates of Hell, under their own or another name, or a pak packed for private use. Gates of Hell content can never be shared.

Do not skip this just because the mod runs. A leftover test file or a loose duplicate will not show up in your own testing and will bite someone else.

In Gates of Hell

Under the GoH header button the Share page works on a Gates of Hell mod: it fills in mod.info with the Gates of Hell version range, packs in the Gates of Hell layout (packer --goh) and runs the release checks against the Gates of Hell game; the lobby file check of "Play together" is not read for Gates of Hell. None of this has been tried in a running game, so before you share a Gates of Hell mod, also check three things by hand:

  • The mod does not replace set/registry.reg or set/registry/dlc.reg. Either one stops the game at start with Resource Error.
  • The mod folder name is plain letters, digits and _ (section 2).
  • Paks sit in resource/ and texts in localizations/ (section 2).

6. Multiplayer compatibility

If your mod changes gameplay data, every player in a match needs exactly the same data. Before a match, the lobby compares the games' data trees:

  • The game tree covers entity/, fx/, properties/, set/ and sound/. A separate map tree covers the single-player, bonus and multiplayer maps.
  • For text-like files (.set, .inc, .ext, .def, .mdl, .mi, .reg, .info, and map files), the lobby compares the contents.
  • For model, volume, material, animation, patch and Lua files, it compares only the file size.
  • Textures, sounds, localization, script/ and interface/ are not compared at all.

The size-only rule has a nasty consequence: if you change a model or volume file and the new file happens to be the same size, the lobby says everything matches, but the match later falls out of sync. If you ship a binary change, also change a text file so that the lobby sees a difference. The tool mpsync shows exactly which of your files are compared by content, which by size, and which not at all:

ARSENAL mpsync --mod "G/mods/mymod" --game "G"
ARSENAL mpsync --game "G" --mods a,b --export fp.json
ARSENAL mpsync --compare a.json b.json

The second and third lines compare two players' setups: each player exports a fingerprint of their game with the mods in order, and --compare lists what the lobby sees and what it misses.

The mod list also has to match, in the same order. A player who is missing a listed mod is told which one. Different game builds, for example 32-bit and 64-bit, cannot play together at all. The Share page's "Play together" step makes a short text card for your friends with the mods, their order and the game build. The rules for writing scripts that stay in sync are in chapter 12, and the symptoms of a desync are in chapter 21.

In Gates of Hell

  • The mod list a match uses is the list of mods that were loaded and applied, not the names in the options.
  • Players must have the same game version and the same build (x64). A host of another version is not even listed.
  • Gates of Hell and Assault Squad 2 (64-bit or not) never play together, and their chat, replays and saves do not cross.
  • By default the game does not compare checksums of the game state during a match (mp_syncLevel 0), so a match whose data differs is probably not stopped with a desync message: it just plays out differently on each PC. Treat matching mod files as your own job.
  • There is no download of mods inside the game. Every player gets the session's mods from the Workshop, so a multiplayer mod for Gates of Hell must be on the Workshop.
  • Whether the lobby compares data files the way described above is not mapped.

7. Versions and the minimum game version

mod.info carries a name, a description and a supported version range. See chapter 3 and Reference 1 for the keys. Four things matter at release time:

  • A legacy mod (for the 3.262 data) needs both MinGameVersion and MaxGameVersion. Without them it is treated as unsupported, unless the player has turned off the mod version check in the console. A modern mod needs only MinGameVersion of 3.301 or higher; its MaxGameVersion is ignored.
  • The two game modes filter mods by version. A mod whose MinGameVersion is 3.301 or higher counts as an Enhanced mod; one written for 3.262 counts as a Classic mod. Wrong-mode mods are switched off without a message. If you want both audiences, ship two copies or follow the guidance in chapter 3.
  • Only the parts that both version numbers have are compared, so 3.262.1 and 3.262 count as equal.
  • A mod.info the game cannot read, for example one with an unescaped quote in the description, stops the game from starting at all, for every player who has it in their mods folder.

Use modinfo before you release:

ARSENAL modinfo "G/mods/mymod"

In Gates of Hell

  • Versions are on the Gates of Hell scale, 1.x (the game is 1.067). An Assault Squad 2 number such as 3.301 is refused with "Unsupported game version". Rewrite both bounds when you move a mod across.
  • MinGameVersion and MaxGameVersion are each optional: a missing bound is open, so a mod with neither loads in any version.
  • A Tags line holds words separated by spaces. The tag develop lifts the version check for that mod, and no_delete hides its delete button. The console variable dev_disableModVersionControl lifts the check for every mod.
  • Priority (a whole number, 1 when missing) orders mods that do not depend on each other: a higher number is applied later and wins.
  • A mod.info the game cannot read skips only that mod, it does not stop the game.

See Reference 1 for these keys.

8. Steam Workshop

Two uploaders can publish a mod. ARSENAL's own Workshop uploader (workshop_gui.exe) is the one the Share page sets up and opens; see The ARSENAL Workshop uploader below. The game also ships its own uploader, mowas_2_workshop.exe in the game folder. Both take your whole mod folder, with these effects:

  • The game's own uploader requires a title, a description of up to 8000 bytes, a preview picture (JPG, PNG or GIF under 1 MB), tags, a visibility setting and a change note.
  • It looks for a preview named preview.jpg, .png, .gif or .jpeg in your mod folder, otherwise in mods/previews/<folder>.jpg. The Share page copies your picture into the mod as preview.png or preview.jpg.
  • Everything in the folder is uploaded. That includes a .git folder, notes and development files. Upload the clean copy the Share page makes, or exclude them yourself.
  • The uploader adds a {FileId "..."} line to your mod.info the first time. Every other byte is preserved. Leave that line in place on later uploads, because it tells the uploader which Workshop item the folder belongs to.
  • The 64-bit build loads a subscribed item in place, from Steam's download folder. The original mowas_2.exe instead copies the download into mods/<Name>/, where <Name> is the Name text from your mod.info. On the original game, changing Name after publishing changes the folder name on every subscriber's machine, and any mod or profile that lists yours will then point at a folder that is gone. In a mod list, a Workshop mod is named by its title, not by its item number.
  • On the original game, a local mod with the same Name as a subscribed one is overwritten on the next sync unless its stamp file is up to date. On the 64-bit build, a mods/ copy of a subscribed item is ignored and the log says it is an old copy, so a fix you make by hand in that copy never loads: rename it or unsubscribe.

The ARSENAL Workshop uploader

The Workshop step of the Share page ends with the "Workshop uploader" box. The uploader is workshop_gui.exe. It works with Assault Squad 2, the 64-bit build and Gates of Hell, and it must sit beside the game program: in the game folder, or in binaries\x64 for Gates of Hell.

  • The box says whether "the uploader is in the game folder", "not the copy ARSENAL has" or "not in the game folder yet". Type "Another game folder, for example Gates of Hell" to set it up for a game other than the one ARSENAL is set to.
  • "Put the uploader into the game folder" lists what it would do with three files, and "Copy these files now" does it (the confirm box). workshop_gui.exe is copied, or replaced when a different copy is there. steam_api64.dll is copied only when the folder has none, and steam_appid.txt is written only when the folder has none, with the Steam id of that game. A steam_api64.dll or steam_appid.txt that is already in the game folder is never overwritten, and no other game file is touched. This is the one time ARSENAL writes into a game folder.
  • "Open the Workshop uploader" starts it. Steam must be running and signed in. Choose your clean copy folder, fill in the title and the picture, and press Upload. On the first upload it writes the Workshop ID into mod.info, and it lists the items you already have.
  • "This copy of ARSENAL does not hold the uploader files (the workshop_gui folder is missing)" means the workshop_gui folder that comes with ARSENAL is not next to the program.

The same from the command line:

ARSENAL workshop status "G"
ARSENAL workshop install "G" --dry
ARSENAL workshop install "G"
ARSENAL workshop start "G"

status says whether the uploader is there and what install would do; --dry shows the plan without copying. A folder that holds none of as64.exe, mowas_2.exe or call_to_arms.exe is refused: "This is not a game folder of Assault Squad 2 or Gates of Hell". If a copy fails, close the uploader and the game and check that the folder is not read-only.

The clean copy

"Show what the clean copy holds" counts the files and lists what is left out; "Make clean copy" writes the mod folder into a folder you choose, which must be empty. Left out are the folders .git, .github, .vscode, .idea, node_modules and __MACOSX, the files UPGRADE.md, .gitignore, .gitattributes, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, files named notes, note or todo (with any ending), and files ending in .bak, .tmp, .orig or .log. Your mod itself is not changed.

The step warns when a Workshop ID exists and the Name in mod.info differs from the folder name or changed since you last saw it, and when the mod has UPGRADE.md (made from another mod: get the original author's permission first). The checklist above the box repeats the rules of this section: upload the clean copy, keep the FileId and Name lines, a PNG or JPG picture under 1 MB, run "Ready to share?" first, and never Gates of Hell content.

In Gates of Hell

  • The game ships its own uploader, call_to_arms_workshop.exe in binaries\x64. The ARSENAL uploader goes into the same folder; the steam_api64.dll that Gates of Hell already has there is left alone.
  • A Workshop item loads in place, from Steam's download folder. Its mod name is mod_<item number>, fixed by the item, so changing Name does not move anything. A Workshop item outside a workshop/content/ folder is skipped with A workshop mod outside of standard location!.
  • FileId in mod.info is read by local mods only. A local folder mods/mod_<item number> loses to the Workshop item of that number, and the log says Warning! Duplicate mod found.
  • Workshop tags are split on commas.
  • You can also upload your own replays to the Workshop from the replay list.
  • The log writes Workshop item <id> installed successfuly when an item arrives, and Steam is in OFFLINE mode. Some features are disabled without Steam.

9. Versioning, changelog and git

Keep a changelog file in your repository, but outside the folder you upload (or exclude it). For each release, note the version, the date, the units and systems you changed and whether the multiplayer data changed, because that tells players whether they must all update together. The Share page's "New version" step raises the version number (small fix, new things, big change), takes a change note and lists the files that changed.

Git works well for mods if you set it up for the game's text files:

  • Put the repository at the mod root, above resource/.
  • Track text sources: .def, .mdl, .mtl, .vol, .set, .inc, .ext, .lng, .txt, extension-less stuff files and .anm.
  • Ignore *.pak, large binaries (.ply, .dds, .tga, .wav), terrain data and logs.
  • Add a .gitattributes with * -text and set core.autocrlf to false, so CRLF line endings and old comment bytes stay byte-for-byte identical. Without this, git may convert line endings and damage a file.
  • Git does not hold your paks, so copy a pak aside before you overwrite it.

When a game update changes vanilla files you build on, two tools tell you what moved:

ARSENAL drift stamp "G/mods/mymod" --game "G"
ARSENAL drift check "G/mods/mymod" --game "G"
ARSENAL release-check --replan "G/mods/mymod"

drift stamp writes a release.json fingerprint of the vanilla files you override. After a game update, drift check shows which of them changed, so you know which of your overrides need a fresh look: your copy of a whole file hides every update the game makes to it. release-check (the Share page's "Game updated?" step) compares the game program with the last known build, and --replan shows what the changes hit in your mod.

10. Release checklist

  1. Edits finished, checked in game (chapter 18), game log read.
  2. build --strict passes, or "Check if ready" on the Share page shows no problems.
  3. Encoding verified: CRLF line endings, UTF-8 string values in data and .lng files, ASCII identifiers.
  4. doctor --release shows no stray or duplicate files.
  5. mod.info has a supported version range and a final Name.
  6. If multiplayer data changed, mpsync run, and a binary-only change paired with a text change.
  7. No Gates of Hell content (release-check --publish passes).
  8. Preview picture present, .git and notes excluded.
  9. Changelog written; git tag made.

In Gates of Hell

For a Gates of Hell mod, replace points 5 to 8 with these:

  1. mod.info versions on the 1.x scale, or no bounds at all.
  2. Mod folder name of plain letters, digits and _; paks in resource/, texts in localizations/.
  3. set/registry.reg and set/registry/dlc.reg not replaced.
  4. For multiplayer, the mod is on the Workshop, because players cannot get it any other way inside the game.

Gates of Hell: summary

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

SectionGates of HellIn short
1. Loose files or paksdiffersNo root resource.pak; loose files under 2 GB
2. How the game mounts a moddiffersOnly resource/, .pat and localizations/; strict folder names
3. Pak roles and namesdiffersSame zip-root rule; CRC warnings, damaged entries stop the game
4. Encoding checkdiffersTexts are .pot; mod .lng files only under localizations/
5. The pre-release gatediffersShare page packs the GoH layout; registry files must stay vanilla
6. Multiplayer compatibilitydiffersVersion and build must match; no checksum desync check by default
7. Versions and the minimum game versiondiffers1.x scale, optional bounds, Tags, Priority
8. Steam WorkshopdiffersItems named mod_<item number>; own uploader in binaries\x64
9. Versioning, changelog and gitnot mappedThe git advice holds for any game; game update checks not mapped
10. Release checklistdiffersFour points replace the Assault Squad 2 ones

Mod tags and priority

Gates of Hell reads two mod.info keys that Assault Squad 2 ignores: Tags (develop, no_delete) and Priority. Both are described in section 7. Assault Squad 2 skips them without a message, so a mod.info that carries them still loads there.

Replays on the Workshop

Gates of Hell can upload a replay you played yourself to the Workshop, as public, friends-only or private. The title is the replay's title and the picture is taken from the map preview. Assault Squad 2 has nothing like it.

Pitfalls

  • A forgotten loose copy can override a pak, so delete extracted copies before release.
  • A pak placed inside resource/ needs the top folder name in its entry paths.
  • A loose .patch file is never read; only one inside a numbered .pat is.
  • Same-size binary edits pass the lobby and desync during play.
  • Changing Name after publishing moves the folder name for subscribers on the original game.
  • A mod made from someone else's needs that author's permission; name the original mod and its author in the description, and publish it as a new Workshop item.
  • Editors that quietly re-encode text files undo all your care.
  • On Gates of Hell, a mod folder name with a - or a space never loads, and a root resource.pak is never read.

Next: Chapter 21, Troubleshooting.

21. Troubleshooting

Something is wrong: the mod is missing, nothing changed, the game closes on start, a match falls apart, or a page of the ARSENAL window refuses to do something. This chapter is organized by symptom. Find the one that matches, read the likely causes in order, and follow the checks. For how to read the log files in depth, see chapter 18.

The short way: Check, fix and read the log walks through the Read Game.log page of the window (Mods > Check & Fix > Read Game.log), which reads the log for you and explains each finding in plain words. The mod.info keys named here are listed in Reference 1, and the in-game console is described in Reference 12, reaching the console.

What you will learn

  • Where to look first for every kind of failure.
  • The most common causes for each symptom, with the exact log messages to search for.
  • What the ARSENAL pages mean when they refuse or find nothing.
  • Which warnings are harmless background noise.
  • How to bisect when nothing obvious shows up.
  • What to attach when you ask for help.

1. Where to look first

Two places answer most questions.

The game log. The game writes log/game.log in your user data folder (under your Documents, in a folder named after the game). It is overwritten each time you start the game, so copy it before you relaunch if it holds something you want to keep. The original mowas_2.exe simply truncates the old log; as64.exe keeps the previous one as game.prev.log. Crash dumps go in log/minidumps/, and multiplayer desync dumps in log/oos/.

Your profile's options.set. The list of active mods lives in its mods block, one line per mod, in the form "<mod folder name>:1". The folder name must match exactly, capitals included. On the original game this is the only reliable way to confirm which mods are active, because its log does not list the mods it loaded. as64.exe writes a Mod '<name>' from ... line for each mod it loads, so there the log answers the question too. A line that names a folder which is not installed is logged as Mod '<line>' was disabled: Not installed.

In the window, the Read Game.log page (Mods > Check & Fix, Assault Squad 2 and the 64-bit build) does both for you: "Explain my last game log" reads the newest log, "Show what is switched on" lists the active mods in their order, "Why is it missing?" explains why a mod or file does not load, and "Read this crash" reads a crash sidecar. If you run several game windows at once, "Read every game window" reads each one's log. "Pick another log folder..." points it at a different user data folder. The page is described in chapter 18. In the Quick Guided Task row, the explore task "what went wrong in the last run" reads the same log step by step (chapter 19).

On the command line, the same reading is:

ARSENAL logtriage "<user data folder>/log/game.log" --mod "<game folder>/mods/mymod" --game "<game folder>"

It groups repeated lines, labels harmless noise as information, and explains crashes and load errors in plain terms.

In Gates of Hell

  • The user data folder is Documents/My Games/Gates of Hell/. With -useLocalDataFolder on the command line, or when Documents lies in OneDrive, it is %LOCALAPPDATA%/Digitalmindsoft/Gates of Hell/ instead. The log line IO: Game config directory: names the one in use.
  • Every log line starts with the time since start, [hh:mm:ss] . Game events such as kills and flags are written as [EVT] lines.
  • The log lists the mods: Scanning mods in, Found N available mods, Mod: activate mod <name>, and each mounted pak as Mount package <file> with <n> entries.
  • A log grows to 250 MB, then goes on in a new numbered file. The multiplayer logs start over each mission, so copy them before the next one.
  • At most 5 crash dumps are kept in log/minidumps/ (dbg_minidumpFileLimit).
  • Under the GoH header button, the Read Game.log page and the explore task "what went wrong in the last run" read the log in the Gates of Hell user folder.

2. Symptom: the mod does not appear in the list

  1. The folder has no file named exactly mod.info. A folder without it is not a mod.
  2. The mod.info is unreadable. Unknown keys are skipped silently, so a misspelled key leaves you with a half-read file. Worse, a mod.info the game cannot parse at all (for example an unescaped quote inside the description) stops the game from starting. Check with ARSENAL modinfo "<game folder>/mods/mymod".
  3. The version range does not match. A legacy mod needs both MinGameVersion and MaxGameVersion; without them it is treated as unsupported. A mod written for the older 3.262 data is hidden in the Enhanced game mode, and a mod that asks for 3.301 or later is hidden in Classic mode. The vfs tool reports a mode mismatch. See chapter 3.
  4. A required mod is missing. Require entries must be installed and active.
  5. A different mod's mod.info is broken. One broken mod.info among your installed mods stops the whole game from launching, whether that mod is active or not. If the game exits instantly, look for a ***** Exception ***** block in game.log, and run modinfo over each folder in mods/.
  6. A Workshop copy on the 64-bit build. as64.exe loads subscribed Workshop items from Steam's download folder. A copy of the same item inside mods/ is ignored, and the log calls it an old copy. Rename your copy or unsubscribe.

In Gates of Hell

  1. The folder name is not allowed. A name with a space, a letter outside plain ASCII, or any of <>+()[]{}!@#$%^&*-=;:|'" is skipped, and only game.log says so: Warning: invalid mod folder name. Rename my-mod to my_mod.
  2. The mod.info is empty or broken. Only that mod is skipped (Warning: empty mod.info file found at, Warning: failed to load mod); the game still starts.
  3. The version is on the wrong scale. Gates of Hell versions are 1.x. A mod that asks for 3.301 is switched off with "Unsupported game version". Fix the bounds, leave them out, or add the tag develop while you work.
  4. A local copy of a Workshop item. A folder mods/mod_<item number> loses to the Workshop item of that number (Warning! Duplicate mod found). A Workshop item outside a workshop/content/ folder is skipped with A workshop mod outside of standard location!.

See chapter 20.

3. Symptom: listed, activated, but nothing changed

This is the most common failure, and it is nearly always a precedence problem.

  1. A loose file overrides your pak, or the other way round. A loose file in resource/ always beats the same path in the mod's root resource.pak. Against a pak that sits inside resource/, the folder scan order decides, and the later name wins, so a loose entity/ folder loses to entity.pak beside it. Run ARSENAL vfs "<game folder>" --mods mymod which set/stuff/gun/yourfile to see the winner, or use "Why is it missing?" on the Read Game.log page. See chapter 4.
  2. Another mod comes later in the load order and replaces the same file. A mod that replaces a file replaces it whole, with no merging. Run ARSENAL conflicts --game "<game folder>" --mods a,mymod.
  3. Your pak's folder paths are wrong. A pak in resource/ must contain entity/... or set/... as its top folders. A pak that leaves them out puts files one level off, and nothing happens. See chapter 20.
  4. A .patch file in the mod root. Only patches inside numbered N.pat archives are read. Numbering must have no gap.
  5. A misspelled key. Unknown keys are skipped silently. Run keylint, or "Check this unit" on the Read Game.log page. The keys themselves are listed in Part III of this guide.
  6. The mod folder was renamed. A line in the profile that names a missing folder is dropped when the game starts. Re-activate the mod under Options, MODS.
  7. You did not press Apply, or the mod is still applying. Applying takes about half a minute, and a very large mod can take minutes.
  8. A built-in or macro setting wins. For example, if an armor macro sets a nonzero value for a side, it overrides your per-volume value. See chapter 9.

A quick sanity check is the Repository: N resources line in game.log: the number changes when files are added or removed, so it tells you quickly whether your pak was seen.

In Gates of Hell

  • The pak sits in the mod root. A root resource.pak and localization.pak, and a localization/ folder, are never read. Put the pak into resource/ and the texts into localizations/<code>/.
  • Mod order. Mods that do not depend on each other are ordered by Priority in mod.info (1 when missing); a higher number applies later and wins.
  • A language file wins. A file under localizations/<code>/ is laid over resource/ and probably beats the same path in any mod (not confirmed in game).
  • To see whether your pak was mounted, look for Mount package <file> with <n> entries in game.log.

See chapter 20.

4. Symptom: the game closes while loading

Open game.log, search for ***** Exception *****, and read the message directly above the stack.

MessageLikely cause and fix
define not foundA macro call ("name" ...) with no visible (define "name" ...). Defines are visible only within the chain of includes of the top-level file. Add the define, include its file, or fix the name.
unexpected tokenThe parser expected something else. Common: a bone, volume or place name that no longer exists after a model swap, a missing or extra bracket, a number where a string belongs. The log names the file and line; compare the block with a working sibling file.
String expected, Identifier expected, Block terminator expected, Block start expectedMalformed text data. Check the file and line shown.
Nested mods not supportedA (mod ...) block inside another (mod ...) block.
pattern not foundA {from "pattern X"} base that is not defined. Define it or fix the name.
Unknown materialA material that is not in the game's material set.
Bone modifiers must be placed after skeleton loadA {bone ...} block appears before the model or skeleton line. Move it below.
Extender not found, next state not foundA reference to something the entity does not define.
Resource not found, File is not found, Resource file ... read errorA mesh, volume, animation or material named in the definition does not exist. Check the exact name and its capitalization.
Invalid block in .VOL file, Unsupported animation version, At least one frame required, Zero speed in ik-boneCorrupt or wrong-format model data, or a bone with speed 0.

Other causes without a precise message: a UTF-16 byte-order mark in a text data file, which is fatal; more than 128 distinct {set} flag names in the scripts, which stops loading; and a modern-format mod listed in a legacy game mode, which can crash on start (the font loader is where it shows up). Check the encoding rules: text files use CRLF line endings, string values are UTF-8 in data and .lng files alike, and identifiers are ASCII. A string saved as cp1251 loads without error but shows as boxes.

If the log shows no Exception block at all but the game vanishes, look in log/minidumps/ for a new .mdmp.log file. Read it before anything else: it contains the log at the moment of the crash and the exception block.

In Gates of Hell

MessageLikely cause and fix
Resource Error at startThe mod replaces set/registry.reg or set/registry/dlc.reg. Leave both files alone.
Failed to read file from pak <name>, Verify integrity of game files via steamA damaged entry in that pak. Repack it, or verify the game files in Steam if it is a game pak.
empty ammo identifierA magazine names ammo with an empty id.
invalid positionA loose file of 2 GB or more. Put it in a pak.
path is too longA file name with letters outside plain ASCII longer than 1023 bytes.
Failed to mount localizationThe base game has no localizations/ folder: verify the game files.

Out of memory gives an Error box and no crash dump. A DirectX error closes the game at once, with no box and no dump; if the game vanishes without a dump, suspect the graphics side first.

5. Symptom: the game crashes only when something happens

A crash that appears when you buy a unit, fire a weapon or reload is usually a missing reference that the game substituted at load time and tripped over later.

  • No Stuff found for tags 'X' (the log says "may lead to crash"). A weapon, ammo or inventory entry names a tag that matches nothing. The game substitutes a dummy and keeps loading; it crashes when the item is used, for example when a gun first reloads. Ammo tags have the form <caliber> <type>, and a wrong form is a typical mistake. This is the one warning that most often turns into a crash.
  • A model whose mesh has no material crashes when you place the unit.
  • A soldier with incomplete breed or vision data crashes when the game updates what he sees; buy squads one at a time to find the bad one.
  • A towed gun reloading with missing ammo crashes on the reload; look for ammo name mismatches on towed guns and howitzer shells.

Read the .mdmp.log next to the dump, or press "Read this crash" on the Read Game.log page. A very small address such as 0x28 or 0x54 means "something it expected to exist does not". The crash text names the part of the game that failed, and that tells you where to look: weapons and ammo, a soldier's senses, wheels and tracks, armour and damage, or reading a data file. The lines directly above the exception are the last warnings before the crash, and they usually name the culprit.

In Gates of Hell

  • A weapon whose fire bone is missing does not crash: the log warns Can't find fxBone in weapon ... held by ....
  • Crash reports go to the game maker's crash service, but none is sent while any mod is applied. The local crash dump in log/minidumps/ is still written, and at most 5 are kept.

6. Symptom: text is missing or shows as a key

  • A name or description shows as a raw key or blank: the key is missing from your .lng file, or your .lng replaced a vanilla file and dropped keys. A .lng in a mod's localization/ folder replaces the vanilla file with the same name wholesale; there is no merging. Use loccover to find missing and dropped keys.
  • Garbled characters: the .lng file was saved in the wrong encoding. It must be UTF-8.
  • Localization key redefinition in the log is normal and appears hundreds of times. A duplicate inside your own file is worth cleaning (the later one wins).

See chapter 14.

In Gates of Hell

  • The game's own texts are .pot files. A mod's localization/ folder is not read, so its .lng files show raw keys. Move them to localizations/<code>/interface/text/.
  • A mod of another localization kind than the game logs Localization mode ... does not match and still loads.
  • The session list takes the reason a game cannot be joined from the keys mp/session_restriction/version, closed, performance, veterancy and player_limit, so a translation needs them too.

See chapter 14.

7. Symptom: models appear untextured or invisible

  • A texture named by a .mtl file is missing or is in the wrong folder.
  • A cloned mesh has no .mtl beside its .ply (a crash at mesh load).
  • Using bump material on non-bump geometry means the mesh has no tangents but the material asks for bump mapping. Remove the bump or re-export the mesh.
  • Automatic MIP generation not supported and No MIP levels are quality and performance warnings, not blockers; re-save new textures with mipmaps.
  • A texture in a different format with the same base name can shadow the one you meant. binhdr reports texture extension shadowing.
  • Models copied from Gates of Hell can have headers the Assault Squad 2 engine rejects. Run ARSENAL binhdr "<game folder>" --mods mymod --summary. Gates of Hell content can never be shared, only used for your own play.

See chapter 16.

8. Symptom: units that cannot move, cannot be selected or do not fire

These have many causes, and several are not confirmed, so treat the list as places to look.

  • Bones. Bone X not found and Can't find bone X mean a modifier is ignored or shots spawn at the origin. After a model swap, names such as the turret or machine-gun bones are the usual victims. Wheeled vehicles need front and back pivot bones; without them the log says no "pivot_back" bones and the wheel offsets fall back to defaults.
  • Locomotion data. Run movlint (see chapter 7).
  • Sensors and vision. A soldier who never reacts can have broken sensor values (see chapter 10).
  • A unit that cannot be selected (unconfirmed): compare its definition against a working unit of the same class and check that it sits in the right entity folder. Copy a vanilla unit in unchanged first, then change one thing at a time.
  • Sound missing: unknown sound file 'folder/name' means the name does not match a folder or file in the sound data. There are no aliases.

9. Symptom: armor and damage surprises

  • Armor does nothing after you edit a volume: a nonzero macro value for that side overrides the per-volume value. Edit the macro arguments.
  • A penetration table is ignored: the table must sit in a block whose tags match the ammo tags exactly; a table for one ammo type is not used by a related type.
  • unknown volume thickness: the thickness trace found nothing, and the game uses the volume's own thickness. If it repeats for one unit, check its volume file.
  • Incorrect thickness for volume means a volume that should accept hits has zero thickness on a side.
  • A {set ...} with an ability level that does not exist (invalid level param) makes the soldier a top-level ability, silently. This is a silent buff.

The Armor page under Models shows the armour of a vehicle as the game reads it, with your mod laid over the game, and which shells go through at which range. See chapter 9 and chapter 8.

10. Symptom: multiplayer desync and lobby mismatch

  • The lobby shows a data mismatch or refuses the join. The two players' data trees differ. The host denies a join unless the data and map checks match, or unless the host allows desync.
  • The lobby is happy, then the match drops into "out of sync". Most often the players have different mod or pak contents. Model, volume, material, animation and script files are compared only by size, so a same-size edit passes the lobby and diverges later. Compare the Repository: N resources number in each player's log, or let each player export a fingerprint with ARSENAL mpsync --game "<game folder>" --mods a,b --export fp.json and compare the two files with ARSENAL mpsync --compare a.json b.json.
  • Other causes: a different mod load order; different game versions or 32-bit against 64-bit; and scripts that read per-machine state such as keys, graphics or the profile.
  • A crash on one machine often shows up as an out-of-sync on the others. Check for a crash first.

Look in log/oos/. A tiny file holds only checksums. A large one is a full snapshot you can text-compare between host and client: the first differing line is the diverged entity. If both checksums differ in the first check and the files are tiny, suspect mismatched mod content. See chapter 12 and, for what the lobby compares, chapter 20.

In Gates of Hell

  • A game is not listed or cannot be joined. Only hosts with the same game version and the same build (x64) are listed; a game can also be closed, full, or outside your performance or veterancy range.
  • No out-of-sync message, but the match plays differently on each PC. By default Gates of Hell does not compare checksums of the game state (mp_syncLevel 0), so differing mod files probably do not stop the match. Check that every player has the same mods from the Workshop.
  • A player lags. The host waits up to 1000 ms for a lagging client (mp_maxClientlag), where Assault Squad 2 waits 750 ms.
  • An out-of-sync dump that would unpack to more than 64 MB is refused: OOS dump rejected: implausible unpacked size.
  • Gates of Hell never plays with Assault Squad 2 or its 64-bit build.

See chapter 20.

11. Symptom: Classic and Enhanced mode problems

  • A mod silently does nothing in one mode: its version declaration puts it in the other mode. Modern mods declare a minimum of 3.301 or higher; legacy ones declare 3.262. Check modinfo and vfs.
  • A modern mod beside legacy content can crash on start.
  • A mod needing the built-in extras does not load in Classic.

Chapter 3 explains how to make a mod work in both.

12. Symptom: poor performance

(Unconfirmed in detail; these are things to try.) Very large mods mount slowly. Textures without mipmaps and bump materials on meshes that cannot use them cost time. Thousands of loose files mount more slowly than a few paks. Pack the mod and re-save textures with mipmaps.

In Gates of Hell

A pak written without CRCs makes the game write no crc for file in package ... performance may be slowed for every entry. Repack it with a tool that stores real CRCs. Text entries of paks are kept in memory after their first read, and model entries are read from the pak each time they are opened.

13. Symptom: an ARSENAL page refuses or finds nothing

These are the messages of the window, with what they mean and what to do.

Copying a model into your mod (Models page).

  • "Pick your mod folder first." The page copies into the mod you picked at the top of the page. Pick it, then press "Copy into my mod" again.
  • "No files were found for this model." The model's name was found, but none of its files are in the game data the page can see. Check the name, and check that the game folder at the top of the window is right.
  • The copy is refused because the target is inside the game. ARSENAL never writes into the game's own data, Steam's Workshop downloads or the Steam library folders. It writes only into a mod folder under mods/. Pick a folder there, or make a new mod with the New mod card on the Mods page.

SOEdit is not found (Models page).

  • "SOEdit was not found on this computer. The button below downloads and installs it, then opens it." Press "Get SOEdit and open it". ARSENAL downloads the latest SOEdit release from GitHub (ThatFrostyy/SOEdit-PatchByFrostyy), checks its size and, when GitHub lists one, its checksum, unpacks it into %LOCALAPPDATA%\ARSENAL\soedit and starts it: "SOEdit was downloaded, installed and started."
  • ARSENAL looks for SOEdit in this order: the path in the environment setting ARSENAL_SOEDIT, the soedit folder next to ARSENAL.exe, the copy it downloaded, the copy of an installed ARSENAL, then a few folders of your own (PATH, Desktop, Downloads, Documents). SOEdit is not part of the ARSENAL download; it comes through this button or ARSENAL soedit install. ARSENAL soedit locate prints what it found.
  • "The latest release could not be read from GitHub." Check the network and try again, or set ARSENAL_SOEDIT to the path of a SOEdit.exe you already have.
  • "There is no SOEdit download for this copy of ARSENAL yet." Set ARSENAL_SOEDIT to the path of a SOEdit.exe you already have.

See chapter 19.

The armour table is empty (Models page, Armor).

  • "Pick a vehicle at the top of the page first (type its name in the search)." The simulator works on one vehicle at a time.
  • "The armour of this model was not found. Pick a vehicle by its name at the top of the page." You picked a model file rather than a vehicle, or a name that has no vehicle definition. Search by the vehicle's name.
  • "This model has no armoured parts that the simulator can read." The vehicle exists, but none of its volumes carry armour the simulator understands, for example an unarmoured truck or a vehicle whose armour comes only from a macro it cannot follow. ARSENAL armorsim table shows the same table on the command line.
  • "Pick your mod folder at the top of the page first." Armour is read with your mod laid over the game, and changes are written only into your mod.

The guide index is missing (Guides & External Tools page).

  • "The guide index was not found." The Guides & External Tools page reads a folder that holds guides.json and a builtin folder. It looks for it in the folder given with --data, then the folder in the environment setting GEM_INDEX_DIR, then the gemindex folder next to ARSENAL.exe. If your copy of ARSENAL came with a gemindex folder, keep it next to the program. Otherwise press "Pick the index folder" and choose the folder of the GEM External Index toolkit; the choice lasts until ARSENAL closes. The "What ARSENAL can and can't make" tab works without the index.

The Quick Guided Task shows a task grey or switches the game. See Quick Guided Task and Use the Quick Guided Task.

  • A grey task names its reason: "not built yet", "not for" and the game, "needs a mod picked" (pick one on the Mods page), "needs the game folder" (set it at the top of the window), or "only on the PC, not from another device" (tasks run only on the PC, not over LAN Remote).
  • "Tasks could not be loaded: ..." The list of tasks did not load. Restart the window; if it stays, attach the message when you ask for help.
  • Under Gates of Hell, a button that leads to a page Gates of Hell does not have, such as "Go to the Play page" or "Share the mod", switches the header to the other game: "That page belongs to ...: switched to ...". Switch back with the game picker in the header.
  • "Throw away" deletes a saved task with its answers and the files you brought. Files the task already wrote into your mod stay; undo them with the Editor's restore points.

The Docs page finds nothing (Help & Docs > Docs). See Whole documents.

  • "No documentation found". The documents are not inside the program file. Keep the guide folder that came with the program next to it, or a folder named docs, then press "Look again".
  • "... is not made yet." A whole document (Doctrine atlas, Modding guide, Engine document) is not there. With Advanced on, the line names the command that makes it.
  • "That document is not here any more. Pick another on the left." The file was moved or deleted while the page was open.
  • "The PDF could not be opened." The PDF is in the folder guide, then dist, next to the program (the engine document: techdoc, then dist).
  • The search box finds nothing inside an open whole document: it searches the chapters. Click into the document and use Ctrl+F.

A file viewer refuses (Editor and dialogs). See File viewers.

  • "Pick a mod first: the file is looked up in it."
  • "No viewer for ... is installed." The file kind has no viewer in this copy of ARSENAL.
  • "The viewer could not open the file: ..." The file is damaged or not what its name says. The message names the reason.
  • "The game does not read .zip files, so their entries cannot be opened here." Use a .pak.
  • "That name opens another copy (a loose file or another pak comes first), so this entry cannot be opened by name." The entry is hidden by a copy that wins; see section 3.
  • A sound note says an .ogg, .mp3 or .flac file was renamed to .wav: the game stays silent. Convert it to a real .wav.
  • A picture note says "DX10 header: the game cannot load it". Save it as DXT1, DXT5 or 32-bit A8R8G8B8.
  • "This browser cannot play sound (no Web Audio)." Open the window in another browser.

LAN Remote and the phone view. See LAN Remote and the phone view.

  • "No network address found. Is this PC connected to a network?" Connect the PC to your home network and switch LAN Remote on again.
  • "Could not listen on: ..." LAN Remote could not start; the message names why. The first time, Windows may ask whether node may use the network; answer it yourself.
  • "This link no longer works" on the other device: someone pressed "New link" on the PC. Scan the new code.
  • A wrong key 20 times locks that address out for 10 minutes. Wait, then open the current link.
  • Running tools, saving and starting are refused on the other device: "View only. Changes are made on the PC." Make the change on the PC. Files outside the game and mod folders are refused.

Arrange mode. See Arrange mode.

  • The page's buttons do nothing: Arrange is on. Press Esc or Done.
  • A part of a page is gone: it was hidden. Start Arrange (on Tools & Settings > Settings, or Ctrl+K "Arrange This Page") and use "Show" with its name, or "Reset this page" in the fold "Profiles, import and reset".
  • "This file is not an ARSENAL layout profile." Import only a file made with Export.
  • Window settings are kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ARSENAL\settings.json. A damaged file is set aside as settings.json.bad-<time> and the settings start empty.

The confirm box. Every step that writes or starts a program asks first, with "Do it" (or the step's name) and "Cancel". Nothing is written before you confirm, so a cancelled step changed nothing. On a risky step the focus starts on Cancel, so Enter alone does nothing. See The confirm box.

The Workshop uploader and the clean copy (Share page). See The ARSENAL Workshop uploader.

  • "This copy of ARSENAL does not hold the uploader files (the workshop_gui folder is missing)." Use the full ARSENAL download and keep its workshop_gui folder next to the program.
  • The box says "the uploader in the game folder is not the copy ARSENAL has": put it there again, and workshop_gui.exe is replaced.
  • "This is not a game folder of Assault Squad 2 or Gates of Hell": the folder you typed holds none of as64.exe, mowas_2.exe or call_to_arms.exe.
  • A copy fails: close the uploader and the game, and check that the folder is not read-only.
  • The uploader opens but cannot upload: Steam must be running and signed in.
  • "the folder ... already has files in it. Pick an empty place, or remove it yourself first." The clean copy goes only into an empty folder.
  • "Not this folder: ... is inside the game folder" or "inside a Steam folder": the package goes to a folder of your own, for example the Desktop.
  • "this mod holds Gates of Hell content (GOH-ORIGIN.tsv)": such a mod is never packed or uploaded. See chapter 20.

A page is missing, or says "Not available". Every game shows the same nine tabs and pages; under Gates of Hell the Units sub-tab adds the GoH unit page. A part of a page that cannot work for the game you picked shows "Not available in" and the game, with the reason, in place of its buttons. Some items, such as Mod Files and Expert Tools, show only with Advanced on: turn it on at Tools & Settings > Settings. See the pages of the window.

Other refusals. Any page that writes refuses a target inside the game install other than mods/<name>, and anything under Steam's Workshop content. A refusal never changes a file. Pick a mod folder of your own and try again. The one exception is the Workshop uploader: after a confirm, the Share page copies its three files into the game folder.

In Gates of Hell

  • "No Gates of Hell install was found on this PC, so this page is off." The GoH unit page needs a Gates of Hell install. Install the game through Steam, or check that ARSENAL finds it.
  • "No Assault Squad 2 folder is set. Choose it on the Mods page first." A unit from Gates of Hell is written into an Assault Squad 2 mod, so that game folder must be set too.
  • The task "a mod with problems (fix them)" only looks under Gates of Hell; it writes nothing. The Check page's fix steps write a Gates of Hell patch mod but leave out the fixes that follow Assault Squad 2 rules, each with a line saying why.
  • "Not available in GoH" on a part of a page is expected, not a fault: for example the Armor part of Models, the bot shopping list, Bot Doctrine, Map Scripts for AI, the price calculator and the test runs. The reason is on the same line.
  • A mod in the Gates of Hell mods folder that ARSENAL did not make is written only with Advanced on; a mod ARSENAL made there, or a new one, is written without it.
  • The Share page under GoH puts the Workshop uploader into binaries\x64; the steam_api64.dll already there is never overwritten.

See chapter 19.

14. Benign messages

Do not chase these. They appear in vanilla and in most modded installs:

  • Localization key redefinition (hundreds of lines)
  • Mission ... is skipped for leftover mission titles
  • Entity redefinition for helmets, bushes, wire, wrecks and shells
  • Automatic MIP generation not supported, No MIP levels
  • No obstacle ID, unknown terrain_pp type, use_blend_tex
  • Media file ... story not found
  • Unknown control panel item for trench items
  • Invalid ricochet angle (cosmetic; the game clamps it)

The rule: a warning line names a file, not a mod, so judge a warning by the file path in parentheses. Compare a log from before your change against one after; new message types or higher counts of No Stuff found, Unknown props, Unread data, Can't preload or invalid level param are yours. The Read Game.log page marks the harmless ones as notes.

In Gates of Hell

  • Unknown props is no longer written, so do not count it.
  • no crc for file in package ... performance may be slowed appears once per entry of a pak written without CRCs: harmless for loading, but repack your own paks.
  • [EVT] lines are game events (kills, flags, zones), not errors.
  • Localization mode ... does not match for a mod of another localization kind: the mod still loads.
  • Every line starts with [hh:mm:ss] ; strip it before you compare two logs.

15. A decision tree

  1. Does the game start? If no, read the top of game.log and look for an Exception block (section 4, then section 2).
  2. Is your mod active? Check options.set, or "Show what is switched on" (section 1 and section 2).
  3. Did the log show a fatal message? Fix it (section 4).
  4. Does the log show a new warning with your file path? Fix it.
  5. Does the change have no effect? Walk section 3.
  6. Does it crash in play? Section 5 and the crash sidecar.
  7. Multiplayer only? Section 10.
  8. Does an ARSENAL page refuse? Section 13.
  9. Still nothing? Bisect: revert your last edit (git for text, a backup for paks), relaunch, and check one unit at a time in a LAN match.

16. What to attach when you ask for help

  • game.log from the failing run, copied before relaunching.
  • The .mdmp.log sidecar if there was a crash (not the large dump).
  • The mod's mod.info and the contents of the mods block in options.set.
  • The output of ARSENAL doctor "<game folder>/mods/mymod" --game "<game folder>".
  • The game executable and version (mowas_2.exe or as64.exe), and whether you are in Classic or Enhanced mode.
  • For multiplayer: both players' logs and the log/oos/ folder.
  • One sentence on what you changed last.

In the window, Help & Docs > Start Here has a "Get help" box: "Make diagnostics text" lists the game folder, the game program, your mods and the end of the newest game.log, with your user name replaced by %USERPROFILE%. "Copy" puts it on the clipboard to paste into your message.

Do not delete logs until you have written down the finding.

In Gates of Hell

  • The logs are in the Gates of Hell user data folder (section 1), which may be under %LOCALAPPDATA% instead of Documents.
  • Copy the multiplayer logs right after the mission: the next mission starts them over.
  • Give the game version (1.067 and its patch number) and the mod list with each mod's Priority.
  • Say which game the problem is in. A Gates of Hell finding may not hold for Assault Squad 2, and the other way round.

Gates of Hell: summary

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

SectionGates of HellIn short
1. Where to look firstdiffersOwn user data folder, time-stamped lines, mods and paks listed in the log
2. The mod does not appear in the listdiffersStrict folder names, 1.x versions, a broken mod.info skips only that mod
3. Listed, activated, but nothing changeddiffersRoot paks and localization/ unread; Priority orders mods
4. The game closes while loadingdiffersNew fatal messages: Resource Error, damaged pak entry, empty ammo identifier
5. Crashes only when something happensdiffersMissing fire bone warns instead of crashing
6. Text is missing or shows as a keydiffers.pot texts; mod .lng only under localizations/
7. Models untextured or invisiblenot mapped
8. Units that cannot move, be selected or firenot mapped
9. Armor and damage surprisesnot mapped hereSee chapter 9
10. Multiplayer desync and lobby mismatchdiffersSame version and build; no checksum desync check by default
11. Classic and Enhanced mode problemsnot mappedGates of Hell versions are on the 1.x scale (section 2)
12. Poor performancediffersPaks without CRCs flood the log
13. An ARSENAL page refuses or finds nothingdiffersSome parts "Not available" under GoH; GoH unit needs both games
14. Benign messagesdiffersUnknown props gone; no crc and [EVT] lines
15. A decision treesame as far as mappedUse the Gates of Hell notes of each section
16. What to attachdiffersOther log folder; copy multiplayer logs per mission

Crash reports in Gates of Hell

Gates of Hell sends crash and out-of-sync reports to its maker's crash service, but not while any mod is applied, so a modded crash leaves only the local dump in log/minidumps/. A BugSplat.ini file read at start with Enabled=0 stops the uploads; the game ships none. Out of memory shows an Error box and writes no dump; a DirectX error closes the game at once with no box and no dump.

Pitfalls

  • Removing the log before you read it. The next launch overwrites it.
  • Fixing three things at once, so you never learn which one mattered.
  • Assuming a clean linter run means the game will accept the mod.
  • Reading a Gates of Hell log with Assault Squad 2 rules: the folder, the line stamps and several fatal messages differ.

Next: Chapter 22, Glossary.

22. Glossary

This chapter explains the terms used throughout the guide, in alphabetical order, including the words the step-by-step pages of Part I and the reference entries of Part III use. Each entry points to the chapter where the idea is covered in detail and, where it helps, to the Part I page or Part III entry. For the keys of mod.info and the mod folder, see Reference 1; for bot scripts and the console, see Reference 12.

A

  • Ability: a named skill level for a soldier, such as a weapon skill, set with a level number. A level number outside the allowed range silently counts as the top level. Chapter 8.
  • Advanced: the switch "Show the Advanced options" on Tools & Settings > Settings of the ARSENAL window; Ctrl+K has it too. It asks before it turns on. It adds items and options inside the tabs, never a tab: under AS64 Project Notes, Mod Files, Test Run and Expert Tools, plus the folds marked Advanced inside pages. While it is on, the header shows a small "Advanced on" chip. Chapter 19.
  • Ammo type: a data entry for a round, with a tag (caliber plus type) that weapons and penetration tables match against. Chapter 9.
  • Apply: the button in the Options mods screen that makes the game re-read the active mods. Chapter 3.
  • ARSENAL: the modding toolkit this guide uses. ARSENAL.exe runs every tool from one command (ARSENAL <tool> ...) and needs nothing else installed; ARSENAL help lists the tools. Without the exe, the same command runs as node tools/as2/as2.js <tool> from the ARSENAL folder (older name: as2). Chapter 19.
  • ARSENAL-gui: the same tools in a window. Double-click ARSENAL.exe or ARSENAL-gui.cmd and its pages open in your browser; each page names the game it serves. Chapter 19.
  • Armour simulator: the Armor tab of the Models page (Models & Sim), and the armorsim command. It shows a vehicle's armour as the game reads it, with your mod laid over the game, and which shells go through at which range. Chapters 9 and 19, and Change armour.
  • Arrange mode: the mode of the ARSENAL window in which you move, hide and show the blocks of a page. Start it on Tools & Settings > Settings ("Arrange the page") or with Ctrl+K "Arrange This Page"; a bar on the page shows "Arranging:" and Done. The layout is kept in a profile. Chapter 19.
  • as64.exe: the 64-bit game program. It adds the console (-console), several game windows on one computer (-instance N) and the control pipe (-control) that testrun uses, and it keeps the previous log as game.prev.log. Chapter 18.
  • as64+: the built-in extension package of the 64-bit build. With it in the active list the game runs in Enhanced mode; without it, in Classic mode. It always loads before every player mod. Chapter 3 and Reference 1.
  • Assault Squad 2 (AS2): the game this guide covers. Chapter 1.

B

  • BOOT OK: what play and the Play page report when the mod loaded and a test match started. It does not mean the mod plays right. Chapter 18.
  • Behind the armour: the panel under the shot test of the Models page that follows a shot past the plates and says what it does to the parts, the crew and the vehicle as a whole. Chapter 9.
  • binaries/x64: the folder of a Gates of Hell install that holds the game program call_to_arms.exe, its own Workshop uploader and steam_api64.dll. The ARSENAL Workshop uploader goes there. Chapter 20.
  • Bisect: finding a fault by turning half of your changes off, then half of what is left, until one change remains. Chapters 18 and 21.
  • Block: one part of a page of the ARSENAL window, which Arrange mode can move, hide or show again. Chapter 19.
  • Bone: a named point or joint in a model's skeleton, used for turrets, muzzles and wheels. A missing bone is a common error after swapping a model. Chapter 16.
  • Bot: the computer player in multiplayer, driven by data and a Lua script. Chapter 10.
  • Bot Doctrine: the page of the ARSENAL window (Game Modes & AI > Bots > Bot Doctrine, 64-bit build) that turns short rules of how small units fought, and characters that follow them, into bot settings in your mod. Not the same as a Gates of Hell doctrine. Bots and chapter 10.
  • Branch task: a task of the Quick Guided Task started from inside another one, for example a new gun inside a vehicle. When it ends you go back to the first task. Chapter 19 and Use the Quick Guided Task.
  • Breed: a data set describing the body and senses of a soldier type. Chapters 6 and 8.
  • Build (tool): the tool that runs all checks and writes paks. Chapter 20.
  • Buy panel: the in-game panel where a player buys units in multiplayer. Each button comes from a unit card in the multiplayer unit lists. Chapter 15 and Change unit numbers.

C

  • Cache: the saved index that tools such as entityindex keep so that they start fast. Chapter 19.
  • call_to_arms.exe: the Gates of Hell game program, in binaries/x64. ARSENAL knows a Gates of Hell folder by it. Chapter 20.
  • check: the front-door tool: give it a mod folder from anywhere and it prints findings plus a verdict for each game build, without running the game. Chapter 19.
  • Card id (unit card, price card): the name of a unit's entry in the multiplayer unit lists, which holds its price, rank needed and unlock time. The buy panel icon is named after it. Squad cards carry the army in brackets. Add a unit.
  • Chassis: the part of vehicle data that defines wheels, tracks and movement. Chapter 7.
  • Classic mode: the game mode that loads mods written for the older data version (3.262). Chapter 3.
  • Clean copy: the copy of your mod folder that the Share page makes for the Workshop uploader, without .git, notes, backups, UPGRADE.md and other leftovers. Chapter 20.
  • Console: the in-game command line of the 64-bit build. It needs the -console start option; open it with the key left of 1. Reference 12.
  • Control pipe: a channel the 64-bit build opens when started with -control, through which a tool sends console commands. testrun uses it. Chapter 18.
  • Confirm box: the one box that every step of the ARSENAL window which writes files or starts a program opens first: what will happen, where, "Do it" and "Cancel". Chapter 19.
  • Conflict: two mods replacing the same file, so only one wins. Chapters 4 and 19.
  • Conquest: a campaign mode only Gates of Hell has, with battles fought over a map of points. It reads fixed files under set/dynamic_campaign (such as values.set and map_points.set), and bot scripts see it through BotApi.Conquest (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 12.
  • cp1251: the old Windows Cyrillic text encoding. In vanilla data it survives only inside ; comments, which the game skips; leave those bytes alone. The 64-bit build reads string values as UTF-8, so a string saved as cp1251 shows as boxes. Chapters 5, 14 and 20.
  • CRC: a checksum. The multiplayer lobby compares checksums of text-like data files and only the sizes of binary ones. Chapters 12 and 20.
  • CRLF: the two-character line ending (carriage return, line feed) used by the game's text files. Chapter 5.
  • Crash dump (minidump): a file the game writes when it crashes, with a text sidecar ending in .mdmp.log. Chapter 18.

D

  • DDA: the older name for the block-and-key text syntax that SDL grew from. Chapter 5.
  • Dedicated server: a game program that runs a multiplayer match with no player at it. Gates of Hell ships one, call_to_arms_server.exe in binaries/x64; its sound is off by default (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 12.
  • def (.def): an entity definition file. Chapter 6.
  • define: a named macro in SDL. Calling an undefined one is fatal. Chapters 5 and 21.
  • Desync: the state where players' games disagree about what happened. See OOS. Chapters 12 and 21.
  • develop (tag): a word in the Tags line of a Gates of Hell mod.info that lifts the version check for that mod, handy while you work on it (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • Direct control: steering one soldier or vehicle by hand. Gates of Hell adds a third-person view to it, switched with the key manual_mode_toggle; the host can allow direct view only, third person only, or either (manualControlMode 1, 2 or 3) (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 7.
  • Docs page: the sub-tab of Help & Docs that reads and searches this guide and the other documents inside the window, chapter by chapter or as one book. Chapter 19.
  • Doctor: the tool that runs all the linters on a mod and, with --release, checks the folder before you ship it. Chapters 19 and 20.
  • Doctrine (Gates of Hell): a choice each player makes in a Gates of Hell lobby for his army; it filters which units he can buy. ARSENAL's Bot Doctrine page is a different thing (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 12.
  • Donor: a working Assault Squad 2 unit of the same kind that a unit ported from Gates of Hell is built on. The donor brings crew places, weapon slots and armour layout. donorpick suggests one. Unit from Gates of Hell.

E

  • Enhanced mode: the game mode for mods that require version 3.301 or newer. Chapter 3.
  • Entity: any game object defined by data: unit, vehicle, building or item. Chapter 6.
  • entityindex: the tool that indexes every entity and what it refers to. Chapter 19.
  • Event: something that happens and that an interaction script can react to. Chapter 11.
  • Expert Tools: the item under Tools & Settings > Other Tools, shown with Advanced on, that lists every ARSENAL tool with its command line, and shows diffs, stat sheets and conflicts. Chapter 19.
  • ext (.ext): a shared template file that entities build on. Chapter 6.
  • Extender: a block in an entity that adds a capability, such as inventory, vitality or a cannon. Chapter 6.

F

  • Fatal error: a load error that closes the game, such as define not found. Chapters 18 and 21.
  • File viewer: the read-only view that a file which is not plain text opens in: sounds, pictures, video, fonts, shaders, archives and bytes. Chapter 19.
  • Flag: a named on/off value in scripts, set with {set}. More than 128 distinct flag names is a load error. Chapters 11 and 12.
  • FX: a visual effect such as smoke, fire or a muzzle flash. Chapter 16.

G

  • gen: the tool that writes a small mod from a spec file, or with --describe from a unit described in plain words; --plan only previews. What it writes is a start: play it before you trust it. Chapter 19.
  • Game card: the data entry that lists a multiplayer game mode in the lobby. Chapter 12.
  • Game folder: where the game is installed. Treat it as read-only. Chapter 2.
  • game.log: the text log the game writes at log/game.log. Chapter 18.
  • Gates of Hell (GoH): a related game on a newer version of the engine. Its data can be ported with care, for your own play only; its content can never be shared. The chapters of Part II say, section by section, where Gates of Hell differs. Chapter 19, Unit from Gates of Hell and the summary below.
  • GEM index: an index of other modders' guides and tools, read by the Guides & External Tools page and the gemindex command. Chapter 19 and Find guides and tools.
  • GOH-ORIGIN.tsv: the list a mod keeps of its files that came from Gates of Hell. The Share page and release-check --publish refuse to pack, copy or publish a mod that has one. Chapters 19 and 20.
  • GoH unit page: the page that brings a Gates of Hell vehicle into an Assault Squad 2 mod, built on a donor. Under GoH it sits in the Units sub-tab of Units & Balance; its step 3 has the fold Translate numbers. Chapter 19 and Unit from Gates of Hell.

H

  • Host: the player who creates a multiplayer match and whose settings the lobby checks. Chapter 12.
  • Human: the entity class for soldiers. Chapter 8.

I

  • inc (.inc): an include file of shared data. Chapter 5.
  • include: the SDL command that pastes another file in. Chapter 5.
  • Instance: one of several game windows on one computer. Start the 64-bit build with -instance N (N from 1 to 9); each keeps its own settings and game.log. Chapter 18.
  • Interaction: a script made of {on event} rules that controls behaviour. Chapter 11.
  • Inventory: the extender that holds a unit's weapons and ammo. Chapters 6 and 8.

K

  • Key: a named setting inside a block, followed by its value. Chapters 5 and 6.
  • keylint: the tool that checks keys for typos and wrong values. Chapter 19.
  • keys.set: the file that defines hotkeys. Chapter 15.

L

  • LAN Remote: lets a phone, a tablet or another computer on your home network view the ARSENAL window through a private link. Changes are made only on the PC. Chapter 19.
  • LOADS_STATIC: the verdict of check when it finds no known crash pattern and accepts the version. It never means the mod works. Chapter 19.
  • Lint: an automatic check for likely mistakes. Chapter 19.
  • Lobby: the pre-match screen where players join and data is compared. Chapter 12.
  • lng (.lng): a localization file of text keys, saved as UTF-8. Chapter 14.
  • Load order: the order in which mods are mounted. Later mods win. Chapter 3.
  • localizations (folder): the folder of a Gates of Hell mod that holds texts and files per language, localizations/<code>/. Gates of Hell does not read the localization/ folder of an Assault Squad 2 mod (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • LOD: level of detail, meaning simpler models shown when far away. Chapter 16.
  • Loose file: a file sitting in a folder rather than inside a pak. It always beats the same path in the mod's root resource.pak; against a pak inside resource/, the folder scan order decides. Chapter 4 and Reference 1.
  • Lua: the scripting language used by multiplayer bots. Chapters 10 and 12.

M

  • Macro: a reusable chunk of SDL with parameters. Chapter 5.
  • Material (.mtl): a file saying which textures and shading a mesh uses. Chapter 16.
  • mdl (.mdl): a model definition file. Chapter 16.
  • mi (.mi): a mission or map file with players, triggers and commands. Chapters 12 and 13.
  • Minidump: see Crash dump.
  • Mod: a folder with a mod.info that changes the game. Chapter 3.
  • mod.info: the mod's description file with name, version range and requirements. Chapter 3.
  • mod_<item number>: the name Gates of Hell gives a mod that comes from the Workshop, fixed by the item number (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • Morale: a soldier's willingness to keep fighting. Chapter 8.
  • Mount: making a folder or pak part of the virtual file system. Chapters 4 and 20.

N

  • Node: the program (Node.js) that runs the modding tools. Chapter 19.

O

  • OOS (out of sync): the multiplayer failure where machines diverge. Dumps go to log/oos/. Chapters 18 and 21.
  • options.set: your profile's settings file, including the list of active mods. Chapters 2 and 3.
  • Override: replacing an original file by giving your mod a file with the same path. Chapter 4.

P

  • Pak: a zip archive of game files. Chapters 4 and 20.
  • Package: the ready mod folder, with its mod.info and its paks, that the Share page writes for friends. Chapter 20.
  • pat (.pat): a numbered archive (1.pat, 2.pat) holding patches. Numbering must have no gap. Chapter 4.
  • Patch (.patch): a file of edit instructions applied from a .pat archive. Chapter 4.
  • Patch mod: a separate mod folder that ARSENAL fix writes its safe repairs into. It loads after your mod, so your mod is never changed. Check, fix and read the log.
  • Pathfinding: how units choose a route. Chapter 7.
  • Penetration: whether a shell gets through armor. Chapter 9.
  • Persona: a way of playing for the multiplayer bot that the Bot Doctrine page and doctrine write into a mod as starting numbers. Bots.
  • Phone view: the ARSENAL window as another device shows it over LAN Remote: every page can be read, nothing can be changed. Chapter 19.
  • Pitfall: a known trap. Each chapter lists the ones for its topic.
  • Play card: the short text the Share page and the release task make for friends: which mods, in which order, on which game build. Chapter 20.
  • pot (.pot): the text file format of Gates of Hell (UTF-8). The game ships no .lng files (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 14.
  • Preset: a saved bundle of game settings for a match. Chapter 12.
  • Priority: a mod.info key only Gates of Hell reads: a whole number, 1 when missing. Among mods that do not depend on each other, a higher number applies later and wins (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.

Q

  • Quant: one tick of game time, the unit used for timers and speeds in data. Chapter 5.
  • Quick Guided Task: the row above the tabs of the ARSENAL window: "I want to" make, change or explore something, then Start. A task asks one question at a time, writes into your mod with restore points, and checks it. Use the Quick Guided Task and chapter 19.

R

  • refcheck: the tool that checks that every name an entity uses exists. Chapter 19.
  • rep (.rep): a Gates of Hell replay, one zip file in replays/. Gates of Hell and Assault Squad 2 cannot read each other's replays (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • Repository: the game's internal list of loaded resources. The log prints Repository: N resources. Chapters 4 and 18.
  • Resource folder: resource/ in the game or in a mod, holding data. Chapter 2.
  • Restore point: the old version of a file, kept just before the Editor or a task writes it, in a folder beside your mod named <mod>.arsenal-undo. Chapter 19.

S

  • sav (.sav): a Gates of Hell saved game, one archive per save. Saves do not cross between Gates of Hell and Assault Squad 2 (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • Saved task: a Quick Guided Task you started and left. Pick it under "Saved tasks" and press Continue, or Throw away. Chapter 19.
  • SOEdit: a model editor for the game's model files, opened from the Models page or with ARSENAL soedit open. It is not part of the ARSENAL download; the Models page offers "Get SOEdit and open it", which downloads its latest release from GitHub. Chapters 19 and 21, and Edit a model.
  • SDL: the text data language used by almost all game data. Chapter 5.
  • Sensor: data defining what a unit sees and hears. Chapters 6 and 10.
  • set (.set): a data file, often a table of values, under set/. Chapters 5 and 6.
  • Share page: the page that gets a mod ready for friends or the Workshop: mod.info, picture, release check, package, clean copy, uploader, new version and play card. Assault Squad 2 and the 64-bit build only. Chapter 20 and Pack and share.
  • Shot tool: the Shot button of the Models page's 3D view: a click on the model fires the chosen shell at that point and shows what happens. Chapter 9.
  • Soft code: the editable text and resource layer, as opposed to the compiled program. Chapter 1.
  • Stage record: the small file the Models page writes into your mod (under .arsenal/soedit/) when it copies a model, so that SOEdit opens the copy rather than the original. Edit a model.
  • Stuff: weapon, ammo and item data files. Chapters 6 and 9.

T

  • Tag: a word used to match things, such as ammo to penetration tables. Chapters 5 and 9.
  • Tags (mod.info): a line of words in a Gates of Hell mod.info: develop lifts the version check and no_delete hides the delete button. Assault Squad 2 skips the line (not tested in a running game, see the summary). Chapter 20.
  • Testrun: the tool that drives the game for automatic checks. Chapter 18.
  • Texture: an image drawn on a model. Chapter 16.
  • Translate numbers: the fold in step 3 of the GoH unit page that shows how a port translates speed, armour and other numbers to Assault Squad 2 scale and lets you choose where the translation is unsure. Chapter 19.
  • Triage: sorting log messages into fatal, suspicious and harmless. Chapters 18 and 21.

U

  • Unconfirmed: a fact not yet confirmed in the game, marked "(unconfirmed)" in this guide. See the README.
  • UTF-8: the text encoding used by .lng files. Chapter 14.

V

  • VFS (virtual file system): the combined view of all game and mod files. Chapter 4.
