Does: Marks the preset as night. Sight ranges are then multiplied by night_vision, unless the target is lit by a light or lightning is shown.

Limits: Without {night} the night_vision value has no effect.

Example: {light {night} {night_vision 0.3}}

See: night_vision.

night_vision

Where: {light ...} block of an environment preset. Type: number, factor.

Values: default 0.13. Vanilla: 105 presets use 1, six use 0.3, one uses 0.2.

Does: Multiplies sight ranges at night.

Limits: Works only with {night}. A LightView near the target (a flare, a burning wreck) counts as lit and cancels it.

Gates of Hell: lights whose view is local (small lamps on a model) no longer count as lighting the target, so they do not cancel the night penalty.

Example: {night_vision 0.3}

See: LightView.

Sound

Sound names in data are paths under the sound/ folder, without the extension. A name that is a folder plays a random .wav from it, taken from a shuffled list so the same file does not repeat at once. There are no aliases. Weapon fireSound names live under weapon/shot/, reloadSound under weapon/reload/.

sound name

Where: any key that takes a sound (fireSound, reloadSound, FX {sound}, scripts). Type: string.

Values: a folder or file path under sound/.

Does: Picks what is played.

Limits: A name that does not exist logs unknown sound file '<name>' and plays nothing. At most 3 copies of one file play at once, and a copy starting within 50 ms of the same one is dropped.

Example: {fireSound "mg42"}

See: folder.set.

folder.set

Where: any folder under sound/, signature sound. Type: file.

Values: the keys Tag, Loudness, Distance, MinDistance, MaxDistance, Volume, Signal, SignalPeriod.

Does: Settings for every sound in the folder and its subfolders; a subfolder inherits from its parent unless it has its own.

Limits: An unknown key gives "unexpected token". A subfolder with its own folder.set starts again from the default loudness: repeat {Distance} or {Loudness} in it to keep the parent's values. {Volume} on a folder of sounds not placed in the world (interface, weather loops) has no effect.

Gates of Hell: a subfolder keeps the distances it inherits from its parent; only the top folder starts from the default loudness. {Volume} also scales sounds not placed in the world. A placed sound whose folder has no minimum distance is stopped, and a warning names the folder.

Example:

{Tag "effects"} {Loudness "shoot normal"} {Distance 10 400}

See: Tag, Loudness.

Tag

Where: folder.set. Type: string.

Values: effects, emotions, speech, environment; any other word counts as the "other" group.

Does: Puts the sounds into a volume and channel group (see percent).

Limits: Vanilla main_environment, used by six folders, falls into the "other" group.

Example: {Tag "speech"}

See: percent.

Loudness

Where: folder.set. Type: string.

Values: a name from the loudness rows of sound/sound.set.

Does: Sets how far and with what priority the sound is heard.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Loudness "blast big"}

See: loudness.

Distance, MinDistance, MaxDistance

Where: folder.set. Type: numbers, metres.

Values: {Distance min max} or the two single keys; folder defaults 0 and 100.

Does: Full volume up to the minimum, silence beyond the maximum.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Distance 10 400}

See: snd_rolloff in sound console variables.

Volume

Where: folder.set. Type: number, factor.

Values: default 1.0.

Does: Volume of the folder's sounds.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Volume 0.8}

See: folder.set.

Signal

Where: folder.set. Type: name and number.

Values: a signal name (movement, shot, hit, injure, explosion, mandie, sound, ally_info) and a radius in metres.

Does: Playing the sound also tells nearby AI units that something happened, so they can react.

Limits: Units with a hearingBias larger than the radius ignore it.

Example: {signal explosion 20}

See: SignalPeriod, hearingBias.

SignalPeriod

Where: folder.set. Type: number, seconds.

Values: any number.

Does: The shortest time between two signals from the same source.

Limits: none known.

Example: {SignalPeriod 1}

See: Signal.

percent

Where: sound/sound.set. Type: row {percent group share [max]}.

Values: vanilla effects 45, emotions 15 max 2, speech 10 max 1, environment 20, main_environment 10.

Does: Share of the sound channels each group may use, and optionally the most sounds of that group at once.

Limits: A group with no row gets 20% and a limit of 1000.

Example: {percent "speech" 10 1}

See: Tag.

loudness

Where: sound/sound.set. Type: row {loudness name min max [priority]}.

Values: 19 rows in vanilla, for example default 20 0, shoot normal 10 0 priority 20, blast big 50 0 priority 40, canonade 400 0.

Does: Named distance and priority classes that Loudness in folder.set refers to.

Limits: A mod sound.set replaces the whole file: keep every name your data uses and default, or the game stops with No 'default' loudness in sound.set.

Example: {loudness "hit" 15 500 15}

See: Loudness.

sound console variables

Where: game console. Type: console commands.

Values: snd_disable, snd_maxFilePlayedChannels, snd_cutoffPart, snd_keepTime, snd_antiReverbThreshold, snd_rolloff.

Does: Switch sound off and tune channels, cut-off and roll-off while testing.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: snd_restart reloads the sounds without restarting the game. snd_ambientBuffersCount (default 8) caps the sounds not placed in the world. The media variables are renamed snd_maxMediaChannels (default 4) and snd_mediaDisabled. snd_compressorGain, snd_compressorMix and snd_compressorRatio do not exist.

Example: snd_disable 1

See: Chapter 18, Chapter 16, section 2.

Environment presets

An environment preset is one file in set/environment/ with the signature environment. The mission command environment {name time apply} blends to it; only one blend runs at a time and there is no game clock that changes it by itself.

environment preset

Where: set/environment/<name>. Type: file.

Values: the blocks light, wind, haze, sky, weather, thunder, video_overlay, grain, dof, glow.

Does: Sets the light, sky, weather and screen effects of a map.

Limits: An unknown block logs unknown environment parameters "<x>". Applying a preset that does not exist logs Can't apply environment preset "<name>", using defaults when a map loads it, and does nothing at all when a mission command asks for it.

Gates of Hell: presets can also have the blocks ocean_wave_works and render_tweaks, which this game does not know (it logs unknown environment parameters). See Gates of Hell only.

Example: {light ...} {haze {enable} {start 2000} {end 4200}}

See: Reference 11 (mission files), Chapter 16, section 3.

light

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: direction (default -0.78 0 -0.62), ambient, diffuse, specular (colours as 0xAARRGGBB), specularPower, {night}, night_vision (0.13), lightsIntensity (0.2), {draw_sun_moon}, sun_moon_radius, color_correction, camera_lens_effetcs.

Does: Sun direction and colours, night, the strength of lamps, colour grading and lens effects.

Limits: camera_lens_effetcs must be written with this spelling.

Gates of Hell: the specular colour is not read; one number specularIntensity (default 1) scales the specular of materials instead. New groups: rim_light {color strength} (the rim light shows only when its strength is above 0), tone_mapping (used with the HDR video option), color_shading gains an intensity, and camera_lens_effetcs gains a mission-wide vision_mode (thermal, night or drone). This game does not know these keys: remove them when you bring a preset over.

Example: {light {direction -0.6 0.2 -0.7} {night_vision 0.3}}

See: night, color_correction.

color_correction

Where: inside {light}. Type: block.

Values: gamma, brightness, contrast, saturation, tone, tone_strength, {color_shading {enable} {shade_tone}}.

Does: Colour grading of the whole picture.

Limits: none known.

Example: {color_correction {saturation 0.9} {contrast 1.1}}

See: light.

camera_lens_effetcs

Where: inside {light}. Type: block.

Values: {light_scattering {enable} {intensity} {ray_length} {color_tone}}, {lens_dirt {enable} {texture}}, {screen_brightening {enable} {intensity}}.

Does: Sun rays, dirt on the lens and a brightening of the screen.

Limits: Some vanilla presets also write keys inside light_scattering that no source describes (listed at the end).

Example: {camera_lens_effetcs {lens_dirt {enable} {texture "..."}}}

See: light.

wind

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: speed x y z, amplitude (default 2).

Does: Wind for water and particles.

Limits: Wind does not move shells or units.

Gates of Hell: the wind block has the keys direction, main_strength (0 to 1), detail_strength (0 to 10) and height_amplification (0 to 5); speed and amplitude are not read, so a preset from this game loses its wind there. Wind also sways plants, and blends between presets.

Example: {wind {speed 2 1 0} {amplitude 2}}

See: NoDependOnWind in Mover.

haze

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, color (default b4bed2), start (2000), end (4200).

Does: Distance fog.

Limits: end must be greater than start, and start at least 0.

Gates of Hell: a map can also have a Haze block with boundary haze (on by default) and height haze (altitude, off by default), and a preset can set altitude_strength and sky_haziness. This game rejects a map Haze block.

Example: {haze {enable} {start 1500} {end 3500}}

See: light.

sky

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, texture, globalEnvironment, color, intensity (0.5), azimuth.

Does: The sky picture and its reflection.

Limits: none known.

Example: {sky {enable} {intensity 0.5}}

See: light.

weather

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, density, fx, "speed x", "speed y", "speed z", "reverse speed probability", sound, volume, "sound 2", "volume 2", "sound 3", "volume 3".

Does: Rain or snow: falling particles and their sounds.

Limits: Off unless {enable} is written. At most 2000 drops. Scripts test {if rain}, which is false for snow.

Example: {weather {enable} {density 0.6} {sound "ambient/rain"}}

See: thunder.

thunder

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, interval a b, color, sound.

Does: Lightning flashes at random intervals.

Limits: Off unless {enable} is written, and no strike happens while sound is empty.

Example: {thunder {enable} {interval 10 30}}

See: weather.

video_overlay

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: on, file, color.

Does: Plays a video over the picture.

Limits: none known.

Example: {video_overlay {on} {file "..."}}

See: .avi.

grain

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, colorAmount, grainAmount, grainParticleSize, lumAmount.

Does: Film grain.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: the block is accepted but nothing in it is read, so preset grain does nothing there.

Example: {grain {enable} {grainAmount 0.05}}

See: light.

dof

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, near_scale, far_scale, near_start, near_end, far_start, far_end, {"3rd_Person" {"3rdP_blurscale" f}}, blur_strength.

Does: Depth of field blur.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: dof gains a second set of ranges, Scenario Settings, used while a mission video or voice plays, and 3rdP_blur_strength (a whole number of passes) replaces 3rdP_blurscale, which it no longer reads. Remove Scenario Settings when you bring a preset over.

Example: {dof {enable} {far_start 300} {far_end 900}}

See: glow.

glow

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: enable, amount.

Does: Glow around bright areas.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: glow also has threshold (default 1.1), which only matters with the HDR video option on.

Example: {glow {enable} {amount 0.4}}

See: dof.

Effects (FX)

An effect is an entity .def whose root is {fx ...}. Data and scripts start one with {spawn "name"}. Inside, views draw it: SpriteView, ParticleView, LightView and DecalView. A view written as {#+ ...} is folded in editors but still read; a view written {## ...} is skipped.

fx

Where: root of an effect .def. Type: block.

Values: views, {sound "name"}, and the effect keys below.

Does: Declares an effect entity. {sound} plays once when it spawns.

Limits: There is no {emit} action; scripts that use it log unknown action. At most 40000 particles exist at once; more are silently not made.

Example:

{fx {sound "explosion/small"}
  {SpriteView {Sprite "$/flash01"} ...}}

See: spawn in Reference 10, Chapter 16, section 4.

SpriteView

Where: inside {fx}. Type: block.

Values: Sprite (a texture; $/ means texture/fx/), Offset, AutoVisible, Orientation, Normal, NormalXY, NormalXZ, NormalYZ, Billboard, Trace, Halo, ConstantSize, SoftIntersection, EmitsHeat, UseDirection, {ground}, {layer ...}, {NotifyOwner}, {delay s}, and the channels below.

Does: One flat picture: a flash, a glow, a tracer.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: a sprite view also takes UseHQ and Halo {Scale {Min} {Max}}, which this game rejects as "unexpected token": remove them when you bring an effect over. Halos fade more sharply by angle, and sprites on a scaled bone are scaled too. A view marked Fire no longer shows only at night: add NightOnly to keep that.

Example: {SpriteView {Sprite "$/flash01"} {Billboard} {delay 0.05}}

See: sprite channels.

sprite channels

Where: inside SpriteView. Type: blocks.

Values: Visibility, Scale, Light, Highlight, each a curve: {linear {min} {max}} or {npower {min} {max} {pow}}; {timer {mode play|loop} {duration s [rand]}}; {preTurn a b}.

Does: Change the sprite over its lifetime: fade, grow, brighten.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Scale {linear {min 0.5} {max 2}}} {timer {mode play} {duration 0.3 0.1}}

See: SpriteView.

LightView

Where: inside {fx} or a model bone. Type: block.

Values: type point, animator, attenuation0, attenuation1, attenuation2, radius, effectonground, offset, falloff, phi, theta, priority, pulseperiod, intensity, radiusfalloff.

Does: A dynamic light.

Limits: A light counts as lighting its surroundings for night sight (see night_vision).

Gates of Hell: TimeToLive (seconds, default 0 means never) makes a light go out by itself; this game does not read it. A local light no longer counts for night sight.

Example: {LightView {type point} {radius 8} {intensity 1.5}}

See: night, night_vision.

ParticleView

Where: inside {fx}. Type: block.

Values: delay, Offset, AutoPause, and the blocks Generator, Mover, Visualizer, EntityGenerator.

Does: A particle system: smoke, dust, sparks, debris.

Limits: Counts toward the 40000 particle limit.

Example: {ParticleView {Generator ...} {Mover ...} {Visualizer ...}}

See: Generator.

Generator

Where: inside ParticleView. Type: block.

Values: {TotalParticles n [spread]}, {TimeToLive s} (below 0 means unlimited), ParticlesInBlock, {EmissionArea {Radius} {Alpha0} {Alpha1} {Psi} {Theta} {Speed} {DistributionLaw disk|sphere}}, {ParticleInit {Speed} {Lifetime}}, AxisZ, AutoTurn, OwnerSpeed, Color.

Does: How many particles are made, where and with what start speed and life.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: a generator that restarts can make more than TotalParticles, so smoke and fire can come out thicker after a restart. Rarely, an EmissionArea angle makes a whole block of particles vanish.

Example: {Generator {TotalParticles 40 10} {TimeToLive 1.5}}

See: Mover.

Mover

Where: inside ParticleView. Type: block.

Values: Gravity, Damping, Vector, Value, {Collisions {Terrain} {Objects} {Once} {Reflection}}, Restitution, NoDependOnWind.

Does: How the particles move: gravity, drag, wind, bounces.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: particles that follow the wind (no NoDependOnWind) drift at a speed set by the wind and the game speed, so the same effect drifts differently in the two games.

Example: {Mover {Gravity -2} {Damping 0.5} {Collisions {Terrain}}}

See: wind.

Visualizer

Where: inside ParticleView. Type: block.

Values: stage blocks Stage, Initial, Collided, Dying, each with {Sprite}, {Freq} and {Flags {KillParticle} {MatchSprites} {Ground}}; RandomSprites.

Does: Which picture a particle shows in each part of its life.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Visualizer {Stage {Sprite "$/smoke01"}} {RandomSprites}}

See: Generator.

EntityGenerator

Where: inside ParticleView. Type: block.

Values: {Entity "name" {Freq}}.

Does: Makes particles spawn another entity or effect.

Limits: none known.

Gates of Hell: also takes {Align x|y|z|invx|invy|invz} to aim the spawned entity, and {SpinX v [spread]}, SpinY, SpinZ to turn it; this game reads only the entity and its frequency.

Example: {EntityGenerator {Entity "debris_small" {Freq 0.2}}}

See: fx.

DecalView

Where: inside {fx}. Type: block.

Values: a decal material and size.

Does: Puts a mark on the ground or a surface (a crater, a scorch).

Limits: Ground decals must be listed in fxmanager.set (see fxmanager).

Gates of Hell: a static decal whose sprite is animated logs <model>: Static decal with non-constant sprite animator and becomes dynamic. Decals, particles and batched scenery show in the thermal view only when marked EmitsHeat.

Example: {DecalView ...}

See: fxmanager.

fxmanager

Where: set/fxmanager.set. Type: block.

Values: groups {name {fx "n"} ... {countLimit n} {timeLimit s}}. Vanilla: shellholes 40, tracks 700 for 10 s, blood 40, flashes 0.05 s.

Does: Caps how many ground marks and tracers of a kind exist and how long they last.

Limits: A ground or tracer effect not listed logs Entity "<name>" must be defined in fxmanager.set before add. Vanilla misses tracewheel06.

Example: {shellholes {fx "crater_small"} {countLimit 40}}

See: entitymanager.

entitymanager

Where: set/entitymanager.set. Type: block.

Values: Enabled, CountScale, and groups {group "n" actor|gameentity|stuff|dead {limit} {remove instant|bury|dissolve} {entity} {tag} {DeadVehicles}}. Vanilla limits: dead 30, broken 5, piece 10, stuff 100, equip 30, shellhole 50.

Does: Removes the oldest corpses, wrecks, dropped items and pieces when a group passes its limit.

Limits: none known.

Example: {group "dead" dead {limit 30} {remove bury}}

See: fxmanager.

Level of detail and rendering keys

level_of_detail.set

Where: set/level_of_detail.set, level_of_detail_manual.set, level_of_detail_zoom.set; signature levelofdetail. Type: file.

Values: ZoomFactor, GrassDistance, GrassFadeDepth, GrassZoomFactor, and classes {name {distance d {NoFog} {NoGetShadow} {NoCastShadow} {off}} ...}.

Does: At what camera distance each class of model drops shadows, fog or disappears.

Limits: Distances in a class must grow, or the game logs Distance should be farther than previous one. A flag stays on in later levels. An empty class logs Empty LOD class '<name>' in <file>. Vanilla scales the distances by 0.75 in multiplayer and 0.70 in co-op. Console r_LODEnable 0 turns it off for testing.

Gates of Hell: there is also level_of_detail_scenario.set, and the files take minzoom, grassthinnerdepth, grassthinnerpower and shadowfallofffactor (how far sun shadows reach; 0 means no shadow distance). Levels take the flags noparallax, nobump, nospecular and parallaxstepsk. This game stops on these keys: remove them when you bring a level of detail file over.

Example: {tank {distance 400 {NoCastShadow}} {distance 900 {off}}}

See: lodclass, Chapter 16, Level of detail.

lodclass

Where: entity .def. Type: string.

Values: a class name from level_of_detail.set.

Does: Chooses the distance rules for this entity.

Limits: none known.

Example: {lodclass "decor_medium"}

See: level_of_detail.set.

NoCastShadows, NoGetShadows, UseShadow

Where: entity .def. Type: switches.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Turn off the shadow the entity casts or receives, or choose a simple shadow.

Limits: none known.

Example: {NoCastShadows}

See: lodclass.

RimLight

Where: entity .def. Type: switch.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Draws a rim light on the model.

Limits: none known.

Example: {RimLight}

See: light.

UseDecal, DecalOrder, DecalTarget, DecalTargetDynamic

Where: entity .def. Type: switches and number.

Values: DecalOrder a whole number.

Does: Whether the entity takes decals, in what drawing order, and whether it is a target for decals while moving.

Limits: none known.

Example: {UseDecal} {DecalOrder 2}

See: DecalView.

TexMods, texmod

Where: entity .def. Type: block of string pairs.

Values: {TexMods {"Option" "variant"}}; texture files named T#variant.dds.

Does: Picks a texture variant (camouflage, markings) for the model.

Limits: none known.

Example: {TexMods {"camo" "winter"}}

See: textures.

camera

Where: set/registry/camera.reg. Type: block.

Values: {perspective {viewAngle 23} {distance 1600} {fov 65}}, {parallel {viewAngle 90} {distance 2000} {fov 0} {centered 1}} in vanilla.

Does: The player's camera angle, distance and field of view.

Limits: Camera shake is off unless the console variable cam_shake is not 0. The third person camera is not set in a moddable file.

Gates of Hell: camera shake is the game option camera_shakes and cam_shake is gone; shakes are stronger and stop more abruptly. The field of view key is camera/main/fov, so a camera/perspective/fov setting is ignored there. Cameras also take zNear, zFar and depthScale.

Example: {camera {perspective {viewAngle 30} {distance 1800} {fov 60}}}

See: Chapter 16, Camera.

Model and animation file kinds

.mdl

Where: next to the model files of an entity. Type: SDL text file.

Values: one {Skeleton ...} with bones and {animation {sequence ...}}, plus {Volume}, {Obstacle} and {Area} blocks.

Does: Builds the model: the bone tree, which mesh each bone shows, its animations and its hit shapes.

Limits: Keys apply in the order they are written. A missing view file logs Unknown view.

Gates of Hell: two animations with the same name stop the load with Animation with duplicate name; this game keeps both. The bone name ##skeleton_views## is reserved. A view that fails to load no longer takes a level of detail slot, so the later levels move down by one.

Example:

{Skeleton
  {bone "body" {VolumeView "body.ply"}
    {bone revolute "turret" {VolumeView "turret.ply"}}}}

See: bone (model), volume in Reference 7 for {Volume}, Chapter 16, section 5, Edit a model or an animation.

bone (model)

Where: inside {Skeleton} of a .mdl. Type: block {bone [type] "name" ...}.

Values: type revolute, prizmatic, socket, planarsocket, wild, or none. Keys: Bone (child), View, SpriteView, VolumeView (the mesh), ParticleView, DecalView, LODView {.. {OFF}}, ControlBone, Name, Matrix34, Position, Orientation, Visibility, Parameters, Terminator, Animation, Color, and for typed bones limits, speed, speed2.

Does: One joint of the model. A typed bone can turn or slide (turrets, guns, wheels, doors).

Limits: Any other type word gives "unexpected token". {limits lo hi} and {speed} on a bone without a type give "unexpected token". {speed 0} logs Zero speed in ik-bone "<name>". State is accepted but does nothing.

Gates of Hell: bones take a Land parameter, which is "unexpected token" here. Several bone names differ: track rollers are numbered (roller_01, roller_02, each with roller_NN_joint) where this game uses one roller and roller_joint; a bone named suspension above a wheel lets it ride the ground; soldiers aim with ik_lng, ik_lat and ik_socket where this game uses ik_updown. On a model brought over, no roller follows the ground (renaming one to roller makes only that one follow), and soldiers lose the aim bend. See Bring a unit from Gates of Hell.

Example: {bone revolute "gun_rot" {limits -8 20} {speed 15}}

See: Parameters.

Parameters

Where: inside a model bone. Type: string.

Values: entries such as "ID=", "WheelRadius=", "Radius=", CommonMesh, align.

Does: Extra settings read by other parts of the game, for example the wheel radius used by the chassis.

Limits: none known.

Example: {Parameters "WheelRadius=6.2"}

See: Reference 4.

sequence

Where: inside {animation} of the .mdl. Type: block with a name.

Values: file, speed, resume, store, movement, pinback, smooth, autostart, duration (frames or percent), rotate, dynamicspeed, blend/pose.

Does: Declares an animation the game and scripts can play by name.

Limits: A sequence without file loads <name>.anm. dynamicspeed ranges must meet exactly, or a near miss leaves a range with zero speed. Avoid duration frames N: it can crash the game.

Gates of Hell: there are two more animation types, blendspace and aimset, and a sequence takes additive and events; this game rejects all of them as "unexpected token". A file name without .anm is first tried as a folder, and every .anm in it is a variant picked at random per entity. duration frames N makes the sequence never end instead of crashing. dynamicspeed ranges only need to meet within 0.00001.

Example: {sequence "fire" {file "fire.anm"} {speed 1.5}}

See: .anm.

bone modifiers in a .def

Where: entity .def, after {Extension}. Type: blocks.

Values: bone names and the bone keys above.

Does: Change bones of the model from the entity file.

Limits: Without {Extension} first, the game logs Bone modifiers must be placed after skeleton load. A bone that does not exist logs Bone <name> not found in <model>.

Example: {Extension "tank.mdl"} {bone "gun_rot" {limits -5 15}}

See: bone (model).

.ply

Where: mesh files named by VolumeView. Type: binary file.

Values: header EPLY or BPLY; chunks BNDS, SKIN, MESH, SUBM, VERT, INDX, ADJA, SHDW, MROR.

Does: The visible mesh of a bone, with its materials.

Limits: Chunks have no stored lengths, so a damaged file cannot be skipped over; an unknown chunk logs Invalid chunk in .PLY file!. About 65535 vertices at most per mesh. A skinned part maps at most 25 bones. A wrong header logs Can't create resource object. A missing .mtl with no .materials file to fall back on crashes the game.

Gates of Hell: a skin variant can swap the mesh: variant camo shows tank#camo.ply when that file exists. This game swaps textures only, so such files do nothing here. A part with no material loads, drawn grey with a warning, where this game crashes: ship every .mtl with a model you bring over.

Example: (binary; export it with a converter)

See: .mtl.

.anm

Where: animation files named by sequence. Type: binary file.

Values: header EANM, version at least 196608 (hex 30000); chunks FRMS, BMAP, FRM2, FRMN.

Does: Bone movements over time.

Limits: An older version logs Unsupported animation version. At least one frame is needed (At least one frame required). At most 255 bones (Animated bones count is limited to 255!). Other errors: unknown chunk in animation, Invalid frame #. A track for a bone the skeleton lacks is skipped. A file ending in _lodN belongs to level of detail N. The bone placement carries root motion.

Example: (binary)

See: sequence.

.mtl

Where: material files named by meshes. Type: SDL text file.

Values: the type word right after material: simple, bump, layered, envmap, ocean, gui.text; keys diffuse, bump, specular, envmap, mask, color, blend.

Does: How a mesh surface is drawn.

Limits: Texture names are written without an extension; a bare name is looked up next to the model. Many more keys exist in vanilla files than are described (listed at the end).

Gates of Hell: materials take more keys, among them lightmap, No_Outlines and Dxt1OpacityFix; bump materials take specular_intensity, gloss_scale and full_specular; layered materials take GlobalNormalmap and GlobalDiffusemap. This game stops on the material and bump keys as "unexpected token", and probably on the layered ones too: remove them when you bring a model over. parallax_scale is multiplied by a console value (r_parallaxGlobalScale, default 0.5), so the same value probably looks deeper here. EmitsHeat takes no number. An unknown material type and a name missing from a .materials library are named in the log.

Example: {material bump {diffuse "t34s"}}

See: textures.

.materials

Where: next to a .ply. Type: text file.

Values: the material names of the mesh.

Does: The fallback that lists materials when no .mtl is found.

Limits: See .ply.

Example: (text list)

See: .ply.

textures

Where: texture folders. Type: .dds, .tga, .bmp, .jpg, .png, and the SDL files .ebm and .tex.

Values: the game looks for the name with each extension in that order; the last one found wins, and .ebm or .tex win over all.

Does: Pictures for meshes, effects and the interface.

Limits: DDS files with the DX10 header are not supported (DXT10 textures are not supported.); the ATI2 format logs Unknown DDS picture format. A texture name that is not found shows a checker pattern and logs nothing. Under /interface/ and /map/, files whose names start with the picture's name and end in two digits are loaded as its animation frames. For the picture flag, the files flag02, flag_02, flag_big_02 and flag1234 are frames; flagx02 and flag123 are not. An unrelated picture whose name starts with the same word and ends in two digits therefore loads as an extra frame: rename it.

Gates of Hell: BC5 normal maps (ATI2, BC5U, BC5S) load; convert them to DXT5 or A8R8G8B8 when you bring a model over, or they are missing here. A texture that is missing or cannot be read shows the checker and the log names it. Only flag02 and flag_02 count as frames of flag. A picture listed twice in a common texture stops the game.

Example: tank_d.dds

See: .ebm and .tex, Chapter 16, Materials and textures.

.ebm and .tex

Where: texture folders. Type: SDL text file.

Values: reference, bitmap, Axis, Filtering, Mipmap, Cursor, NoCompression, AlphaChannel, TextureAnimation, Blend, Animation, Play, Reverse, Loop, PingPong, AsyncStart, Frame.

Does: Describe a texture: its source picture, filtering, and animation frames.

Limits: A file that is not SDL logs Not SDL file!; a wrong signature logs File signature mismatch.

Example: {bitmap "flag.dds"} {Mipmap 0}

See: textures.

.wav

Where: sound/ folders. Type: RIFF wave file.

Values: vanilla files are mono, 44.1 kHz, IMA ADPCM or 16-bit PCM.

Does: The only sound format the game plays. The "Look & Sound" page (Models & Sim > Look & Sound) has a "Sound of this weapon" block: "Find sound" shows the folder and files a weapon plays, "Listen" plays them, "Choose file... / Check" tests your own file, "Preview" makes it playable in the game, "Write the sound into my mod" writes it as IMA ADPCM or 16-bit PCM, and "ffmpeg recipe (make a safe wav)" gives the command lines to convert a file.

Limits: .ogg files are ignored; .mp3 is ignored too (unconfirmed). Sounds placed in the world should be mono.

Gates of Hell: probably also plays .wav only, so ship mod sounds as .wav there too.

Example: sound/weapon/shot/mg42/01.wav

See: sound name, Chapter 16, section 2, Models & Sim.

.avi

Where: video folders. Type: video file.

Values: Xvid (MPEG-4 Part 2) picture with MP3 sound.

Does: Videos and overlays.

Limits: A video in another codec, H.264 among them, does not play; a menu video then falls back to its still picture without an error. The exact conversion settings that work are unconfirmed.

Gates of Hell: videos are decoded by a newer Xvid (1.3.5).

Example: video/intro.avi

See: video_overlay, Chapter 16, Video.

Not described yet

These keys appear in vanilla data but no source describes their effect yet:

  • light scattering keys in presets: sample_count, sun_radius, ray_intensity, lum_worldToSun_ratio, darken
  • images.set keys: user_ambient, ally_ambient, enemy_ambient, user_diffuse, ally_diffuse, enemy_diffuse, size, alpha, humans_light, vehicles_light, shadow, cloudsonwater, scrollspeed, windspeed
  • FX keys: peak, turn, scalex, scaley, greenlight, bluelight, redlight, shiftx, shifty, shiftz, prescalex, prescaley, preshiftx, nightonly, storeable, constrain, power, fire
  • .mtl keys: alpharef, alphatocoverage, tile, layer, parallax_scale, height, diffuse1, modulate2x, amount, glow, nolight, rimlight, translucency, emitsheat, fadeaway, zbias, period, bumpvolume, envamount, fakereflection
  • speaker keys: signals, signaldepend, soundname
  • entity key zclipvisibility

Gates of Hell only

The Gates of Hell notes in this book have not been tested in a running game. Check them in your own game before you depend on them.

These keys and files exist only in Gates of Hell, and this game does not read them. The entries above say which ones stop a file here, so remove those when you bring data over.

filters.set

Where: sound/filters/filters.set. Type: file.

Values: named chains of bandpass {center} {width} {strength}, lowpass {cutoff} {strength} and paramEq {center} {q} {gain} {strength}. q is held between 0 and 1 and gain between -18 and 18 dB.

Does: Sound filters laid over every sound placed in the world, for example inside a closed vehicle or when the soldier is wounded (woundedEffect).

Limits: An unknown filter type crashes the game. More than 8 filters in a chain probably overrun the game's table.

Example: {woundedEffect {lowpass {cutoff 500.0}}}

See: sound console variables.

snd_restart

Where: game console. Type: console command.

Values: none.

Does: Restarts the sound system and reloads the sounds, so a sound edit shows without restarting the game.

Limits: none known.

Example: snd_restart

See: sound console variables.

ocean_wave_works

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: ocean_mode, and sea_settings, lake_settings, river_settings, each with global, waves, ocean_look and shore.

Does: Sets the look of sea, lake and river water; the preset applies the group for the map's kind of water.

Limits: Values are clamped.

Example: {ocean_wave_works {sea_settings {global {patch_scale 120.096} {wind_dependency 0.85}}}}

See: environment preset.

render_tweaks

Where: environment preset. Type: block.

Values: decal_bias (default 1).

Does: Pushes decals on the ground away from it to stop them flickering into the ground.

Limits: none known.

Example: {render_tweaks {decal_bias 0}}

See: DecalView.

tone_mapping and tone curves

Where: {light} of a preset; curve files set/curves/tonemapping/*.bzc. Type: block and text files.

Values: max_white_percentile, min_mapping_range, curve "<file>".

Does: Picks the tone curve that maps the bright picture to the screen.

Limits: Works only with the HDR video option on. A change takes effect at the next day or night change.

Example: {tone_mapping {max_white_percentile 0.999} {min_mapping_range 1} {curve "/set/curves/tonemapping/dark2.bzc"}}

See: light.

video/hdr

Where: player video options. Type: option.

Values: on or off.

Does: Draws the picture in high dynamic range, with automatic exposure and the tone curve.

Limits: A device without HDR turns the option off. The video presets are also different: there is a maximum preset, so a saved preset number 5 means a different preset in the two games.

Example: (set in the video options)

See: tone_mapping and tone curves.

no_select_visor

Where: entity tag. Type: word.

Values: present or absent.

Does: An allied unit that the player cannot select also opens the fog of war with its sight when it has this tag.

Limits: none known.

Example: (in the entity's tags)

See: Fogable.

blendspace

Where: inside {animation} of the .mdl. Type: block with a name.

Values: {at v "anim"} rows and {resume}.

Does: Blends the two neighbouring animations by a value the game sets, for example a speed.

Limits: Errors: Invalid blend value, Invalid animation, Empty blendspace animation, Zero animation speed is invalid!. Form: {blendspace "walk" {at 0 "walk_slow"} {at 1 "walk_fast"}}. No stock Gates of Hell file uses it.

See: sequence.

aimset

Where: inside {animation} of the .mdl. Type: block with a name.

Values: h_limits, v_limits (degrees, default -90 to 90), left_anm, center_anm, right_anm, {center N}.

Does: Aims by blending a left, centre and right animation.

Limits: Use only the _anm forms: plain left, center or right with a string loops forever. Form: {aimset "aim" {left_anm "aim_l.anm"} {center_anm "aim_c.anm"} {right_anm "aim_r.anm"}}. No stock Gates of Hell file uses it.

See: sequence.

UseHQ and Halo

Where: SpriteView; Gates of Hell data also has UseHQ in a DecalView. Type: switch and block.

Values: UseHQ before Sprite; Halo {Scale {Min} {Max}}.

Does: UseHQ loads the sprite's texture at high quality. Halo keeps a halo's size on screen between Min and Max.

Limits: none known.

Example: {DecalView reverse_cone {useHq} {Sprite "reverse_cone.ebm"}} Form: {Halo {Scale {Min 0.5} {Max 2}}}. No stock Gates of Hell file uses it: stock halos hold only other keys, such as {halo {usedirection}}.

See: SpriteView.

TimeToLive (LightView)

Where: LightView. Type: number, seconds.

Values: default 0, which means the light never goes out by itself.

Does: A light that is switched on goes out by itself when the time is up.

Limits: none known.

Example: {lightview Light {type point} {radius 100} {timetolive 2}}

See: LightView.

camera_shakes

Where: player game options, in the game group. Type: option.

Values: on or off.

Does: Turns the camera shake from blasts on or off; it replaces the console variable cam_shake.

Limits: The server never shakes.

Example: (set in the game options)

See: camera.

Reference 9: Interface and Localization

This chapter lists the data keys of the interface: action files, command panel layouts, hotkeys, fonts, HUD settings, menu backgrounds, skins and page scripts. It also lists the rules of .lng text files, the text formatting tags, and the text keys the game asks for. Chapter 15 teaches the interface and chapter 14 teaches localization; this chapter is the lookup table.

How to read this chapter

All the files here are SDL text files: plain text made of nested blocks in curly braces, with ; starting a comment. Text files must be saved as UTF-8 with Windows line endings (CRLF). Names and identifiers stay plain ASCII.

The screens themselves are built into the game program. Data can change pictures, actions, panel layouts, keys, fonts, colours, skins, menu backgrounds and a few page scripts, but it cannot add new screens, move the command grid or resize the purchase panel.

A colour is written in one of three ways, depending on the file: a colour name such as white, red, dyellow or dgreen; a quoted "r g b" text with values from 0 to 255, sometimes with a fourth alpha value; or a hexadecimal 0xAARRGGBB number, where AA is the opacity.

Action files

Taught in chapter 15, section 4. The job: Icons and interface.

An action is one order a unit can be given, such as repair or throw a grenade. Each action can have a file at interface/action/<name>.set. When the name matches an action built into the game, the file configures that action. Any other name creates a new custom action, named after the file. Custom actions run a list of instructions, described under instructions below.

The built-in actions are: none, select, disable, move, rotate, cover, accelerate, cancel, drop, pour_in, pour_out, fortification, board, emit, enter, repair, collect, examine, care, injection, attach, detach, reinforce, throw_ap_grenade, throw_at_grenade, throw_sk_grenade, aimed_shot, bazooka_shot, suppression_fire, advance, attack, attack_ground, attack_melee, heal, medic, call_ally, mine, barricade, barbwire and hedgehog.

The game numbers actions in the order it creates them and sends those numbers in multiplayer orders. The host and every client must therefore load exactly the same set of action files, or orders arrive as the wrong action.

action

Where: action file, root block. Type: block.

Values: holds the keys below; an empty {action} keeps every default.

Does: Holds the settings of one action. Keyword names inside it are not case-sensitive.

Limits: A file that names no built-in action creates a new custom action, even if you only meant to change an existing one and misspelt its name. Gates of Hell: barricade, barbwire and hedgehog are no longer built in; every fortification is one {action "name"} block of interface/action/fortify.set. New built-in actions are airstrike, teleport, mine_ap and mine_at, and repair can be configured like a custom action (not confirmed).

Example:

{action
    {cursor}
    {button}
    {fx "flashblue"}
}

See: chapter 15, section 4.

cursor

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: word, an optional quoted cursor name and an optional second name.

Values: a folder name under interface/cursor/; without a name, the action's own name is used.

Does: Sets the mouse cursor shown while the action is chosen. A second name gives the cursor shown at a position.

Limits: A cursor name with no folder shows no cursor and logs nothing. Gates of Hell: the pick-up action shows its second cursor over an item when the inventory has room for it, so the second name works as a "room" hint there.

Example:

{action
    {cursor "use"}
}

See: button.

button

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: word, an optional quoted picture name.

Values: a picture name under interface/scene/panel_control/, which may include a subfolder; without a name, the action's own name is used.

Does: Sets the picture of the action's command panel button.

Limits: Leaving the key out entirely gives the button a placeholder picture. A picture name with no file also shows the placeholder and logs nothing.

Example:

{action
    {cursor}
    {button "repair"}
}

See: Icon folders and frames.

fx

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: text, a ground effect name.

Values: an effect name such as "flashred", "flashgreen" or "flashblue".

Does: Plays a ground effect where you click when you give the order.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: adds FxEntity, which shows a model at the point you click instead; see Gates of Hell only.

Example:

{action
    {cursor}
    {fx "flashgreen"}
}

See: none.

item

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: text, item tags.

Values: a text of item tags; when absent, the action uses the item in the unit's right hand.

Does: Makes the action need an inventory item that has all the tags.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{action
    {item "matchbox"}
    {item_in_box}
}

See: item_in_box.

item_in_box

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: flag, no value.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Lets the required item be anywhere in the inventory instead of in the hand.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{action
    {item "matchbox"}
    {item_in_box}
}

See: item.

ShowCount

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: flag, no value.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Shows the number of the required items on the button.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: the badge text comes from actionbar/count_white, not actionbar/count_black.

Example:

{action
    {button}
    {ShowCount}
}

See: actionbar/count_black.

apply_to_all

Where: action file, inside {action}. Type: flag, no value.

Values: present or absent.

Does: When a squad commander is selected, applies the action to the whole squad.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{action
    {cursor}
    {apply_to_all}
}

See: none.

target

Where: action file of a custom action, inside {action}. Type: word with arguments.

Values: ground; entity ["tags"], optionally followed by volume "name"; or volume "name" optionally followed by able <ability>.

Does: Sets what the custom action can be used on: a point on the ground, an object with the tags, or a named volume of an object. able limits a volume target to volumes with that ability, such as contact or touch.

Limits: The abilities are the ones listed under volume in Reference 10; this game has no blockcamera. Gates of Hell: also knows the volume ability blockcamera, and able blockcamera filters work there.

Example:

{action
    {target volume "dynamite_activate" able contact}
    {cursor "use"}
}

See: Reference 10, volume.

instructions

Where: action file of a custom action, inside {action}. Type: block of instructions.

Values: instruction blocks from the list under "Not described yet".

Does: Lists the steps the unit carries out, in order, as an order when you use the action.

Limits: An instruction name the game does not know logs "Unknown instruction" and then crashes the game. Gates of Hell: plant does nothing there and logs that it is not implemented; install takes only the object and an optional turn in degrees (the distance and exact_placement words are gone); animations takes a paint word that this game rejects as an unexpected token. New instructions are listed under Gates of Hell only.

Example:

{instructions
    {bind volume "dynamite_activate"}
    {effect_object "switch"}
}

See: instant.

instant

Where: action file of a custom action, inside {action}. Type: block of instructions.

Values: instruction blocks.

Does: Runs the instructions at once when the action is chosen, without an order.

Limits: It only runs when exactly one unit is selected.

Example:

{instant
    {effect "switch"}
}

See: instructions.

Command panel layouts

Taught in chapter 15, section 5. The job: Icons and interface.

The command panel is the grid of order buttons. Its main part has 4 columns and 3 rows, 12 cells. The layouts are in set/panel_control/: right_main.set is the normal page, right_attack.set the attack page and right_useitem.set the item page. A file right_special.set is named by the game but never loaded, so it has no effect.

Besides action names, a panel may list these built-in item types: gc_cp_command_use, gc_cp_command_cancel, gc_cp_state_manual_control, gc_cp_state_inventory, gc_cp_state_objectives, gc_cp_state_message_history, gc_cp_state_map, gc_cp_state_map_control, gc_cp_state_map_zoom_in, gc_cp_state_map_zoom_out, gc_cp_leave_unit, gc_cp_state_smoke_decoy, gc_cp_game_menu, gc_cp_state_highlight_stuff, gc_cp_state_highlight_corpses, gc_cp_state_highlight_silhouettes, gc_cp_state_pose, gc_cp_state_fire, gc_cp_state_move, gc_cp_state_speed, gc_cp_state_cannon, gc_cp_squad_control, gc_cp_state_weapon, gc_cp_state_reload, gc_cp_state_attach, gc_cp_state_supply, gc_cp_browse_attack, gc_cp_browse_useitem, gc_cp_browse_special, gc_cp_browse_back and gc_cp_dummy. The gc_cp_browse_ items switch the panel to another page, and gc_cp_dummy is an empty button. The others are the built-in buttons their names describe; the game draws and runs them itself.

panel_control

Where: panel layout file, root block. Type: block.

Values: one child block per item.

Does: Holds the items of one panel page, in order.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: loads six lists, front, right_main, right_attack, right_useitem, right_special and a new right_emplacement, so right_special.set works there. Its battle screen draws the buttons in layout bars whose grid the layout file sets (3 by 3 when not set) instead of the fixed 4 by 3 grid.

Example:

{panel_control
    {gc_cp_state_fire
        {position 0 0}
    }
}

See: chapter 15, section 5.

<item name>

Where: panel layout file, child block of {panel_control}. Type: block named after an action or a built-in item type.

Values: an action name, built-in or from an action file, or one of the built-in item types above. The block may be empty.

Does: Puts that button on the panel page. A button with no position takes the first free cell, row by row, in file order.

Limits: A name that is neither an action nor a built-in item type logs "Unknown control panel item" and leaves a button that does nothing; on the minimap panel the same mistake crashes the game. Every name is checked each time a panel is built, so one bad name gives many warnings. An action button only appears when the selected units can do the action. Gates of Hell: has more item types (gc_cp_state_auto_medic, gc_cp_state_hatch, gc_cp_state_reverse, gc_cp_lock_ammo, gc_cp_state_altitude, gc_cp_state_manual_control_mode, gc_cp_browse_emplacement); copied into this game they become buttons that do nothing.

Example:

{panel_control
    {rotate
        {position 2 1}
    }
}

See: position, condition.

position

Where: panel layout file, inside an item block. Type: two whole numbers, column and row.

Values: column 0 to 3, row 0 to 2; when absent, -1 -1, which means the first free cell.

Does: Places the button in a fixed cell.

Limits: When two items claim the same cell, the first one listed wins and the other is hidden. Items without a position are hidden when all 12 cells are taken.

Example:

{gc_cp_browse_attack
    {position 0 1}
}

See: priority.

condition

Where: panel layout file, inside an item block. Type: one or more quoted words.

Values: the condition terms below; when absent, no condition.

Does: Shows the button only for selections that meet every term.

Limits: An unknown term stops the game with the error "Unknown condition term" when the panel is built. Without disabled, a button whose action is unavailable is hidden, which includes every action button while you control a unit directly. Gates of Hell: the order panels also know the terms helicopter, hatch and engine, and -<tag> hides the button when a selected unit has that tag. Its layout bars match any unit tag or a soldier's ability name, such as medic or barricade, hide the button without a log message when a term is unknown, and log "ambiguous condition term" when a term matches two ways.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_pose
    {position 2 0}
    {condition "human"}
}

See: condition terms below.

priority

Where: panel layout file, inside an item block. Type: whole number.

Values: any whole number; default 0.

Does: Decides which item is placed first when two items want the same cell; the lower number goes first.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{repair
    {position 3 0}
    {priority 1}
}

See: position.

browse

Where: panel layout file, inside an item block. Type: word.

Values: a tag.

Does: Nothing; the game reads it and never uses it.

Limits: It has no effect.

Example:

{gc_cp_browse_useitem
    {position 1 1}
    {browse "useitem"}
}

See: none.

Panel condition terms

Taught in chapter 15, section 5. The job: Icons and interface.

vehicle

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only if a selected unit has the vehicle tag.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_speed
    {condition "vehicle"}
}

See: condition.

tank

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only if a selected unit has the tank tag.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_weapon
    {condition "tank"}
}

See: condition.

cannon

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only if a selected unit has the cannon tag.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_cannon
    {position 3 0}
    {condition "cannon"}
}

See: condition.

tractor

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only if a selected unit has the tractor tag.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_supply
    {position 3 0}
    {condition "tractor"}
}

See: condition.

human

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only if a selected unit has the human tag.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_pose
    {position 2 0}
    {condition "human"}
}

See: condition.

single

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only when exactly one unit is selected, counting each squad member.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_state_inventory
    {condition "single"}
}

See: multiple.

multiple

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only when more than one unit is selected, counting each squad member.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_squad_control
    {condition "multiple"}
}

See: single.

commander

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button only when one unit is selected and it leads a squad.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{gc_cp_squad_control
    {condition "commander"}
}

See: apply_to_all.

disabled

Where: panel layout file, inside {condition}. Type: quoted word.

Values: the word itself.

Does: Shows the button even when its action is unavailable, drawn greyed out.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{throw_ap_grenade
    {position 0 0}
    {condition "disabled"}
}

See: condition.

Hotkeys

Taught in chapter 15, section 6. The job: Icons and interface.

The default key map is interface/profiles/default/keys.set; note the plural "profiles". The game copies the files in interface/profiles/ into the player's own profile folder. Each player profile keeps its own keys.set, which overrides every action it lists and is rewritten by the game. Whether your mod's default replaces a copy the player already has is unconfirmed.

Key names are written as KEY_ followed by the key: KEY_A to KEY_Z, KEY_0 to KEY_9, KEY_F1 to KEY_F15, KEY_NUMPAD0 to KEY_NUMPAD9, KEY_COMMA, KEY_PERIOD, KEY_SLASH, KEY_BACKSLASH, KEY_SEMICOLON, KEY_APOSTROPHE, KEY_GRAVE, KEY_LBRACKET, KEY_RBRACKET, KEY_MINUS, KEY_EQUALS, KEY_ESC or KEY_ESCAPE, KEY_ENTER or KEY_RETURN, KEY_BACKSPACE or KEY_BACK, KEY_TAB, KEY_SPACE, KEY_CAPSLOCK, KEY_PAUSE, KEY_SYSRQ, KEY_HOME, KEY_END, KEY_INSERT, KEY_DELETE, KEY_PRIOR or KEY_PGUP, KEY_NEXT or KEY_PGDN, KEY_UP, KEY_DOWN, KEY_LEFT, KEY_RIGHT (also with ARROW added), KEY_ADD, KEY_SUBTRACT, KEY_MULTIPLY, KEY_DIVIDE, KEY_DECIMAL, KEY_NUMPADPLUS, KEY_NUMPADMINUS, KEY_NUMPADSTAR, KEY_NUMPADSLASH, KEY_NUMPADPERIOD, KEY_LSHIFT, KEY_RSHIFT, KEY_LCONTROL, KEY_RCONTROL, KEY_LALT, KEY_RALT, KEY_SHIFT, KEY_CONTROL, KEY_ALT (either side), KEY_LWIN, KEY_RWIN, KEY_APPS, KEY_NUMLOCK, KEY_SCROLL and KEY_ANY (any key). Mouse buttons are MOUSE0 or MOUSE_LEFT, MOUSE1 or MOUSE_RIGHT, MOUSE2 or MOUSE_MIDLE (spelt that way), MOUSE3 and MOUSE4 for the side buttons, and MOUSE5 to MOUSE7.

The action ids the game reads are:

GroupIds after the slash
common/center_active, prev_unit, next_unit, toggle_attack, toggle_position, slowdown, stuff_highlight, corpses_highlight, toggle_objectives, toggle_message_history, toggle_equipment, dismiss_squad, toggle_map, toggle_map_control, show_selection_circle, game_menu, pause, screenshot, videocapture, set_commander
control_manual/toggle, quick_aim, modify, forward, backward, left, right, fire, next_weapon, fire_mode, next_ammo, next_mgun
control_camera/mouse_rotate, zoom_in, zoom_out, rotate_left, rotate_right, increase_view, decrease_view
control_human/stay_lie, pose_up, pose_down, drop_from_hands
multiplayer/chat_team, chat_all, show_statistics, leave_unit, push_to_talk, toggle_microphone, show_notification
groups/assign_1 to assign_9, select_1 to select_9
actions/throw_ap_grenade, throw_at_grenade, throw_sk_grenade, bazooka_shot, attack, attack_ground, attack_melee, heal, emit, cancel, examine, drop, rotate, repair, attach, smoke_decoy, use

Three of these, actions/smoke_decoy, common/show_selection_circle and common/set_commander, are missing from the shipped default file and so start unbound. Selecting with the left mouse button and ordering with the right one are fixed and cannot be changed in this file.

keys

Where: key map file, root block. Type: block.

Values: one block per action id.

Does: Holds the default key of every action.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{keys
    {"common/dismiss_squad"
        {value KEY_K}
    }
}

See: chapter 15, section 6.

"group/action"

Where: key map file, child block of {keys}. Type: block named by a quoted action id.

Values: an id from the table above. The part before the slash only groups and sorts the options screen.

Does: Sets the key of that action. The options screen titles it with the text key options/keys/<id>.

Limits: An id the game does not read is saved and shown in the options screen but does nothing. Custom actions from action files cannot get a key at all, and show no key badge on their button; only built-in actions and actions whose button is use can. Gates of Hell: most common/ ids moved to other groups (interface/pause, interface/toggle_map, actions/toggle_attack, control_camera/center_active, groups/dismiss_squad and others), so an id copied from this game is unbound there; control_human/stay_lie, pose_up, pose_down and control_manual/next_mgun are gone. An action file with a Key line takes the key bound under that name, so custom actions can have keys.

Example:

{"common/center_active"
    {value "SHIFT + KEY_F"}
}

See: value.

value

Where: key map file, inside an action id block. Type: word or quoted text.

Values: a bare key name, or a quoted combination of key names and modifiers joined with +. Modifiers are SHIFT, CTRL, ALT and DOUBLE (a double press); ~SHIFT, ~CTRL, ~ALT and ~DOUBLE mean that modifier must not be held. An empty text "" leaves the action unbound.

Does: Sets the key or combination for the action. The name is not case-sensitive.

Limits: An unknown name is silently ignored, so a misspelt key leaves only the modifiers or nothing bound. MOUSE_MIDDLE is not a known name. Gates of Hell: its key dialog can also bind the left and right mouse buttons.

Example:

{"common/slowdown"
    {value KEY_BACKSPACE}
}

See: key names above.

noedit

Where: key map file, inside an action id block. Type: flag, no value.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Locks the key so the player cannot change it in the options screen.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: the pause key interface/pause can always be changed. Each key there also belongs to a category; see Gates of Hell only.

Example:

{"common/pause"
    {value KEY_PAUSE}
    {noedit}
}

See: single.

single

Where: key map file, inside an action id block. Type: flag, no value.

Values: present or absent.

Does: Makes the action take a key without modifiers, as used for keys you hold down.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{"common/stuff_highlight"
    {value KEY_C}
    {single}
}

See: noedit.

Fonts

Taught in chapter 15, section 7. The job: Icons and interface.

Fonts are files in interface/font/ ending in .font. Each points to a bitmap font description file (.fnt, in the binary AngelCode format) whose glyph pages are <name>_<page>.tga pictures beside it. Text picks a font by name, size and style; when the exact size is missing the game uses the biggest size not above the wanted one.

font_atlas

Where: font file, root block. Type: block.

Values: holds the keys below.

Does: Describes one font at one size and style.

Limits: A font named main at size 10 must exist; without it, or with no fonts at all, the game stops at start-up. A character the font lacks is drawn as ?. Gates of Hell: the default size is 8, so it needs main at size 8 and stops with "No default font" without it. A font set moved between the two games needs both sizes.

Example:

{font_atlas
    {name "main"}
    {size 10}
}

See: chapter 15, section 7.

name

Where: font file, inside {font_atlas}. Type: text.

Values: a font family name, such as main, arial_hq, arial_narrow, bookman or impact.

Does: Names the family the text tag <f(...)> asks for.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{font_atlas
    {name "impact"}
    {size 21}
}

See: <f(...)>.

size

Where: font file, inside {font_atlas}. Type: whole number.

Values: 0 to 255.

Does: Sets the size the text tag <s(...)> asks for.

Limits: Sizes above 255 do not fit the value the game stores. Gates of Hell: text that asks for size 0 or less gets size 8 instead of 10.

Example:

{font_atlas
    {name "main"}
    {size 12}
}

See: <s(...)>.

style

Where: font file, inside {font_atlas}. Type: whole number.

Values: 0 for normal; bold fonts ship as separate files of the same family.

Does: Sets the style of this font file.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{font_atlas
    {name "main"}
    {style 0}
}

See: <b>.

binary_data

Where: font file, inside {font_atlas}. Type: text, a file name.

Values: the .fnt file beside the .font file.

Does: Points to the glyph description of the font.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{font_atlas
    {name "main"}
    {binary_data "main_10.fnt"}
}

See: none.

HUD settings

Taught in chapter 15, section 7. The job: Icons and interface.

The file set/interface.set holds selection colours, the inventory grid, aim cursors, the damage scheme colours and the manual aiming read-out. The file interface/scene/minimap/minimap.set holds the minimap colours.

interface

Where: set/interface.set, root block. Type: block.

Values: holds the blocks below.

Does: Holds the HUD settings.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{interface
    {inventory
        {cell_size 31 35}
    }
}

See: chapter 15, section 7.

selection colors

Where: set/interface.set, {interface {selection {colors ...}}}. Type: block of colours.

Values: keys active, examining, manual, selectable, selected and senseless, each a colour name or "r g b".

Does: Sets the colour of unit selection marks in each state.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{colors
    {selected   white}
    {examining  "0 128 90"}
}

See: colours in How to read this chapter.

cell_size

Where: set/interface.set, {interface {inventory ...}}. Type: two whole numbers, pixels.

Values: width and height of one cell.

Does: Sets the size of one inventory grid cell.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{inventory
    {cell_size 31 35}
}

See: none.

aim_spot

Where: set/interface.set, inside {interface}. Type: block of picture paths.

Values: keys normal, ground, busy and target, each a cursor path under /interface/cursor/.

Does: Sets the aiming cursor pictures.

Limits: A path with no file shows no cursor and logs nothing. Gates of Hell: scales these pictures to a tenth of their size, so this game's aim pictures look tiny there and Gates of Hell's look ten times too big here.

Example:

{aim_spot
    {normal "/interface/cursor/sight"}
    {busy   "/interface/cursor/wpn_busy"}
}

See: cursor.

structure colors

Where: set/interface.set, {interface {structure {colors ...}}}. Type: block of colours.

Values: keys work, repairing, broken and destroyed.

Does: Sets the colour of vehicle parts in the damage scheme for each state.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: adds a vehicle_view block that colours its vehicle panel by percent of health; whether it still reads this block is not confirmed. See Gates of Hell only.

Example:

{colors
    {work      white}
    {destroyed "80 80 80"}
}

See: none.

manual_targetting

Where: set/interface.set, inside {interface}. Type: block.

Values: a range block with show, offset x y, size w h, and colours invalid, satisfy and optimal; further sub-blocks are listed under "Not described yet".

Does: Sets the range read-out shown while you aim a unit by hand: whether it shows, where and how big, and its colour when the target is out of range, in range, or at the best range.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: the block is spelt manual_targeting there, with one t; the old spelling is not read, so every read-out stays off until you rename it. It also adds an accuracy_circle block.

Example:

{range
    {show}
    {offset 40 10}
    {invalid red}
}

See: none.

minimap settings

Where: interface/scene/minimap/minimap.set, {minimap {settings ...}}. Type: block of numbers.

Values: tracer_length, a number; max_tracers, a whole number.

Does: Sets how long shot tracers are drawn on the minimap and how many may show at once.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{settings
    {tracer_length 0.9}
    {max_tracers   100}
}

See: minimap colors.

minimap colors

Where: interface/scene/minimap/minimap.set, {minimap {colors ...}}. Type: block of 0xAARRGGBB numbers.

Values: keys neutral, self, ally, coop_ally, enemy, selected, friendly_tracer and enemy_tracer.

Does: Sets the minimap colour of units by side and of tracers.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{colors
    {enemy 0xffE10000}
    {self  0xff004BE1}
}

See: minimap settings.

Menu backgrounds and music

Taught in chapter 15, section 3. The job: Icons and interface.

The file interface/pages/interface.set sets the background picture, video and music of each menu screen.

location

Where: interface/pages/interface.set, top-level block. Type: block named by a quoted screen name.

Values: "main", "login", "single", "multi", "multi_ingame", "options" or "credits".

Does: Holds the background of that menu screen.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{location "single"
    {background
        {media "main" {file "/music/campaign_theme" loop}}
    }
}

See: background.

background

Where: interface/pages/interface.set, inside {location}. Type: block.

Values: holds picture, video and media.

Does: Groups the background settings of the screen.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{background
    {picture "/interface/pages/main/video_bkg"}
}

See: location.

picture

Where: interface/pages/interface.set, inside {background}. Type: text, a picture path without extension.

Values: a path under /interface/.

Does: Sets the still background picture.

Limits: A path with no file shows nothing and logs nothing. Gates of Hell: a background can have a version per army; the army's file is used only when it exists, otherwise the plain one, so a mod need not ship one file per army.

Example:

{background
    {picture "/interface/pages/main/video_bkg"}
}

See: video.

video

Where: interface/pages/interface.set, inside {background}. Type: text, a video path without extension.

Values: a path under /video/.

Does: Plays a video behind the menu.

Limits: Only XviD-encoded .avi files are decoded. A video larger than 1280 by 720 may show only a still frame (unconfirmed). Gates of Hell: the video can also be chosen per army, falling back to the plain file as for picture.

Example:

{background
    {video "/video/menu"}
}

See: picture.

media

Where: interface/pages/interface.set, inside {background}. Type: block named by a quoted channel, holding file.

Values: a channel name such as "main", then {file "<path>" [loop]} with a music path without extension.

Does: Plays music on the menu screen, repeating it with loop.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{media "main"
    {file "/music/main_theme" loop}
}

See: location.

Skins

Taught in chapter 15, section 3. The job: Icons and interface.

Widget skins are set in set/registry/default_skin.reg, and the main menu has its own main_menu_skin.reg of the same shape.

default_skin

Where: skin registry file, root block. Type: block.

Values: one block per widget kind, such as dialog, inputline, scrollbar, listbox and slider.

Does: Sets the look of the game's widgets.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: menu pages, message, confirm and input boxes, the game over and objectives windows and the message history are drawn with the main_menu_dark_skin skin instead of main_menu_skin, so a skin mod for menus needs that skin's data. Its world debug texts take their style from a skin entry debug_console/text_style.

Example:

{default_skin
    {dialog
        {frame_size 1}
    }
}

See: dialog.

dialog

Where: skin registry file, inside {default_skin}. Type: block.

Values: frame_size (whole number), face_color and frame_color ("r g b"), text_style (a text of formatting tags without the angle brackets).

Does: Sets the frame width, fill colour, frame colour and default text style of dialog windows.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{dialog
    {face_color "77 77 77"}
    {text_style "f(arial_hq)s(8)c(255 255 255)"}
}

See: Text formatting tags.

folder

Where: skin registry file, inside a widget block such as {scrollbar}. Type: text, a folder path.

Values: a folder under /interface/skin/.

Does: Points the widget at the folder holding its pictures.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{scrollbar
    {folder "/interface/skin/editor/scrollbar/"}
}

See: none.

Page scripts

Taught in chapter 15, section 3. The job: Icons and interface.

Page scripts are the .ps files in interface/pages/script/. The game loads all of them. A script adds handlers to menu pages; pages built into the game, such as the lobby and options, cannot be rebuilt from a script. Arguments passed to a handler are read as #0, #1 and so on.

script

Where: page script file, root block. Type: block of page blocks.

Values: one {"<page name>" ...} block per page; the name "page" applies to every page.

Does: Holds the handlers and children each page gets.

Limits: Adding to an existing page by name is unconfirmed. Gates of Hell: builds its screens, the battle screen included, from layout files under interface/layout/ (XML); menu pages do not carry over between the games and must be rewritten. Whether it still reads page scripts is not confirmed. See Gates of Hell only.

Example:

{script
    {"page"
        {on key "KEY_ESC" {call "back"}}
    }
}

See: on.

on

Where: page script file, inside a page block. Type: block, an event then actions.

Values: on create, on key "KEY_X", on button "name", on end "name", or on "name" for a handler that call can run.

Does: Runs the actions when the page is created, when a key is pressed, when a named button is clicked, when a named sequence ends, or when the handler is called by name.

Limits: In on key, a key name the game does not know stops the game with "Invalid key for bind"; unlike the key map, it is not skipped.

Example:

{"page"
    {on key "KEY_ESC"
        {call "back"}
    }
}

See: call.

call

Where: page script file, inside an on handler. Type: block, a quoted handler name then arguments.

Values: a handler name and any arguments.

Does: Runs the named handler, passing the arguments as #0, #1 and onwards.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{on key "KEY_ESC"
    {call "back"}
}

See: on.

align

Where: page script file, inside an on handler. Type: block with a word.

Values: begin, center or end.

Does: Aligns the current element to the start, the centre or the end.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{on create
    {align center}
}

See: none.

Icon folders and frames

Taught in chapter 15, section 2. The job: Icons and interface.

The interface never writes a file extension. A picture name such as /interface/scene/unit_icon/pz4j finds the files pz4j_00.tga to pz4j_03.tga. The game prefers .ebm and .tex files and otherwise takes .dds, .tga, .bmp, .jpg or .png. Names are not case-sensitive. Under /interface/ and /map/ a frame may be written name_00 or name00.

The frame numbers mean:

FrameState
_00normal
_01mouse over it
_02pressed
_03disabled
_04checked, for buttons that stay on

Command panel buttons can have four variants of four frames each, so up to 16 frames. A missing picture never logs an error: the game shows a placeholder or nothing.

Folder under interface/scene/HoldsPicture name
unit_icon/multiplayer purchase cards and category buttonsthe card name, for squads with the side in brackets, such as riflemans(usa)
unit_icon_small/the unit list in gamethe vehicle's definition name
squad/soldier portraits, side markers and group numbersthe breed's portrait name
panel_control/command panel buttonsthe action's button name
structure/damage scheme per vehicle modelthe model name
portrait/soldier and crew portraitsthe portrait name

Category buttons of the purchase panel look for unit_icon/<tag>(<army>), then unit_icon/<tag>, then the icon of the first card in that category, then the placeholder. Cursors are folders of animated frames under interface/cursor/<name>/.

.lng text files

Taught in chapter 14, section 2. The job: Add or change text and translate it.

Text lives in .lng files. A mod's localization/ folder is read as the game's /interface/text/ folder. Vanilla texts are desc.lng (names), info.lng (tooltips), #dlg_frontend.lng, #dlg_ingame.lng, #dlg_mp.lng, #tips.lng, mission.lng, campaign.lng and mission files under mission/single/.

All .lng files are loaded, in sorted path order. A mod file at the same path as a vanilla file replaces the whole vanilla file; keys are not merged, so every vanilla key your copy leaves out shows as its raw key. When the same key appears twice, the later one wins and the log says "Localization key redefinition". A mod file whose name starts with # sorts before desc.lng, so a key it shares with desc.lng loses to the vanilla text. Text changes need a game restart; nothing has to be repacked. In the ARSENAL window, the Quick Guided Task "a mod with problems (fix them)" can remove the earlier copy of a repeated key for you (Use the Quick Guided Task).

tags

Where: .lng file, root block. Type: block.

Values: nested key blocks and text blocks.

Does: Holds every text of the file.

Limits: A file whose root is not {tags ...} stops the game with "Identifier expected!". A file saved as UTF-16 or UTF-32 stops the game with "Please resave file in UTF8". A file saved in a Windows code page loads, but every non-ASCII letter shows as a replacement mark. A UTF-8 byte order mark is allowed. Gates of Hell: still reads .lng files with the same root and key rules, but only under localizations/<language code>/interface/text/; a .lng left in this game's localization/ folder is not loaded. Texts there come in two layers, the chosen language over the default one, and may also be gettext .po, .pot or .mo files. Whether a mod's own .lng folder is mounted there is not confirmed.

Example:

{tags
    {"entity"
        {"pz4j" "Pz.Kpfw. IV"}
    }
}

See: chapter 14, section 2.

key block

Where: .lng file, inside {tags} or another key block. Type: block named by a quoted name.

Values: a name; names may contain spaces and brackets.

Does: Adds one level to the key path. The full key is the file name without extension, then each block name, joined by /. For a file whose name starts with #, the file name is left out; a file in a subfolder gets the folder path in front.

Limits: Keys are not case-sensitive, so 75mm_41M and 75mm_41m are the same key. Gates of Hell: a key defined twice inside one file keeps its first text, not the last; across files the later file still wins and the log says "Localization key redefinition" with both places.

Example:

{"squad"
    {"riflemans(usa)" "Riflemen"}
}

See: Text keys.

text block

Where: .lng file, inside a key block. Type: block of quoted strings.

Values: one or more strings. Escapes are \", \\, \n for a new line and \t for a tab.

Does: Defines one text. Several strings in a row are joined.

Limits: A string must not run past the end of its line. A key the game asks for but nobody defines shows as the key itself, with no log message. Where the game fills numbers into a text, its % placeholders must stay in the same number and order as in vanilla, or values go missing or land in the wrong place. Gates of Hell: a missing key still shows as the key itself, but the log says Missing text: [key] once per key.

Example:

{"zb30_mag mg_mauser" "7.92 mm\n Range - <c(ffaf00)>800 m<c(ffffff)>"}

See: Text formatting tags.

Text formatting tags

Taught in chapter 14, "Colours and formatting tags". The job: Add or change text and translate it.

Tags change how text is drawn. Several changes can share one tag, such as <f(impact)s(28)c(255 255 255)>. Write <<, or &lt;, for a literal <; &gt;, &amp; and &quot; also work. A tag without its closing > swallows the rest of the text.

<c(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with a colour.

Values: c(RRGGBB) in hexadecimal, c(r g b) in decimal, or c*(k) to brighten by a factor.

Does: Changes the text colour from that point.

Limits: Close each coloured run, or the colour carries on to the end of the text.

Example:

{"hint" "Range - <c(ffaf00)>200 m<c(ffffff)>"}

See: </c>.

</c>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag.

Values: none.

Does: Returns to the default text colour.

Limits: The spelling <c/> is unconfirmed; use </c> or an explicit colour.

Example:

{"hint" "<c(ff0000)>Warning</c> text"}

See: <c(...)>.

<e(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with an effect name.

Values: shadow, shadow_ex, highlight, disabled, default.

Does: Draws the text with that effect.

Limits: None known. Gates of Hell: shadow_ex and highlight look swapped there: its highlight draws what shadow_ex draws here. Swap the two names when you move texts between the games.

Example:

{"title" "<e(shadow)>Briefing"}

See: none.

<f(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with a font family name.

Values: a font name from the font files.

Does: Changes the font family from that point.

Limits: A character the font lacks is drawn as ?.

Example:

{"title" "<f(impact)s(28)>Victory"}

See: Fonts.

<s(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with a size.

Values: s(28) for a size, s+2 or s-2 to change the current size.

Does: Changes the font size from that point.

Limits: When the exact size is missing, the next smaller size is used.

Example:

{"title" "<s(18)>Objectives"}

See: size.

<b>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag.

Values: <b> on, <b-> off.

Does: Switches bold text on or off.

Limits: Bold needs a bold font file of the same family and size.

Example:

{"label" "<b>Note:<b-> read this"}

See: <i>.

<i>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag.

Values: <i> on, <i-> off.

Does: Switches italic text on or off.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{"quote" "<i>Hold the line<i->"}

See: <b>.

<p(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with a number.

Values: a spacing in pixels.

Does: Sets the spacing between letters.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{"title" "<p(2)>MISSION"}

See: none.

<t(...)>

Where: inside any text. Type: tag with a number.

Values: a tab width.

Does: Sets the width a \t tab moves the text.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{"row" "<t(80)>Range\t200 m"}

See: none.

Text keys

Taught in chapter 14, section 4 and, for the keys the interface asks for, chapter 15, section 8. The job: Add or change text and translate it.

The key families below are the ones the game looks up. In each entry, "Where" gives the vanilla file and block path the key normally lives in.

desc/entity/<model>

Where: desc.lng, {"entity" {"<model>" ...}}. Type: text.

Values: the model is the base name of the vehicle or gun definition file.

Does: Names the vehicle or gun in game and on its multiplayer card. A card whose name differs from the model also needs its own key here.

Limits: A missing key shows the raw key on screen and logs nothing.

Example:

{"entity"
    {"pz4j" "Pz.Kpfw. IV Ausf. J"}
}

See: chapter 14, section 4.

desc/squad/<name>(<side>)

Where: desc.lng, {"squad" {"<name>(<side>)" ...}}. Type: text.

Values: the card name and the side in brackets, as the card is written in the multiplayer unit files.

Does: Names a squad card and titles its info window. Cards that some vehicle macros build use the bare name without a side.

Limits: A wrong case or a missing side shows the raw key. Gates of Hell: its unit cards and info windows take their texts from other keys (mp/unit_info/..., entity_info/...). Where it still asks for this key and finds none, a squad shows ???<name> instead of the raw key (not confirmed which screens still ask).

Example:

{"squad"
    {"riflemans(usa)" "Riflemen"}
}

See: info/squad/<name>.

desc/human/mp/<side>/<breed>

Where: desc.lng, {"human" {"mp" {"<side>" {"<breed>" ...}}}}. Type: text.

Values: the breed file name; _vision and _assist variants are separate breeds and need their own keys.

Does: Names a soldier.

Limits: None known.

Example:

{"human" {"mp" {"usa"
    {"rifleman" "Private"}
}}}

See: none.

desc/weapon/<tags>, desc/ammo/<tags>, desc/stuff/<tags>

Where: desc.lng, {"weapon" ...}, {"ammo" ...} or {"stuff" ...}. Type: text.

Values: the item's tags in order, without weapon, ammo, grenade and pattern, joined by spaces. Items tagged ammo use ammo, items tagged weapon use weapon, all others use stuff.

Does: Names an item and gives its stat lines. An item's own Desc setting replaces the key.
